Setting the model's temperature to zero
explain: Instructions steer behavior while guardrails enforce denied topics on input and output. WAF does not understand semantic topics, removing knowledge harms in-scope answers, and temperature affects randomness, not scope.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Multiple departments want their own agents but must share a common set of approved tools (ticketing, HR lookup) with consistent authentication. Which AgentCore capability supports shared tooling?
options: Each department copying tool code into its own agent with separate credentials
A shared S3 bucket of tool scripts downloaded at runtime
One monolithic agent that all departments must use for every task
AgentCore Gateway, exposing approved tools (APIs, Lambda functions, MCP targets) centrally with managed authentication for agents to consume
explain: A gateway centralizes tool exposure, auth, and governance while departments keep their own agents. Copied code and credentials drift, script buckets are unmanaged, and a single monolith removes department autonomy.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Documents for a Bedrock Knowledge Base live in S3 as PDFs, including scanned pages. What does the ingestion process do to make them retrievable?
options: It extracts text (including from documents via parsing options), splits it into chunks, generates embeddings, and stores the vectors in the configured vector store
It copies the PDFs into DynamoDB tables keyed by file name
It fine-tunes the foundation model on each PDF
It indexes file names only, leaving content unprocessed
explain: Ingestion parses, chunks, embeds, and indexes content into a vector store for semantic retrieval. Copying files, fine-tuning, and filename-only indexing do not enable content-based retrieval.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A knowledge base returns irrelevant passages for precise product-code questions while general questions work well. Which retrieval improvement should the architect try?
options: Increase the chunk size to the entire document for every query
Use hybrid search (combining semantic vector search with keyword search) or add metadata filtering, since exact codes match keywords better than embeddings alone
Remove all metadata from chunks so the search is purely semantic
Lower the number of results returned to one
explain: Hybrid search pairs vector semantics with keyword precision, which suits codes and part numbers. Whole-document chunks dilute relevance, stripping metadata removes useful filters, and returning one result risks missing the answer.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A multi-tenant knowledge base must ensure one tenant's retrieved documents never appear in another tenant's answers. Which design enforces this?
options: Rely on the model to ignore other tenants' passages if they appear
Store all tenants together with no metadata and sort results by date
Attach tenant metadata to chunks and apply mandatory metadata filters per tenant at query time (or use separate knowledge bases/data sources per tenant for strict isolation)
Use one retrieval call for all tenants and split the answer afterward
explain: Metadata filtering (or physical separation) constrains retrieval to the caller's tenant before generation. Model goodwill is not isolation, unfiltered stores leak by design, and post-splitting means cross-tenant content already entered the prompt.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Which vector store options can back a Bedrock Knowledge Base for RAG workloads?
options: Amazon EBS volumes formatted for vector files
Amazon SQS queues holding embedding arrays
Route 53 records encoding vector data
Amazon OpenSearch Serverless, Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector, Pinecone, MongoDB Atlas, or Redis Enterprise Cloud as supported vector stores
explain: Bedrock Knowledge Bases support several managed vector stores including OpenSearch Serverless and Aurora with pgvector. Block volumes, queues, and DNS are not vector indexes for knowledge bases.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Users complain that RAG answers miss information that spans two sections of a manual. Which chunking adjustment is most likely to help?
options: Increase chunk overlap (and review chunk size) so context that crosses boundaries is preserved in at least one chunk
Set chunk size to a single sentence for maximum precision
Disable chunking and embed each full manual as one vector
Remove headings and tables before ingestion
explain: Overlap preserves cross-boundary context that fixed chunking would split. Sentence-sized chunks lose surrounding meaning, whole-document vectors blur retrieval, and stripping structure removes valuable content.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A knowledge base must stay current with a Confluence-like source and an S3 bucket, adding new documents automatically. What should the architect configure?
options: A one-time manual upload of all documents into the vector store
Multiple data sources on the knowledge base (supported connectors and S3) with scheduled or event-triggered sync jobs that incrementally ingest changes
A Lambda function that retrains the foundation model when pages change
Users emailing updated documents to the support team for re-typing
explain: Knowledge bases support multiple data sources with incremental sync on schedule or trigger. One-time uploads go stale, retraining is not ingestion, and manual processes do not scale or stay current.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A RAG system's retrieved passages are correct but final answers still hallucinate extra claims. Which prompt and product controls reduce this?
options: Raise the temperature so the model is more creative with the passages
Remove citations to simplify the answer format
Instruct the model to answer only from retrieved context and cite sources, enable knowledge-base retrieval confidence/reranking options where available, and apply guardrails for groundedness checks
Return more chunks regardless of relevance so the model has extra material
explain: Grounding instructions, citations, reranking, and groundedness guardrails constrain answers to sources. Higher temperature increases invention, removing citations hides provenance, and irrelevant extra chunks worsen grounding.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A company wants to test whether a new embedding model improves retrieval quality before switching production traffic. Which approach is safest?
options: Change the embedding model in place and let old and new vectors mix in one index
Delete the production knowledge base and rebuild it during business hours
Keep both models' vectors in the same fields and average query results manually
Create a separate knowledge base (or data source configuration) using the new embedding model, re-ingest, evaluate retrieval metrics side by side, then switch the application if it wins
explain: Embeddings from different models are not comparable in one index; a parallel knowledge base allows clean evaluation. Mixing vectors corrupts similarity search, and rebuilding in place risks downtime.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Structured product data lives in Redshift and Aurora, and users want natural-language answers over it alongside document RAG. Which Bedrock Knowledge Base capability covers structured sources?
options: Knowledge bases for structured data (SQL) that generate queries against supported stores such as Redshift and Aurora, in addition to unstructured document knowledge bases
Converting all database rows to PDFs and ingesting them as documents
Asking the foundation model to memorize nightly database exports
Using Athena alone with no Bedrock involvement for the chat experience
explain: Bedrock supports structured-data knowledge bases that translate questions to SQL over supported databases. PDF conversion loses structure and freshness, memorization is impossible at scale, and Athena alone does not provide the managed conversational RAG layer.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A knowledge base query must only consider documents published in the last 90 days and from the EMEA region. How is this enforced at retrieval time?
options: Delete older documents from S3 every night so they cannot be retrieved
Store publication date and region as chunk metadata and pass metadata filters with the Retrieve or RetrieveAndGenerate call
Add the date and region to the end of the user's question and hope the model filters
Create a new knowledge base every 90 days and discard the old one
explain: Metadata filters restrict retrieval deterministically by attributes. Deleting source documents destroys records, prompt hints are not enforcement, and recreating knowledge bases is wasteful.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: After ingestion, some source documents never appear in retrieval results. Which console/API evidence should the architect check first?
options: The foundation model's provisioned throughput utilization
CloudFront cache hit ratio for the application
The ingestion job history for the data source, reviewing per-document failures and parsing or embedding errors
The VPC route tables in the application account
explain: Ingestion job details list documents that failed to parse, chunk, or embed, pinpointing the gap. Model throughput, CDN caching, and routing do not explain missing indexed documents.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A RAG application needs to return the retrieved passages themselves to a custom generation step rather than using Bedrock's managed generation. Which API pattern fits?
options: Call RetrieveAndGenerate and intercept the passages before generation
Use the knowledge base console search test and copy results manually
Query the vector store's S3 bucket directly for chunk text files
Call the Retrieve API to get ranked chunks, then pass them to the model of the application's choice in its own prompt
explain: Retrieve returns chunks for applications that manage their own generation. RetrieveAndGenerate couples retrieval with Bedrock generation, console testing is manual, and vector stores are not browsed as S3 text files.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A trained model must serve real-time predictions with single-digit-millisecond latency for a fraud check inside a checkout flow. Which SageMaker deployment should be used?
options: A SageMaker real-time endpoint with an instance type and autoscaling sized for the latency budget
SageMaker batch transform run on each checkout request
An asynchronous inference endpoint with a queue per request
A SageMaker training job invoked per prediction
explain: Real-time endpoints are built for low-latency synchronous inference. Batch transform processes offline jobs, asynchronous endpoints suit large payloads and long jobs with polling, and training jobs do not serve predictions.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A model processes uploaded documents that take several minutes each and arrive sporadically; the team wants to pay only when work exists and tolerate queued processing. Which SageMaker option fits?
options: A real-time endpoint provisioned for peak load around the clock
SageMaker asynchronous inference (or serverless inference for smaller, intermittent workloads) that scales to zero and queues requests
A multi-model endpoint kept fully loaded at all times
An EMR cluster running the model continuously
explain: Asynchronous and serverless inference handle long or intermittent inference without always-on capacity. Always-on endpoints and clusters waste spend for sporadic work.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Inference traffic for a recommendation model varies tenfold between night and day. How should its SageMaker real-time endpoint scale?
options: Manually resize the endpoint each morning and evening
Use a single large instance and accept queueing at peak
Configure Application Auto Scaling for the endpoint variant on invocations per instance (or a custom metric) with min and max instance counts
Scale the training cluster instead of the endpoint
explain: Endpoint auto scaling adjusts instance count to traffic automatically. Manual resizing is error-prone, one instance bottlenecks at peak, and training capacity does not serve predictions.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A team hosts dozens of similar low-traffic models and wants to cut endpoint costs by sharing infrastructure. Which SageMaker feature helps?
options: One dedicated endpoint per model on the largest instance type
Batch transform jobs running continuously
Model Registry entries that serve traffic directly
Multi-model endpoints that load models onto shared instances on demand (or serverless inference for very low traffic)
explain: Multi-model endpoints consolidate many models behind one endpoint, loading them as needed. Dedicated large endpoints multiply cost, batch transform is offline, and the registry versions models rather than serving them.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A new model version must be validated with live traffic before full rollout, limiting risk if it underperforms. Which endpoint pattern supports this?
options: Production variants with weighted traffic (for example, 90/10) or shadow variants that receive mirrored traffic for comparison
Replacing the production model at midnight with no fallback
A/B labels applied to the training data
Blue/green DNS records pointing at two training jobs
explain: Variant weighting and shadow deployments expose a new model to controlled real traffic with instant rollback by shifting weights. Uncontrolled replacement risks the whole workload, and training artifacts do not serve traffic.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A vision model needs GPU acceleration and the lowest possible inference cost for steady, high-volume traffic. Which decision matters most?
options: Run the model on the largest CPU instance to avoid GPU quotas
Select a GPU instance family sized to the model, use the right inference optimization (compilation/quantization where suitable), and autoscale to steady demand
Place the endpoint behind CloudFront to cache predictions for identical images only
Use provisioned throughput in Bedrock instead of the custom model endpoint
explain: Instance selection and model optimization dominate GPU inference cost and performance for a custom model. Oversized CPUs underperform GPUs for vision, caching rarely helps unique images, and Bedrock serves foundation models, not this custom model.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: An ML team must track which model version, data, and approval produced each endpoint to satisfy audit requirements. Which SageMaker capability provides this lineage and governance?
options: S3 versioning alone on the model artifacts bucket
A shared spreadsheet of deployments maintained by data scientists
SageMaker Model Registry with model versions, approval workflows, and deployment history (supported by SageMaker governance/lineage tooling)
CloudTrail logs searched manually after each incident
explain: The Model Registry versions, approves, and tracks deployments of models with lineage. Bucket versioning lacks approval semantics, spreadsheets drift, and raw logs are evidence, not a governance workflow.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A Bedrock-based chat feature and a custom SageMaker model both need to be invoked from the same application; when is SageMaker the right choice over Bedrock?
options: For every workload, because Bedrock cannot be invoked from applications
When the team wants a foundation model with no endpoint management at all
When the task is generic text generation with no custom training
When the model is custom-trained on proprietary data or a specialized task that available foundation models do not cover, and the team accepts managing the endpoint
explain: SageMaker suits custom models and specialized inference under team control. Bedrock is fully invocable from apps and is the lower-effort choice for generic foundation-model tasks, which is exactly when SageMaker is not needed.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A company needs a dedicated, private connection from its data center to AWS with consistent bandwidth, separate from the public internet. Which service provides this?
options: AWS Direct Connect with a virtual interface to the VPC or Transit Gateway
AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the internet
Amazon CloudFront with a custom origin
AWS Global Accelerator over public IPs
explain: Direct Connect is a private dedicated network connection to AWS. VPN runs over the internet, CloudFront is a CDN, and Global Accelerator routes user traffic over the AWS backbone but is not a private data-center link.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Direct Connect is the primary hybrid link and the business requires automatic failover if the DX connection fails, with no manual intervention. Which design provides this?
options: Set up a second VPN only and remove Direct Connect
Configure a Site-to-Site VPN as a backup path with route preferences so BGP advertises DX as preferred and VPN takes over on failure (or a second diverse DX connection for higher resilience)
Rely on Route 53 health checks to switch the DX circuit
Back up DX with a weekly DataSync job
explain: DX plus VPN backup (or dual DX) with BGP preference is the standard resilient hybrid design. Removing DX loses the primary benefit, DNS does not reroute network paths, and data sync is not connectivity failover.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Two data centers and 30 VPCs across accounts need full many-to-many hybrid connectivity with centralized routing control. Which architecture scales best?
options: A mesh of VPC peering connections plus separate VPNs per VPC
One VPN per VPC managed individually from each data center
AWS Transit Gateway connecting the VPCs and both Direct Connect gateways/VPNs, with route tables segmenting environments
Direct Connect public VIFs only, with internet routing between VPCs
explain: Transit Gateway is the hub for many VPCs and on-premises links with centralized routing and segmentation. Peering meshes and per-VPC VPNs explode in count, and public VIFs do not provide private VPC-to-VPC routing.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A hybrid link must encrypt traffic in transit over Direct Connect to satisfy compliance, even though DX itself is private. Which option adds encryption?
options: Enable S3 default encryption on buckets used by hybrid apps
Use TLS only at the application and declare the network requirement met without a network control where MACsec/VPN is mandated
Order a second DX connection and alternate traffic daily
Run IPsec VPN over Direct Connect (public or transit VIF with VPN) or use MACsec on supported DX ports for layer-2 encryption
explain: VPN over DX and MACsec are the recognized ways to encrypt DX traffic. Storage encryption and daily alternation do not encrypt the link, and app TLS may complement but the question asks for a network-layer control.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: After adding a backup VPN to a DX setup, traffic prefers the VPN path even when DX is healthy, causing higher latency. What should the architect adjust?
options: BGP routing: ensure DX routes are preferred (for example, via local preference behavior for DX-propagated routes and AS path/community settings) so VPN is only used on DX failure
Disable BGP on the VPN so routes are static and preferred
Increase the VPN tunnel bandwidth by ordering more tunnels
Change the VPC CIDR so DX routes become shorter
explain: AWS prefers DX-propagated routes when configured correctly; VPN preference problems are fixed in BGP attributes and route propagation, not by disabling routing or changing CIDRs. Extra tunnels do not set preference.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A company consolidates hybrid connectivity and needs on-premises users to reach a private API in a VPC without traversing the internet. Which path achieves this?
options: Publish the API on a public ALB and allow-list the office IP only
Route on-premises traffic over Direct Connect (or VPN) through Transit Gateway to the VPC hosting a PrivateLink interface endpoint or internal ALB for the API
Give on-premises users IAM access keys to call the API through the console
Replicate the API into the data center nightly
explain: Private hybrid routing to an internal endpoint keeps traffic off the internet with network control. A public ALB still traverses the internet, console access is not application connectivity, and replication is not access.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Bandwidth over a single 1 Gbps Direct Connect port is saturated during nightly replication. Which options relieve this without redesigning the architecture?
options: Move replication onto the backup VPN only, permanently
Compress the VPC route tables to free bandwidth
Aggregate multiple DX connections with Link Aggregation Groups (LAG) or upgrade to a higher-capacity port, and schedule/shape replication traffic
Enable jumbo frames on the VPC and expect a tenfold gain
explain: LAG and larger ports increase DX capacity; traffic scheduling reduces contention. The VPN is typically lower bandwidth, route tables do not consume link bandwidth, and jumbo frames give marginal, not tenfold, relief.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A hybrid environment must keep working if an entire DX location becomes unavailable. Which design addresses location-level failure?
options: Order two ports in the same DX location on the same device
Document a manual procedure to order a new connection during an outage
Use a single DX connection with a larger port speed
Provision Direct Connect connections in two different DX locations with diverse paths into Transit Gateway, tested with BGP failover
explain: Geographically diverse DX locations protect against a location failure. Same-location redundancy shares the failure domain, ordering during an outage takes weeks, and port speed does not add resilience.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: On-premises applications need to resolve AWS private hosted zone names, and AWS workloads need to resolve on-premises DNS names. Which Route 53 Resolver design provides both directions?
options: Create an inbound Resolver endpoint for on-premises queries into AWS and an outbound endpoint with forwarding rules for on-premises domains, associated with the VPCs
Publish the private hosted zone publicly with split records
Copy DNS records nightly between the two DNS systems with scripts
Use DHCP options to point all systems at a single on-premises server with no AWS endpoint
explain: Inbound endpoints let on-premises resolvers query AWS private zones; outbound endpoints plus rules forward AWS queries on-premises — the bidirectional hybrid DNS pattern. Public exposure, manual copying, and one-sided pointing each break a direction or a control.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A company runs the same domain name with different answers inside AWS and on the public internet (split-horizon). Which Route 53 construct supports the internal version?
options: A single public hosted zone with VPC-only records flagged as private
A private hosted zone with the same domain associated with the VPCs, while the public hosted zone serves internet resolvers
Alias records that detect the querier's location automatically
A Resolver rule that rewrites public answers for internal clients
explain: Private hosted zones shadow the public namespace for associated VPCs — classic split-horizon. Public zones cannot hide records by VPC, aliases do not change visibility, and resolver rules forward rather than rewrite zones.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Queries from a VPC for the corporate domain 'corp.example.com' must be forwarded to on-premises DNS servers, while all other queries use normal resolution. Which configuration does this?
options: A private hosted zone for corp.example.com with copies of all corporate records
An inbound Resolver endpoint with a rule for the corporate domain
A Route 53 Resolver forwarding rule for corp.example.com pointing to the on-premises DNS IPs, associated with the VPC and using an outbound endpoint
A DHCP option set replacing the VPC's DNS server with the corporate server for all queries
explain: Conditional forwarding via outbound endpoints and domain rules is exactly this pattern. Duplicating records drifts, inbound endpoints serve the reverse direction, and replacing all DNS breaks AWS name resolution.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: After associating a private hosted zone with a new VPC, instances there still cannot resolve its names. Which checks are most relevant?
options: Check whether the zone's records have TTLs below 60 seconds
Ensure the zone is also associated with the on-premises DNS server
Confirm the instances have public IP addresses
Verify the VPC has DNS resolution and DNS hostnames enabled (or custom DHCP/resolvers correctly forwarding) and that the zone association completed for that VPC
explain: Private zone resolution requires the association plus VPC DNS support settings; custom resolvers must forward correctly. TTL values, on-premises association (not a concept for zones), and public IPs are irrelevant.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A company must continuously synchronize millions of files from an on-premises NFS server to S3, handling incremental changes efficiently and verifying data integrity. Which service is purpose-built for this?
options: AWS DataSync with an agent at the source, scheduled or continuous sync tasks to S3
AWS Storage Gateway in cached volume mode
A nightly rsync cron job to an EC2 instance that copies to S3
Amazon EFS replication from the on-premises server
explain: DataSync accelerates and automates large-scale transfers with incremental detection and verification. Storage Gateway presents storage volumes/files rather than syncing existing shares, rsync scripting lacks managed verification and scale features, and EFS replication works between EFS systems.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: On-premises applications expect an SMB file share, but the company wants the data stored durably in S3 with local caching for active files. Which service fits?
options: AWS DataSync used as a live file share for applications
AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway presenting SMB/NFS backed by S3
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server deployed on-premises
S3 mounted directly by applications with a third-party driver only
explain: File Gateway gives on-premises apps a standard file protocol with S3 as the durable backend and local cache. DataSync moves data but is not a share, FSx is an AWS-region service, and direct S3 mounts are not standard file shares.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: External partners must upload files over SFTP into S3 with their access restricted to their own folders and managed identities. Which service provides this?
options: An EC2 instance running an open-source SFTP server maintained by the team
S3 presigned URLs emailed to partners for each upload
AWS Transfer Family with an SFTP server endpoint, user identities, and logical directories/session policies scoping each partner to its prefix
A public FTP service fronted by a NAT gateway
explain: Transfer Family is the managed SFTP/FTPS/AS2 service landing data in S3 with per-user scoping. Self-managed EC2 adds patching risk, presigned URLs are per-object workarounds, and plain FTP is insecure and unmanaged.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A migration must move a live database's files and an NFS share to AWS with minimal downtime and continuous replication until cutover. Which pairing is most appropriate?
options: Copy everything once with a USB drive shipped after shutdown
Use Storage Gateway as the replication engine for the database files
Stop all writes for a week while a single full copy completes
Use DataSync for the file share replication (and a database migration service such as DMS for the database) with a planned cutover window
explain: DataSync handles continuous file replication and DMS handles databases, minimizing the final cutover. One-time copies and week-long shutdowns ignore the minimal-downtime requirement, and Storage Gateway is not a replication tool for existing data.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A DataSync task between an on-premises agent and S3 is far slower than the link capacity. Which factors should the architect investigate first?
options: Agent sizing/placement, number of files and small-file overhead, task bandwidth limits, and whether the agent can reach the service endpoint with enough parallel connections
Whether S3 bucket versioning is enabled
The color depth of files being transferred
Whether the VPC has DNS hostnames enabled
explain: DataSync throughput depends on agent resources, file profile, throttling settings, and connectivity. Versioning and DNS hostnames do not throttle transfers, and file content type metadata like color depth is irrelevant.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Applications on-premises need low-latency access to a dataset that is mastered in S3, with only the working set stored locally. Which Storage Gateway mode matches?
options: Volume Gateway stored mode replicating full volumes to the data center
File Gateway with a local cache sized for the working set, backed by the S3 bucket
Tape Gateway with virtual tapes in S3 Glacier
DataSync in continuous mode mounted as a drive
explain: File Gateway caches frequently accessed files locally while S3 holds the full dataset. Stored volumes keep primary data on-premises, tape gateway targets backup, and DataSync is not a mountable drive.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A company must transfer files from an Azure-hosted storage account and from Google Cloud into S3 as part of a consolidation. Which service supports these cross-cloud sources?
options: AWS Storage Gateway, which mounts other clouds as local shares
AWS Transfer Family, which pulls files from other clouds on a schedule
AWS DataSync, which supports transfers from other clouds' object storage (and on-premises) into AWS storage
S3 Cross-Region Replication configured with external endpoints
explain: DataSync includes locations for other clouds' storage and on-premises systems for managed migration into AWS. Storage Gateway serves on-premises apps, Transfer Family receives client uploads, and S3 replication works between S3 buckets.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Audit requires proof that every migrated file arrived in S3 bit-for-bit identical to the source. Which DataSync behavior provides this assurance?
options: S3 bucket logging showing PUT requests occurred
A spot check of ten files chosen by the migration team
MD5 values stored in file names by the source application
DataSync's data integrity verification, which checks transferred data and reports task execution results and verification status
explain: DataSync performs integrity verification during transfer and reports it per task execution. Access logs prove requests, not content equality, spot checks are sampling, and filename hashes are an application convention, not verification.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Legacy on-premises tape backups must be replaced with a cloud-backed solution that the existing backup software sees as a tape library. Which service provides this?
options: AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway presenting a virtual tape library backed by S3 and Glacier archives
AWS Backup with a tape emulation vault
DataSync tasks that copy backup files to S3 nightly
Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval used directly by the backup software
explain: Tape Gateway emulates a VTL for existing backup applications with cloud storage behind it. AWS Backup does not emulate tapes, DataSync file copies change the backup workflow, and backup software expects a tape interface, not raw object storage.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A hybrid file workload needs POSIX file access from both on-premises servers (through a gateway) and EC2 instances in AWS over the same S3-backed data. Which combination is valid?
options: Mount one S3 bucket as a POSIX drive on all systems with no caveats

File Gateway for on-premises access and native S3 or gateway access patterns in AWS, recognizing S3 is the system of record rather than a shared POSIX filesystem; for true shared POSIX, use FSx or EFS in AWS instead
Use Volume Gateway to share individual files with EC2
Replicate the bucket with DataSync every minute to simulate locking
explain: The honest design treats S3 (via File Gateway) as object-backed file access without distributed POSIX locking; workloads needing true shared POSIX semantics belong on FSx/EFS. Pretending S3 is a locking filesystem, sharing block volumes as files, or minute replication all create data-corruption risk.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A legacy monolith exposes business logic only through a message queue using an enterprise messaging protocol; a new serverless API must integrate with it without rewriting the monolith. Which service bridges this?
options: Amazon SQS, forcing the monolith to be rewritten to the SQS API first
EventBridge with a schema that rewrites the monolith's protocol
Amazon MQ as the managed message broker for the legacy protocol, with Lambda/API Gateway components translating API calls to queue messages
AWS Transfer Family converting API calls into messages
explain: Amazon MQ supports standard protocols such as AMQP and OpenWire used by legacy systems, letting modern components integrate via the broker. SQS would require monolith changes, EventBridge does not translate broker protocols, and Transfer Family moves files.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A mainframe-era application can only produce flat files on a schedule; a modern API must serve that data with low latency. Which integration pattern modernizes access without touching the legacy app?
options: Expose the legacy file directory directly through a public ALB
Rewrite the mainframe application as Lambda functions in the same project
Have API Gateway read files from the on-premises server over the internet per request
Ingest the files with Transfer Family or DataSync into S3, process them with Lambda/Glue into a queryable store, and expose the data through API Gateway
explain: Decoupled ingestion plus a modern query layer is the standard strangler-style integration. Direct directory exposure is insecure, rewriting the mainframe violates the constraint, and per-request remote file reads are slow and fragile.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A legacy SOAP service must be presented to partners as a modern REST API with request transformation. Which AWS service can front and transform it?
options: Amazon API Gateway with integration request/response mapping templates transforming REST/JSON to the legacy SOAP/XML backend
Amazon CloudFront with origin request policies rewriting SOAP bodies
Route 53 alias records that translate protocols
An NLB that converts REST calls to SOAP at Layer 4
explain: API Gateway supports non-proxy integrations with mapping templates that transform payloads between REST and SOAP backends. CloudFront policies do not rewrite bodies into SOAP, DNS does not translate protocols, and Layer 4 balancers do not inspect payloads.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A company is incrementally replacing a monolith: new features are built as Lambda-backed APIs while old features stay on-premises, with traffic shifted feature by feature. Which routing approach enables this strangler pattern?
options: Cut over the entire monolith on a single weekend
Place API Gateway (or an ALB) in front of both, routing specific paths to the new Lambda services and the rest to the legacy system, shifting paths as features migrate
Duplicate all traffic to both systems and merge responses manually
Freeze all new features until the monolith is fully rewritten
explain: A front door with path-based routing is the strangler-fig mechanism for gradual migration. Big-bang cutover and feature freezes are the alternatives this pattern exists to avoid, and response merging is not a routing strategy.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A legacy application requires a persistent TCP connection and a proprietary binary protocol; the team wants to expose it to cloud services without changing the protocol. Which fronting option is appropriate?
options: API Gateway REST APIs terminating the binary protocol
CloudFront with a custom origin speaking the binary protocol
A Network Load Balancer (optionally with PrivateLink) passing TCP through to the legacy endpoints over the hybrid connection
Lambda functions holding persistent connections open indefinitely
explain: NLB provides Layer 4 pass-through for arbitrary TCP protocols. API Gateway and CloudFront are HTTP-based, and Lambda cannot hold indefinite persistent connections.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Batch jobs in a legacy system are triggered by dropping files into a directory; the modernized pipeline must react the same way in AWS. Which event pattern replicates this trigger?
options: Poll the S3 bucket from an EC2 instance every hour
Require the legacy system to call a new REST API it cannot speak
Use CloudWatch alarms on bucket size to start jobs
Land files in S3 (via Transfer Family or File Gateway) and use S3 event notifications to EventBridge/Lambda to start the modern processing
explain: S3 event notifications are the cloud-native equivalent of a file-drop trigger. Polling adds delay and cost, the legacy system cannot adopt new APIs by assumption, and bucket-size alarms are coarse and unreliable triggers.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A factory site needs Kubernetes workloads to run locally for latency, managed with the same EKS APIs and tooling as the cloud clusters. Which offering fits?
options: Amazon EKS Anywhere running EKS clusters on the factory's own infrastructure
Amazon ECS Anywhere with Kubernetes scheduling enabled
AWS Outposts running a full public Region at the factory
Amazon EKS with nodes placed in a Local Zone near the factory
explain: EKS Anywhere extends EKS to customer-managed on-premises infrastructure. ECS Anywhere is for ECS, not Kubernetes, Outposts are AWS-operated racks with AWS services rather than customer-run EKS Anywhere clusters, and Local Zones are AWS facilities, not the factory floor.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A shipping fleet's shore offices run a small number of ECS tasks on local servers that must be managed from the AWS control plane. Which service enables this?
options: Amazon EKS Anywhere with ECS compatibility mode
Amazon ECS Anywhere, registering external instances with the ECS control plane
AWS Outposts installed in each shore office
Fargate tasks scheduled onto on-premises servers
explain: ECS Anywhere lets external instances join ECS clusters for task management. EKS Anywhere targets Kubernetes, Outposts is heavyweight AWS hardware for larger footprints, and Fargate runs only on AWS infrastructure (or Outposts).
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A hospital must keep imaging workloads and data physically in its building for regulatory reasons while using AWS services and APIs consistently. Which option meets this?
options: A Local Zone in the nearest metro area
Direct Connect to the closest Region with data residency controls
AWS Outposts racks deployed in the hospital, extending AWS infrastructure and services on-premises
EKS Anywhere on the hospital's existing servers only
explain: Outposts place AWS-operated infrastructure inside the customer's facility for residency and locality needs. Local Zones are AWS sites, not the hospital building; DX still processes in a Region; EKS Anywhere covers Kubernetes on customer hardware but not the broader AWS services consistency asked for.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A media company in a city without a Region needs single-digit-millisecond latency for rendering previews from AWS compute placed near its users. Which placement option helps?
options: AWS Outposts shipped to each end user's office
Wavelength zones embedded in consumer laptops
A second Availability Zone in the existing Region
AWS Local Zones, deploying compute in the metro area close to end users
explain: Local Zones extend AWS infrastructure into population centers for low-latency placement. Outposts are for customer facilities at enterprise scale, Wavelength targets mobile carrier networks, and existing AZs remain in the Region's geography.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A retail chain wants consistent container operations: EKS in AWS for headquarters systems and EKS on store hardware for point-of-sale resilience during WAN outages. Which pairing delivers this?
options: Amazon EKS in the cloud plus EKS Anywhere in stores, sharing cluster tooling, add-ons, and GitOps workflows
ECS in the cloud plus Docker Compose in stores
Outposts in every store regardless of size
Cloud EKS only, accepting store outages when the WAN fails
explain: EKS plus EKS Anywhere gives one Kubernetes operational model across cloud and stores, including disconnected-tolerant local operation. Mixed ECS/Compose splits tooling, Outposts per store is disproportionate, and cloud-only fails the resilience requirement.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: An organization with hundreds of VPCs wants on-premises DNS servers to resolve names in a centrally managed private hosted zone without creating endpoints in every VPC. Which design centralizes hybrid DNS?
options: Create an inbound endpoint in every VPC and synchronize them with scripts
Host the private zone in a central networking account with an inbound Resolver endpoint there, and have on-premises resolvers forward to that endpoint; share associations as designed
Publish the central zone to the internet with a restrictive TTL
Point on-premises DNS at the VPC's .2 resolver address directly across DX
explain: Central inbound endpoints in a hub account are the scalable pattern for on-premises resolution of AWS private zones. Endpoints everywhere multiply cost and management, public publishing breaks privacy, and the VPC resolver is not directly reachable as a hybrid endpoint in that way.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A VPC uses a custom DHCP option set pointing to on-premises DNS; after adding Resolver forwarding rules, AWS service names stop resolving for some instances. What is the likely design flaw?
options: Forwarding rules require TTLs under 60 seconds to function
The outbound endpoint needs a public IP to resolve AWS names

Instances bypass Route 53 Resolver entirely via the custom DNS servers, so forwarding rules and private zones do not apply to them; DNS should flow through Resolver (or the custom servers must forward appropriately)
Private hosted zones cannot coexist with DHCP option sets
explain: Resolver rules only affect queries that reach Resolver; a DHCP set sending queries straight on-premises sidesteps them. TTLs, public IPs, and coexistence claims are not the mechanism.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A company needs DNS firewall-style protection to block queries for known malicious domains across all its VPCs. Which Route 53 feature provides this?
options: Route 53 health checks that fail over away from malicious domains
Private hosted zones containing blocklist records pointing to 127.0.0.1 for every bad domain
AWS WAF rules applied to DNS query traffic
Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall with domain lists and rules associated with the VPCs
explain: Resolver DNS Firewall filters outbound DNS by domain lists centrally. Health checks reroute service traffic, hand-maintained block zones do not scale, and WAF inspects HTTP, not DNS resolution.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Two DX connections terminate in different locations but both advertise the same on-premises prefixes; the architect must ensure deterministic primary/backup behavior. Which BGP approach is standard?
options: Advertise the primary path with attributes AWS honors for preference (such as shorter AS path / appropriate communities) and the backup with less-preferred attributes, verifying with DX route visibility
Advertise identical attributes and rely on packet order to choose paths
Set the VPC route table to prefer one DX connection manually per subnet
Use DNS weights to steer the network traffic between connections
explain: Deterministic DX failover is engineered with BGP attributes AWS evaluates. Identical advertisements yield unpredictable selection, VPC route tables do not choose between DX paths in that manner, and DNS does not steer routed infrastructure traffic.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A failover test shows the VPN backup takes several minutes to start carrying traffic after DX failure because tunnels were down. Which practice keeps the backup ready?
options: Create the VPN only during an outage to save cost
Keep both VPN tunnels up continuously with BGP sessions established and monitored (and use accelerated VPN/DPD settings as appropriate) so failover is a routing change, not a tunnel negotiation
Ping the VPN gateway weekly from on-premises
Rely on IKE renegotiation triggered by user traffic after failover
explain: An always-up, BGP-established VPN fails over in seconds because routes simply shift. Creating or negotiating tunnels during an incident adds the delay observed, and weekly pings do not maintain readiness.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Hybrid workloads need to reach S3 and DynamoDB from on-premises without crossing the public internet or hair-pinning through a VPC unnecessarily. Which DX configuration supports this?
options: A private VIF, which can reach S3 public endpoints directly without a VPC
An interface endpoint in the VPC reachable from on-premises with no routing configuration
A Direct Connect public virtual interface, which advertises public AWS service routes over the private connection (with traffic still to public service IPs but over DX)
S3 Cross-Region Replication between the data center and a bucket
explain: Public VIFs carry traffic to AWS public services over the DX connection. Private VIFs reach VPC resources, gateway/interface endpoints need VPC routing design, and replication is not an access path.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: An enterprise is consolidating from dozens of VPNs to Transit Gateway and needs per-environment routing isolation between production and development traffic that both cross the hub. Which TGW feature provides this?
options: Separate NAT gateways for each environment in the hub VPC
Security groups applied to the Transit Gateway itself
Distinct DX port speeds per environment
Multiple Transit Gateway route tables with controlled associations and propagations per attachment segment
explain: TGW route tables segment which attachments can reach each other, the hub equivalent of VRFs. NAT, security groups (not applied to TGW), and port speeds do not create routing domains.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Two VPCs in the same Region need private communication, and the teams accept that the VPCs have non-overlapping CIDRs and no transitive routing through them. Which connectivity is simplest?
options: VPC peering between the two VPCs with routes added in each VPC's route tables
AWS PrivateLink, which routes general VPC-to-VPC traffic
A Transit Gateway, required for any two-VPC communication
Direct Connect between the VPCs
explain: Peering directly connects two VPCs at low cost when its limits (non-overlapping CIDRs, non-transitive) are acceptable. PrivateLink exposes specific services, not general routing; Transit Gateway is for scale and hub designs, not a requirement; DX connects on-premises networks.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A VPC peering design fails because both VPCs use 10.0.0.0/16. Which alternatives solve connectivity despite overlapping CIDRs?
options: Enable peering anyway and add more specific routes
Expose the needed services with PrivateLink endpoint services, or renumber/migrate one VPC; peering and Transit Gateway cannot route between overlapping CIDRs
Use a NAT gateway inside the peering connection to translate routes automatically
Merge the two VPCs' route tables so the overlap resolves itself
explain: Overlapping CIDRs cannot be routed between VPCs by peering or TGW; PrivateLink avoids routing entirely by exposing services. More specific routes do not fix identical address space for return traffic, and there is no automatic NAT inside peering.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A SaaS provider must let hundreds of customer VPCs access its service without opening the provider VPC or managing peering with each customer. Which design scales?
options: Create a VPC peering connection with every customer VPC
Publish the service on the internet with customer IP allow lists
Offer the service through PrivateLink (an endpoint service behind an NLB); each customer creates an interface endpoint in their VPC
Give each customer a VPN into the provider VPC
explain: PrivateLink endpoint services are built for many-consumer, one-way service exposure without network sharing. Peering and VPNs do not scale and expose network topology, and internet exposure weakens the private posture.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: An architect needs centralized inspection: all traffic between VPCs and to the internet must pass through a shared services VPC containing network appliances. Which hub design supports this?
options: VPC peering in a full mesh with inspection instances in each VPC
PrivateLink endpoints between every pair of VPCs
Route 53 routing policies that direct packets through the inspection VPC
AWS Transit Gateway with route tables steering traffic through the inspection VPC (using Gateway Load Balancer or appliance mode as appropriate)
explain: Transit Gateway enables hub-and-spoke steering through a central inspection point. Full-mesh peering cannot transitively route through a hub, PrivateLink is service-specific, and DNS does not steer packets.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A company grows from 5 to 200 VPCs and its peering mesh has become unmanageable. Which migration gives centralized routing, segmentation, and a path to hybrid links?
options: Migrate inter-VPC connectivity to AWS Transit Gateway with per-segment route tables
Keep peering and document connections in a spreadsheet
Replace peering with internet VPNs between VPCs
Use one giant VPC and merge all workloads into it
explain: Transit Gateway replaces quadratic peering growth with a hub, route-table segmentation, and hybrid attachment. Spreadsheets do not reduce complexity, internet VPNs regress security, and merging VPCs destroys isolation boundaries.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A consumer VPC's interface endpoint for a PrivateLink service resolves but connections time out. Which checks are most likely to find the cause?
options: Check the VPC's internet gateway route for the endpoint traffic
Verify the endpoint's security group allows traffic from the consumers, the service's NLB listener and target health, and that the endpoint service allows the consumer principal
Confirm the endpoint has a public DNS name enabled globally
Ensure the consumer VPC has a NAT gateway for endpoint replies
explain: Interface endpoint failures are usually security group, listener/target, or allowed-principal issues. Endpoint traffic stays private and local to the AZ subnets, so internet and NAT components are not in the path.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Workloads in a VPC need private access to S3 and DynamoDB without traffic leaving the AWS network or using an internet gateway. Which endpoints should be created?
options: Interface endpoints powered by PrivateLink for both services at per-hour cost
NAT gateways in each AZ configured for AWS service traffic
Gateway VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB in the VPC's route tables
An internet gateway with restrictive route tables
explain: Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB are free and integrate with route tables. Interface endpoints also work but cost more and suit other services, NAT sends traffic toward the internet path, and an internet gateway contradicts the private requirement.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A database VPC must be reachable from app VPCs but app VPCs must not reach each other, and the database VPC must not initiate connections to apps. Which hub configuration expresses this?
options: One shared TGW route table for all attachments so routing is symmetric
VPC peering between every app and the database with default routes
PrivateLink for the database's general network access

Transit Gateway route tables: associate app VPCs with a route table that propagates only the database VPC, and give the database VPC a route table without routes back-initiating to apps (with security groups enforcing direction at the resource layer)
explain: TGW route-table design controls which attachments learn which routes, providing the segmentation described; stateful security groups handle initiation direction. A shared table makes everything reachable, and PrivateLink is for services, not database network reachability in general.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A new Region's VPCs must connect to the existing Transit Gateway design for inter-Region traffic. Which construct links the hubs?
options: Transit Gateway peering between the two Regions' transit gateways, with static routes added for the peered TGW
VPC peering directly attached to a transit gateway
An inter-Region Direct Connect public VIF
Route propagation automatically flooding all routes between Regions
explain: TGW peering connects regional hubs; routes to the peer are added statically. VPC peering cannot attach to a TGW, public VIFs serve on-premises connectivity, and routes do not flood automatically across the peering.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A team wants to expose an internal application to a partner's VPC only, without the partner seeing other services or the VPC CIDR topology beyond the endpoint. Which pattern fits best?
options: VPC peering restricted by a NACL to the application's port
PrivateLink endpoint service in front of the application, with the partner account as an allowed principal creating an interface endpoint
A shared Transit Gateway attachment for the partner
Publishing the application privately via a custom DNS name on the internet
explain: PrivateLink exposes exactly one service with no route to the rest of the VPC. Peering and TGW share network reachability more broadly, and internet publishing contradicts the privacy goal.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: An enterprise allocating VPC CIDRs across hundreds of accounts keeps running into overlaps and waste. Which service and practice solve allocation centrally?
options: Let each account pick CIDRs and record them in a wiki
Allocate /16 blocks to every VPC regardless of size to avoid overlaps
Use Amazon VPC IP Address Manager (IPAM) with pools per Region/environment to allocate and audit CIDR assignments automatically
Use IPv6 only and skip planning because the space is large
explain: IPAM provides centralized pools, automated allocation, and overlap prevention with audit history. Wikis drift, uniform /16s waste space and still collide, and IPv6 still needs a plan.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A VPC design must place public web servers, private application servers, and databases with no internet path in separate tiers across two AZs. Which subnet design achieves this?
options: One subnet per AZ containing all tiers with security groups as the only separation
Public subnets for all tiers, relying on private IP addresses for databases
A single large subnet spanning both AZs for simplicity
Public subnets with an internet gateway route for web, private subnets with NAT for app egress, and isolated private subnets with no NAT route for databases, each tier in both AZs
explain: Tiered subnets with distinct route tables per tier and AZ are the standard VPC segmentation pattern. Mixing tiers in one subnet weakens network controls, public subnets expose databases at the routing layer, and subnets cannot span AZs.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: An architect sizes a VPC for a workload that will grow to about 4,000 hosts per subnet tier and wants room to grow without renumbering. Which CIDR choice is most defensible?
options: Allocate a generously sized VPC (for example /16) and carve subnets such as /20s per tier/AZ, tracked in IPAM, leaving unallocated space for future tiers
Create a /28 VPC and add secondary CIDRs weekly as hosts grow
Use a /8 VPC so growth is never a concern
Pick overlapping CIDRs in each AZ and rely on routing to sort it out
explain: Right-sized initial allocation with reserved headroom avoids painful renumbering. Tiny blocks force constant secondary CIDRs, /8 is not assignable as a VPC block of that scale in normal practice and wastes planning discipline, and overlaps break routing.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A workload needs outbound internet access from private subnets in three AZs with high availability and no single point of failure. Which design is correct?
options: Deploy one NAT gateway in a single AZ for all private subnets to save cost, accepting the cross-AZ dependency
Deploy a NAT gateway in each AZ and point each AZ's private route tables at its local NAT gateway
Use the internet gateway directly from private subnets with private IPs
Replace NAT with a NAT instance for higher availability
explain: Per-AZ NAT gateways keep egress resilient and local. A single NAT is an AZ-level single point of failure, private subnets cannot use an IGW without public IPs, and NAT instances are less available and lower throughput than managed NAT gateways.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Security requires that a VPC have no internet gateway and no NAT, with AWS services reached privately for a regulated workload. Which combination delivers this isolated design?
options: A private subnet design with a NAT gateway in a neighboring VPC
An internet gateway with a deny-all NACL
An isolated VPC using VPC endpoints (gateway and interface) for required AWS services and no IGW/NAT routes
Direct Connect public VIF as the subnet's default route
explain: Isolated subnets plus endpoints give AWS access with zero internet path. NAT in another VPC still creates an internet path, deny NACLs on an IGW leave an unnecessary attack surface and operational risk, and a public VIF default route is not isolation.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A team must add more IP addresses to an existing VPC whose primary CIDR is exhausted, for a new subnet tier. Which supported action extends the address space?
options: Edit the existing CIDR block to a larger size in place
Borrow unused addresses from a peered VPC's range
Convert existing subnets to IPv6 only to free IPv4 space instantly
Associate a secondary IPv4 CIDR block with the VPC and create the new subnets from it
explain: VPCs support additional associated CIDR blocks. The primary CIDR cannot be resized in place, another VPC's addresses cannot be borrowed, and protocol conversion is a project, not an addressing shortcut.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Micro-segmentation requires that even within the application tier, the payments service cannot initiate connections to the reporting service, though both share subnets. Which control provides this granularity?
options: Security groups attached per service (with security-group referencing) to control service-to-service traffic regardless of shared subnets
NACLs on the shared subnet separating the two services
Separate route tables for each service within the same subnet
DHCP options assigning different DNS servers per service
explain: Security groups operate at the instance/ENI level, enabling per-service rules inside a subnet. NACLs act at the subnet boundary and cannot distinguish workloads in the same subnet, route tables are per subnet, and DNS settings do not filter traffic.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A VPC Flow Logs review shows unexpected traffic, and the team wants a complete record of all network flows for compliance, retained long-term in cheap storage. Which configuration meets this?
options: Enable flow logs only for REJECT traffic to CloudWatch for a week
Enable VPC Flow Logs for the VPC (ALL traffic) delivering to S3 with lifecycle policies for long-term retention (optionally queried with Athena)
Rely on instance-level packet captures rotated daily
Use CloudTrail data events as the network flow record
explain: Flow Logs to S3 with lifecycle management provide complete, durable flow records. Reject-only short-lived logs miss accepted malicious flows, packet captures do not scale, and CloudTrail records API calls, not network flows.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: An architect must prevent any VPC in the organization from accidentally using a CIDR reserved for the on-premises network (172.16.0.0/12). Which governance approach enforces this?
options: Send an email reminder to account owners each quarter
Rename the on-premises network to match AWS allocations later
Define IPAM pools that exclude the on-premises ranges and require allocations from pools (backed by SCPs/config rules preventing manual conflicting CIDRs)
Allow overlaps and fix them if a hybrid route fails
explain: IPAM pool governance plus preventive controls stops conflicting allocations at creation time. Reminders are not enforcement, renaming a corporate network is unrealistic, and overlaps discovered at routing time cause outages.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A design review finds database subnets have a route to a NAT gateway they never use, widening the egress surface. What is the cleanest correction?
options: Add a NACL denying all outbound traffic but keep the NAT route for emergencies
Give the databases public IPs so the NAT route is unnecessary
Leave the route; unused routes create no risk
Move databases to isolated subnets whose route tables contain only the local route (plus specific endpoint routes), removing the NAT route
explain: Removing the route eliminates the egress path entirely, the strongest control. NACL denies can be edited or misordered, public IPs increase exposure, and unused internet routes are exactly the accidental-egress risk auditors flag.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A company must inspect and block malicious traffic entering all its VPCs from the internet and between VPCs, with centrally managed rules including domain and IPS signatures. Which service provides this?
options: AWS Network Firewall with centrally managed rule groups deployed at VPC boundaries (including via Transit Gateway inspection designs)
Security groups with very long rule lists on each instance
AWS WAF applied to the VPC route tables
CloudFront shield rules applied to private subnets
explain: Network Firewall is the managed stateful inspection service for VPC traffic with IDS/IPS-style and domain rules. Security groups lack deep inspection, WAF protects HTTP applications not network flows, and CloudFront does not inspect VPC-internal traffic.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A public web application is hit by SQL injection and cross-site scripting attempts. Which service should filter these HTTP attacks before they reach the ALB?
options: AWS Network Firewall with Layer 4 rules on the VPC
AWS WAF attached to the Application Load Balancer (or CloudFront) with managed rule groups for SQLi and XSS
Security groups blocking the attacking ports
NACLs denying the payload patterns
explain: WAF inspects HTTP payloads with managed rules for injection attacks at the ALB or CloudFront. Network Firewall focuses on network/transport and domain filtering, and security groups/NACLs cannot parse HTTP bodies.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Third-party virtual appliances (firewalls from a vendor) must inspect east-west and egress traffic transparently without changing application routing design per subnet. Which load balancer inserts them?
options: Application Load Balancer with the appliances as an HTTP target group
Network Load Balancer with TLS listeners to the appliances
Gateway Load Balancer, distributing traffic to the appliance fleet using GENEVE encapsulation while keeping flows symmetric
A Transit Gateway Connect attachment to the appliances
explain: Gateway Load Balancer is designed to deploy and scale third-party appliances transparently. ALB/NLB target groups treat appliances as endpoints rather than inline bump-in-the-wire inspection, and TGW Connect is for SD-WAN/gRE connectivity.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: An instance must allow inbound HTTPS only from the ALB and outbound connections only to a specific S3 prefix list, with return traffic automatically permitted. Which control fits, given its stateful nature?
options: A NACL with explicit rules for both directions including ephemeral ports
A route table restricting destinations per instance
An IAM policy attached to the instance role limiting network ports
A security group on the instance referencing the ALB's security group for inbound and the S3 managed prefix list for outbound
explain: Security groups are stateful, support referencing other groups and prefix lists, and apply per ENI. NACLs are stateless and need ephemeral-port rules, route tables are subnet-wide, and IAM policies do not filter network traffic.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: After tightening a NACL, outbound application requests work but responses never arrive. What is the classic NACL mistake?
options: NACLs are stateless, so the ephemeral port range for return traffic was not allowed in the opposite direction
Security groups overrode the NACL and blocked the responses
The route table needs a rule for ephemeral ports
Flow Logs show the NACL needs a reboot to apply
explain: Stateless NACLs require explicit rules for return traffic on ephemeral ports — the most common NACL failure. Security groups do not override NACLs, routes do not handle ports, and NACL changes apply without reboots.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A security team wants to detect and alert on port-scanning behavior against VPC workloads at the network level and automatically block repeat offenders' domains and IPs centrally. Which combination is most aligned?
options: NACLs updated manually after each scan is noticed
AWS Network Firewall (with Suricata-compatible rules) plus GuardDuty findings feeding centralized response, rather than hand-maintained subnet ACLs alone
WAF rate rules on the instances' private endpoints
CloudTrail alarms on DescribeSecurityGroups calls
explain: Network Firewall provides stateful inspection with IPS-style rules at scale, complemented by GuardDuty detection. Manual NACL updates cannot keep pace, WAF covers HTTP apps not network scans, and API-call alarms do not detect scanning traffic.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: An ALB's security group allows port 80 from anywhere, but the business requires HTTPS only. A scanner flags this. What is the correct remediation and a defense-in-depth addition?
options: Change the NACL to deny port 80 while leaving the security group open
Add a second security group that denies port 80 to override the allow
Remove the port 80 rule (or redirect HTTP to HTTPS at the ALB listener without exposing backends), and attach AWS WAF with managed rules to the ALB
Move the ALB to a private subnet so port 80 is unreachable
explain: Security groups have no deny rules, so the allow must be removed; listeners can redirect HTTP to HTTPS safely at the edge, and WAF adds application filtering. NACL surgery is brittle, deny groups do not exist, and a private ALB breaks the public application.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: All egress from application VPCs must be filtered so workloads can reach only approved domains (for example, software update sites), blocking data exfiltration to arbitrary endpoints. Which services enforce domain-based egress control?
options: Security groups with the approved domains listed as hostnames
NACLs containing the IP addresses of the approved domains, updated manually
CloudFront distributions in front of the update sites
AWS Network Firewall with domain-list rule groups (or a centralized egress design with Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall complementing it)
explain: Network Firewall filters egress by domain (SNI/Host) with managed rule groups, and DNS Firewall blocks resolution of unapproved domains. Security groups do not accept hostnames, domain IPs change too often for manual NACLs, and CloudFront is inbound content delivery.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A compliance rule requires TLS inspection avoidance: the design must NOT decrypt employee traffic, yet must still block known malicious IPs and domains at the perimeter. Which configuration respects this?
options: Deploy Network Firewall with IP/domain deny rules that do not require TLS decryption, leaving payload inspection out of scope
Require a TLS-inspecting proxy for all traffic regardless of policy
Use WAF to inspect encrypted payloads at Layer 7 for all VPC traffic
Block all TLS traffic at the NACL so nothing encrypted leaves
explain: IP and domain (SNI/DNS) filtering blocks known-bad destinations without decrypting payloads. Forced decryption violates the stated policy, WAF does not cover all VPC traffic, and blocking TLS entirely breaks the business.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: An incident shows a compromised instance communicating with a command-and-control domain that DNS-based controls missed because the malware used hardcoded IPs. Which additional network control would catch this?
options: Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall alone with more domain lists
AWS Network Firewall egress rules restricting outbound traffic to approved destinations (and GuardDuty findings for known malicious IPs), since IP-level egress filtering does not depend on DNS
Longer TTLs on internal DNS records
Enabling DNSSEC on the private hosted zones
explain: Hardcoded-IP exfiltration bypasses DNS controls, so destination-based network egress filtering and threat-intel detections are needed. More DNS lists still depend on DNS, and TTL/DNSSEC changes do not filter IP traffic.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A team must prove which workloads initiated rejected connection attempts at a subnet boundary during an audit window last month. Which data source answers this?
options: CloudTrail management events for the VPC
Security group rule change history in AWS Config
VPC Flow Logs (including REJECT records) stored in S3 and queried with Athena for the audit window
Application logs from the workloads that were online
explain: Flow Logs record accepted and rejected flows with source/destination and are retained in S3 for historical queries. CloudTrail logs API activity, Config tracks configuration changes, and application logs miss traffic from workloads that never logged it.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A Gateway Load Balancer deployment shows asymmetric traffic: return packets bypass the appliances, breaking their stateful inspection. What is the design requirement being violated?
options: Appliances must terminate TLS to see return traffic
The appliances need public IP addresses for return paths
Security groups must be disabled on appliance instances
GWLB flows must remain symmetric through the same appliance endpoint (GENEVE), with route tables in the appliance and consumer VPCs configured so both directions traverse the GWLB endpoints
explain: Gateway Load Balancer depends on symmetric routing through its endpoints for stateful appliances. TLS termination, public IPs, and disabling security groups are not the symmetry mechanism and introduce new risks.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Web ACL rules must differ per environment: production blocks a managed rule group's full set while staging only counts them during tuning. How is this managed cleanly in AWS WAF?
options: Create separate web ACLs per environment with the rule action set to Block in production and Count in staging, then promote the tuned configuration
Use one web ACL and change its rules hourly to match each environment
Set the staging ALB's security group to count mode
Apply the managed rules to CloudFront only and copy them weekly
explain: WAF rule actions are per web ACL; separate ACLs let staging tune in Count mode safely. Sharing one ACL makes environments interfere, security groups have no count mode, and manual copying drifts.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A public application must be reachable over both IPv4 and IPv6 from the internet while its backend instances can remain on private addressing. Which design delivers dual-stack access?
options: Enable IPv6 only on the Route 53 records and keep an IPv4-only VPC
Create a dual-stack VPC/subnets, assign IPv6 CIDRs, and use a dual-stack ALB (with AAAA records in Route 53) so clients can connect over either protocol
Give every backend instance a public IPv4 address instead
Use a NAT64 instance fleet as the only entry point
explain: Dual-stack subnets plus a dual-stack load balancer provide native IPv6 ingress with AAAA records. DNS alone cannot add IPv6 to an IPv4-only network, public backends reduce security, and NAT64 translation fleets are a workaround, not native dual-stack.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Instances in private subnets need outbound IPv6 internet access for updates but must not be reachable inbound over IPv6. Which gateway provides this?
options: A NAT gateway, which handles IPv6 the same as IPv4
The standard internet gateway with security groups alone as the stateful barrier for unsolicited IPv6
An egress-only internet gateway for IPv6 traffic
A NAT instance with IPv6 forwarding enabled
explain: Egress-only internet gateways allow outbound IPv6 and block unsolicited inbound, mirroring NAT semantics for IPv6. NAT gateways are IPv4-only, a plain IGW makes routed IPv6 addresses publicly reachable at the network layer, and NAT instances are legacy IPv4 constructs.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: A VPC is being designed IPv6-first for a new workload, but it must still reach a legacy IPv4-only database in another VPC. Which statement reflects the right planning?
options: IPv6 VPCs automatically translate to IPv4 databases with no configuration
An IPv6-only subnet can route to an IPv4 CIDR using a standard route table entry
The VPC's IPv6 block can be chosen freely like RFC1918 space

Plan dual-stack during transition: IPv6 CIDRs are AWS-assigned /56 per VPC with /64 subnets, keep IPv4 for the legacy path (or use translation options deliberately), because VPC IPv6 does not automatically interoperate with IPv4-only resources
explain: Dual-stack coexistence is the practical transition; IPv6 does not natively reach IPv4-only endpoints without translation design. Free choice applies to IPv4 RFC1918, while VPC IPv6 blocks are Amazon-provided, and plain routes cannot bridge protocol families.
domain: Domain 1: Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud

q: Security reviews must apply equally to IPv6 traffic, but the team's NACLs and security groups only contain IPv4 rules. What gap does this create and how is it closed?
options: IPv6 traffic bypasses IPv4-only rules where dual-stack is enabled; add explicit IPv6 rules (::/0 and specific prefixes) to security groups, NACLs, route tables, and firewall rule groups mirroring IPv4 policy
IPv6 traffic is automatically governed by IPv4 rules with the same CIDRs
Disabling DNS AAAA records closes the gap while IPv6 stays enabled
Flow Logs do not record IPv6, so the gap cannot be audited anyway
