The main alternatives fail because obscurity is not authorization, per-function email checks scatter the control and miss non-Lambda paths, and time-of-day rules do not distinguish admin users from other users.

q: A retailer's EKS nodes were compromised through one vulnerable pod, and the blast radius included every database the node role could reach. Beyond per-pod roles, what change most directly shrinks this node-level exposure?
options: Move all pods to a single node so there is only one role to monitor
Restrict the worker node IAM role to only the permissions nodes themselves need and block pod access to node credentials for workloads that have their own Pod Identity associations
Give the node role administrator access so incident response is faster next time
Let pods keep using the node role but rotate node credentials hourly
explain: Restrict the worker node IAM role to only the permissions nodes themselves need and block pod access to node credentials for workloads that have their own Pod Identity associations. Nodes need only a small set of permissions for registration and image pulls; removing data-plane permissions from the node role and preventing credential theft confines a pod compromise. The main alternatives fail because broadening the node role increases blast radius, rotation does not reduce what stolen credentials can do, and consolidating nodes concentrates rather than limits exposure.

q: A platform team wants auditors to be able to verify that a third-party monitoring vendor can never extend its own access beyond the read-only role it assumes. The vendor's role already has a read-only policy. What additional evidence-backed control bounds the vendor permanently?
options: Add a CloudWatch alarm that fires when the vendor assumes the role
Attach a permissions boundary to the vendor role capping it at read-only actions, so no policy edit can grant it more
Publish the vendor role's policy in a public repository for transparency
Require the vendor to send a weekly attestation email describing its access
explain: Attach a permissions boundary to the vendor role capping it at read-only actions, so no policy edit can grant it more. A permissions boundary is enforced by IAM itself, so the vendor role's effective permissions cannot exceed read-only no matter what its policies later say. The main alternatives fail because transparency and attestations document access without limiting it, and an alarm detects assumption, which is the vendor's normal and expected behavior.

q: An enterprise IdP can issue both SAML 2.0 and OIDC tokens, and a new mobile workforce app must federate to AWS from phones where a browser redirect flow fits SAML poorly. Which federation choice fits the mobile use case?
options: Use OIDC federation with the IdP for the mobile app's token exchange into Identity Center or Cognito, reserving SAML for the browser-based console flows
Issue each phone a client certificate and skip federation entirely
Create IAM users mirroring each mobile user so no federation is needed
Require the mobile app to implement the full SAML web browser SSO profile with XML signatures
explain: Use OIDC federation with the IdP for the mobile app's token exchange into Identity Center or Cognito, reserving SAML for the browser-based console flows. OIDC is designed around JSON tokens and authorization-code flows that suit mobile clients, while SAML's XML browser profile is built for web SSO. The main alternatives fail because SAML on mobile is brittle and unsupported in this pattern, certificates identify devices rather than user federation, and mirrored IAM users reintroduce long-lived credentials.

q: When an employee leaves, their Okta account is disabled within an hour, yet their federated AWS sessions sometimes remain usable until they expire naturally. Which configuration most directly shortens this residual access window?
options: Delete the organization's SAML provider until the leaver's sessions expire
Reduce permission set session durations in Identity Center and rely on SCIM deprovisioning to block new sessions for disabled users
Increase session durations so leavers are less tempted to share credentials
Store the leaver's name in a deny list inside every IAM policy in the organization
explain: Reduce permission set session durations in Identity Center and rely on SCIM deprovisioning to block new sessions for disabled users. Shorter sessions bound how long already-issued credentials remain useful, and SCIM deprovisioning through the IdP prevents the disabled identity from starting new ones. The main alternatives fail because longer sessions widen the window, per-policy deny lists are unmaintainable, and deleting the SAML provider locks out the entire workforce.

q: A CI/CD role can deploy CloudFormation stacks anywhere, and a misuse case showed it updating stacks belonging to other teams in production. How should the role be scoped to its own team's stacks?
options: Let the pipeline keep broad access but review its CloudTrail history weekly
Give the pipeline a separate AWS account and forbid it from deploying anywhere else
Require the pipeline to request a human approval for every deployment in chat
Add conditions to the role policy limiting cloudformation actions to stack ARNs matching the team's naming pattern and requiring a team tag on new stacks
explain: Add conditions to the role policy limiting cloudformation actions to stack ARNs matching the team's naming pattern and requiring a team tag on new stacks. ARN and tag conditions in the identity policy constrain which stacks the role can touch while preserving automated deployment for its own stacks. The main alternatives fail because a separate account breaks the shared production deployment model, weekly review detects rather than prevents misuse, and chat approvals do not change what the role itself is allowed to do.

q: A break-glass procedure must give on-call engineers emergency console access that is exceptional, strongly authenticated, and fully attributable. Which design meets that bar?
options: A dedicated federated break-glass role in Identity Center requiring phishing-resistant MFA, assigned to a tiny on-call group, with alerting on every assumption
A shared IAM user named admin whose password is sealed in an envelope in the office
An access key kept by the engineering manager and lent out during incidents
standing administrator permission set assigned to all engineers for faster response
explain: A dedicated federated break-glass role in Identity Center requiring phishing-resistant MFA, assigned to a tiny on-call group, with alerting on every assumption. Federated, MFA-gated, narrowly assigned roles make emergency access attributable to a person and visible to monitoring, which shared credentials can never be. The main alternatives fail because shared users, shared keys, and standing admin for everyone destroy attribution and keep emergency-level access permanently in place.

q: A multi-cloud analytics job running in Azure must load curated data into an AWS lake hourly, using the company's private CA that already issues workload certificates in both clouds. Which AWS feature turns that existing certificate trust into AWS credentials?
options: IAM SAML provider configured with Azure's metadata document
IAM Roles Anywhere with a trust anchor registered for the private CA
Amazon Cognito identity pools with an Azure AD enterprise connection
AWS Site-to-Site VPN so the Azure job appears to come from the VPC
explain: IAM Roles Anywhere with a trust anchor registered for the private CA. Roles Anywhere is cloud-agnostic: any workload presenting a certificate from a trusted CA can exchange it for temporary role credentials. The main alternatives fail because a VPN changes network reachability, not credential issuance, Cognito pools serve application user identities, and SAML providers federate human sign-ins rather than workload certificates.

q: An organization wants a single place to see which of its S3 buckets, Lambda functions, and snapshots are reachable from outside its accounts, refreshed continuously. Which deployment provides that view?
options: Amazon GuardDuty with S3 Protection enabled in every account
AWS Security Hub CSPM with a custom insight for public resources
One analyzer per account with findings emailed to each account owner
IAM Access Analyzer with an organization-level analyzer in the delegated administrator account
explain: IAM Access Analyzer with an organization-level analyzer in the delegated administrator account. An organization analyzer in a delegated admin account aggregates external access findings for supported resource types across all accounts continuously. The main alternatives fail because per-account analyzers fragment the view the requirement asks to centralize, and Security Hub and GuardDuty aggregate security findings of other kinds rather than policy-based external access analysis.

q: A SaaS product lets each tenant's support engineer assume a role in the tenant's account, and one engineer was socially engineered into using a rogue tenant's role ARN. Which control would have blocked the rogue session even with a valid-looking ARN?
options: A requirement that support sessions last no more than 15 minutes
A CloudTrail alarm on role assumptions from new source networks
An SCP that denies role assumption outside business hours
An external ID unique to each legitimate tenant, required by the role trust policy on every AssumeRole call
explain: An external ID unique to each legitimate tenant, required by the role trust policy on every AssumeRole call. The external ID is checked by the trust policy itself, so a session for a tenant whose ID the engineer cannot supply is refused before it starts. The main alternatives fail because short sessions, alarms, and time windows limit or observe rogue access but do not prevent the confused deputy session from being established.

q: A database team wants temporary just-in-time access to a production account only while a change ticket is open, with access expiring automatically. Which pattern implements this with Identity Center at its core?
options: A shared on-call role whose password rotates when tickets close
IAM users created per ticket and deleted by a weekly cleanup job
A permanent permission set whose policy contains a date condition edited by hand
Time-bound Identity Center account assignments for the team's group, granted when the ticket opens and removed automatically when it closes
explain: Time-bound Identity Center account assignments for the team's group, granted when the ticket opens and removed automatically when it closes. Identity Center group assignments can be granted and revoked programmatically, so the ticket system can time-box federated access without standing entitlements. The main alternatives fail because hand-edited date conditions and per-ticket IAM users are error-prone manual variants of the same idea, and shared role passwords are not federated access at all.

q: A gaming company authenticates players with Cognito, and game servers need to know a player's verified user ID without trusting values the client sends. Which practice should the servers follow?
options: Trust the user ID field in the game client's request payload after login
Validate the Cognito-issued token on the server side and read the subject claim from the verified token
Store each player's password hash in the game database for local verification
Look up the player by their chosen display name in the user pool
explain: Validate the Cognito-issued token on the server side and read the subject claim from the verified token. Only a server-verified token proves the identity Cognito issued; claims taken from it cannot be forged by the client. The main alternatives fail because client-supplied IDs and display names are attacker-controlled, and copying password hashes out of the managed pool creates a new credential store to breach.

q: An enterprise is choosing between keeping hundreds of account-local SAML providers or consolidating workforce federation in Identity Center. Which benefit is decisive for consolidation?
options: Identity Center removes the need for an external IdP altogether
SAML providers in each account automatically synchronize their role policies
Account-local providers give SCIM provisioning that Identity Center lacks
One federation point where permission sets and account assignments are managed centrally instead of a provider and roles maintained in every account
explain: One federation point where permission sets and account assignments are managed centrally instead of a provider and roles maintained in every account. Identity Center centralizes the IdP connection, permission sets, and assignments, eliminating per-account provider and role upkeep. The main alternatives fail because account-local providers do not synchronize with each other, an external IdP is still the identity source, and SCIM provisioning is an Identity Center capability rather than a local-provider one.

q: A workload on a factory-floor server with no internet path to AWS credential endpoints still needs temporary AWS credentials when connectivity is restored each night. The server already has a certificate from the plant CA. Which design fits?
options: Pre-generate a year of session tokens and store them on the server in advance
Install the AWS root credentials in the server's TPM for offline signing
Register the plant CA as a trust anchor in IAM Roles Anywhere and have the server's credential helper request temporary credentials when it connects
Use an EC2 instance profile delivered over the plant's private subnet
explain: Register the plant CA as a trust anchor in IAM Roles Anywhere and have the server's credential helper request temporary credentials when it connects. Roles Anywhere credential helpers exchange the server's X.509 certificate for temporary credentials on demand, which suits an intermittently connected workload. The main alternatives fail because pre-generated tokens expire long before a year and storing them is storing credentials, root credentials must never be distributed to workloads, and instance profiles exist only on EC2.

q: A security architect must design service-to-service calls between internal APIs so no shared API keys exist anywhere in the estate. Which authentication model should be mandated?
options: One API key per environment stored in a shared configuration bucket
IAM role credentials with SigV4 signing for each service's requests, scoped by per-service policies
Static bearer tokens issued by a spreadsheet-managed register
Mutual TLS alone with no authorization layer behind it
explain: IAM role credentials with SigV4 signing for each service's requests, scoped by per-service policies. Per-service IAM roles give each caller an identity, temporary credentials, and an authorizable policy, eliminating shared secrets. The main alternatives fail because shared keys and spreadsheet tokens are exactly the shared-secret model being banned, and mTLS authenticates a connection without expressing what the caller may do.

q: A regulator asks a bank to demonstrate that workforce access to customer data systems follows joiner-mover-leaver events within one business day. Which evidence chain best answers the regulator?
options: Screenshots of the IdP user list taken at each audit
CloudTrail records of console sign-ins sampled monthly
A spreadsheet of access reviews signed by team managers quarterly
SCIM provisioning logs and Identity Center assignment records tied to the HR-driven IdP lifecycle
explain: SCIM provisioning logs and Identity Center assignment records tied to the HR-driven IdP lifecycle. SCIM and assignment records show automated, timestamped propagation of HR lifecycle events into AWS access, which is the control the regulator is testing. The main alternatives fail because screenshots and quarterly spreadsheets are point-in-time and manual, and sampled sign-in logs show usage rather than whether entitlements tracked employment changes.

q: A partner's developers need access to exactly one prefix of a shared S3 bucket from their own account, and nothing else in the hosting account. Which grant is most precise?
options: An IAM user in the hosting account with the managed AmazonS3FullAccess policy
A pre-signed URL for the bucket root refreshed daily by an administrator
A bucket policy granting the partner account root full control of the bucket
A cross-account role in the hosting account whose policy allows only the needed actions on that bucket prefix
explain: A cross-account role in the hosting account whose policy allows only the needed actions on that bucket prefix. A scoped cross-account role expresses exactly the principal, actions, and prefix required and issues temporary credentials for them. The main alternatives fail because account-root bucket grants and full-access managed policies overshoot the single prefix, and daily root pre-signed URLs hand out broad reusable access.

q: An Identity Center administrator notices some users can still open the AWS access portal for an account after being removed from its assignment group. What is the most likely cause and fix?
options: The access portal caches assignments for 30 days and cannot be changed
Removed users keep access until their permission set is deleted
Group removal never affects account access in Identity Center
The users retain a direct user-level assignment to that account; remove direct assignments and manage access only through group assignments
explain: The users retain a direct user-level assignment to that account; remove direct assignments and manage access only through group assignments. Assignments can be made to users directly as well as via groups, so a leftover direct assignment explains continued access and removing it restores group-based control. The main alternatives fail because portal assignments are not cached for a month, deleting permission sets would affect everyone using them, and group removal does revoke group-derived assignments.

q: A team uses Verified Access for a legacy internal wiki and now needs the same identity and device checks for an internal HR application with different access rules per department. Which Verified Access construct should they add?
options: A second VPN endpoint dedicated to the HR department
A new VPC containing only the HR application and a copied wiki policy
A Cognito user pool for HR staff separate from the corporate IdP
A separate Verified Access group for the HR application with its own access policy referencing department claims and device trust
explain: A separate Verified Access group for the HR application with its own access policy referencing department claims and device trust. Verified Access groups bind an application set to its own policy, so department claims and device requirements can differ from the wiki's rules. The main alternatives fail because a VPN abandons per-application Verified Access control, copying the wiki policy ignores the differing department rules, and a separate Cognito pool fragments the corporate identity the design relies on.

q: A pharmaceutical firm must ensure that even account administrators cannot grant themselves access to a regulated research bucket from outside the organization network perimeter. Which layered design enforces this against the administrators themselves?
options: Quarterly access reviews where administrators attest to their own behavior
An IAM policy on the administrator role asking them not to use other networks
A CloudWatch alarm paging the compliance team when the bucket is read externally
A bucket policy with an explicit deny for requests not coming through the approved VPC endpoints or from outside the organization, which applies regardless of identity policy allows
explain: A bucket policy with an explicit deny for requests not coming through the approved VPC endpoints or from outside the organization, which applies regardless of identity policy allows. Resource-based explicit denies bind every principal including administrators, so network and organization conditions on the bucket enforce the perimeter independently of identity policies. The main alternatives fail because self-imposed identity policies can be edited by the administrators they constrain, and alarms and attestations observe or record behavior instead of preventing it.

q: A new OIDC provider is being registered for a partner CI system, and the architect must prevent tokens from any other audience on the same issuer from being accepted. Which trust policy element is essential?
options: An SCP allowing OIDC assumption in all accounts without conditions
A requirement that the partner use the same role name in every account
A condition on the token's expiration allowing only tokens older than one hour
A condition requiring the token's aud claim to equal the expected client ID for this provider
explain: A condition requiring the token's aud claim to equal the expected client ID for this provider. The audience claim identifies which client the token was minted for, so checking it stops tokens issued for other applications of the same IdP from being replayed here. The main alternatives fail because token age conditions do not identify the intended client, role naming is cosmetic, and unconditional SCP allowances widen rather than narrow token acceptance.

q: A retail platform wants developers to debug production only by assuming a read-only role whose sessions are recorded in the organization's trail and limited to one hour. Which settings deliver both constraints?
options: Set the IAM user password policy to expire every hour for the debug group
Create the role in each account with no trail so debugging is frictionless
Allow the role to be assumed with long-term keys for faster incident access
Set the role's maximum session duration to one hour and ensure the role is assumable only via the federated Identity Center permission set logged by the organization CloudTrail trail
explain: Set the role's maximum session duration to one hour and ensure the role is assumable only via the federated Identity Center permission set logged by the organization CloudTrail trail. Role maximum session duration caps federated sessions, and Identity Center assumptions are recorded by CloudTrail like other role assumptions in the organization trail. The main alternatives fail because password policies govern sign-in passwords, not role sessions, long-term keys bypass the federated logging path, and removing trails destroys the required record.

q: An architect is replacing password-based database logins for applications with IAM-based access where the database supports it, to remove another class of stored secret. Which principle from the identity domain does this extend?
options: Give each application the database master credentials for reliability
Prefer temporary, identity-bound credentials issued to the workload's role over static shared secrets
Store the strongest possible password in the most central vault available
Rotate shared secrets more frequently until risk reaches zero
explain: Prefer temporary, identity-bound credentials issued to the workload's role over static shared secrets. IAM-issued temporary credentials tie database access to the workload's verified identity and expire automatically, extending the same federation principle used for AWS APIs. The main alternatives fail because vaulting and rotating shared passwords still leaves shared secrets in place, and distributing master credentials maximizes rather than removes exposure.

q: A merger brings 800 staff from an acquired company whose identities live in a separate IdP that will operate for a year. How should workforce access be structured during the transition?
options: Force the acquired staff onto the parent IdP before granting any AWS access
Share one administrator account between both companies during the transition
Configure both IdPs as trusted identity sources for the access strategy, with Identity Center assignments mapping each company's groups to permission sets until the directories consolidate
Create IAM users for all 800 staff on day one and merge them later
explain: Configure both IdPs as trusted identity sources for the access strategy, with Identity Center assignments mapping each company's groups to permission sets until the directories consolidate. Identity Center can federate an external IdP while group-based assignments are mapped per source, letting both workforces be governed under one access model during migration. The main alternatives fail because 800 hand-made IAM users recreate the legacy problem at scale, blocking access until directory migration finishes stalls the business, and a shared admin account destroys attribution between the companies.

q: A security review finds a Lambda function URL in a development account is publicly invocable, discovered weeks after deployment. Which preventive identity control would have surfaced this at creation time?
options: IAM Access Analyzer external access findings reviewed through an organization analyzer with alerting on new public findings
A monthly penetration test of the development account
A requirement that developers name public resources with a public- prefix
Encrypting the function URL's traffic with TLS 1.3
explain: IAM Access Analyzer external access findings reviewed through an organization analyzer with alerting on new public findings. Access Analyzer evaluates the resource policy that made the URL public and reports it as external access continuously, so alerting on new findings catches it at creation. The main alternatives fail because naming conventions rely on developer honesty, monthly tests leave weeks of exposure, and TLS encrypts traffic to the public endpoint without restricting who can invoke it.

q: A team wants one IAM policy that lets project leads start and stop only EC2 instances tagged with their own project, across three project tags in use today and more later. Which condition design delivers this?
options: List every current instance ID in the policy's resource element
Duplicate the policy per project and plan to add copies as projects launch
Allow start and stop on all instances and filter misuse in billing reports
Match aws:PrincipalTag/project against ec2:ResourceTag/project in an ABAC condition on the start and stop actions
explain: Match aws:PrincipalTag/project against ec2:ResourceTag/project in an ABAC condition on the start and stop actions. ABAC tag matching scales to new projects automatically because authorization follows the tags rather than enumerated resources or duplicated policies. The main alternatives fail because enumerated IDs go stale as instances are replaced, per-project copies multiply maintenance, and billing reports cannot prevent an unauthorized stop.

q: A cloud broker platform assumes roles into hundreds of customer accounts from one central account, and one customer's trust policy was copied from another's without its external ID. What risk does the missing external ID create and how is it fixed fleet-wide?
options: Any customer who learns that account's role ARN could trick the broker into acting there; add the per-customer external ID condition to every trust policy and verify with Access Analyzer
No risk exists because role ARNs are random; rotate the ARNs annually
The broker's sessions will last too long; shorten the central role's duration limit
The broker will be billed for the customer's usage; add a cost allocation tag condition
explain: Any customer who learns that account's role ARN could trick the broker into acting there; add the per-customer external ID condition to every trust policy and verify with Access Analyzer. Without an external ID the confused deputy protection is absent, so a malicious customer can steer the broker's privileged session into a victim account; the fix is the ID condition plus analyzer verification. The main alternatives fail because session length and billing are unrelated to the steering risk, and role ARNs are discoverable identifiers, not secrets, so rotating them is not a control.

q: An internal tool needs to call AWS APIs on behalf of the signed-in employee, using the employee's own permissions rather than a powerful service account. Which pattern preserves the employee's identity end to end?
options: Federate the employee through Identity Center or Cognito, exchange the token for a role session with the employee's scoped permission set, and call APIs with those temporary credentials
Ask the employee to paste their access key into the tool at startup
Grant the tool's role administrator access and log employee names in the tool's database
Hard-code a service account key in the tool and tag its calls with the employee's name
explain: Federate the employee through Identity Center or Cognito, exchange the token for a role session with the employee's scoped permission set, and call APIs with those temporary credentials. Identity propagation through federation keeps authorization decisions bound to the actual user and their entitlements, with CloudTrail attribution to match. The main alternatives fail because tagging or logging a name beside a shared powerful credential does not constrain what the credential can do, and collecting user keys recreates long-lived secret handling.

q: A healthcare startup must prove to an enterprise customer that its workforce access uses phishing-resistant authentication for administrative roles. Which Identity Center configuration provides this?
options: Increase the password length requirement for the corporate IdP to 20 characters
Allow SMS codes as the second factor for administrator sign-ins
Require WebAuthn/FIDO2 security keys as the MFA method for administrative permission set assignments
Send a confirmation email to the administrator's manager after each sign-in
explain: Require WebAuthn/FIDO2 security keys as the MFA method for administrative permission set assignments. FIDO2/WebAuthn authenticators are phishing-resistant because the credential is bound to the legitimate origin, satisfying the customer's explicit requirement. The main alternatives fail because SMS codes can be phished or SIM-swapped, after-the-fact emails do not authenticate the session, and longer passwords remain phishable knowledge factors.

q: A logistics firm lets warehouse supervisors use a shared tablet app that opens AWS-backed dashboards, and individual accountability for actions taken in the app is currently impossible. Which identity change restores per-person accountability?
options: Let supervisors pick their name from a dropdown after the app signs in with a shared login
Record the tablet's device ID as the acting identity in audit logs
Embed one IAM access key in the tablet app and rotate it monthly
Require each supervisor to sign in individually through the app's Cognito user pool so actions carry their own identity, instead of a shared app credential
explain: Require each supervisor to sign in individually through the app's Cognito user pool so actions carry their own identity, instead of a shared app credential. Individual sign-in binds every session and API call to a verified person, which is what accountability requires. The main alternatives fail because a shared embedded key and a shared login both attribute actions to the credential rather than the person, and a device ID identifies hardware shared by the whole shift.

q: A development team in one account needs to read a KMS-encrypted dataset owned by another account, and both the bucket policy and key policy must agree to the access. A request keeps failing with access denied despite the bucket policy allowing the team. Which additional grant is most likely missing?
options: A VPC endpoint policy allowing traffic to the team's VPC
The KMS key policy or a grant allowing the team's principal to use the key for decryption
A Cognito identity pool role mapped to the team's group
An SCP in the team's organization allowing S3 access
explain: The KMS key policy or a grant allowing the team's principal to use the key for decryption. Access to KMS-encrypted objects requires authorization on both the object and the key, so a missing key-side grant blocks decryption even when S3 allows it. The main alternatives fail because endpoint, SCP, and Cognito settings do not substitute for the key policy permission that KMS evaluates on every decrypt call.

q: An organization discovers service accounts in its data platform still authenticate with access keys created years ago, several belonging to departed vendors. Which replacement and guardrail pair eliminates this class of credential?
options: Move service authentication to IAM roles and Roles Anywhere where needed, and apply an SCP denying creation of new access keys for service principals
Move the keys into a central S3 bucket with versioning enabled
Rotate every service access key and document the new rotation owner
Require vendors to confirm by email each quarter that keys are still needed
explain: Move service authentication to IAM roles and Roles Anywhere where needed, and apply an SCP denying creation of new access keys for service principals. Roles issue temporary credentials automatically and an SCP can stop the long-lived pattern from being recreated, addressing both the existing keys and future drift. The main alternatives fail because rotation and storage changes keep long-lived keys alive, and quarterly emails are an attestation rather than a technical control.

q: A support engineer needs to view (but never change) resources in forty customer accounts during escalations, without forty separate logins. Which Identity Center design provides this?
options: A single cross-account role in each account trusting the engineer's personal IAM user key
Forty IAM users with the same password set by the engineer
Browser bookmarks to each account's root sign-in page
One Identity Center user assigned a read-only permission set across the forty accounts, signed in once through the access portal
explain: One Identity Center user assigned a read-only permission set across the forty accounts, signed in once through the access portal. Identity Center gives one federated identity with per-account permission set assignments, so a single sign-in reaches all forty read-only roles. The main alternatives fail because per-account users and personal-key trusts fragment identity and lifecycle, and root sign-ins bypass role-based least privilege entirely.

q: A fintech wants temporary elevation: engineers normally run read-only, but during an approved incident they may assume a write role for two hours. Which combination implements time-boxed elevation cleanly?
options: Give engineers the write role's access keys in a sealed break-glass vault
Permanently assign both permission sets and trust engineers to use the read-only one by default
An incident-scoped Identity Center assignment or session granted on approval that expires automatically, layered on the standing read-only assignment
Edit the read-only permission set to add write actions during incidents and remove them after
explain: An incident-scoped Identity Center assignment or session granted on approval that expires automatically, layered on the standing read-only assignment. Time-bound assignments make elevation an explicit, expiring grant tied to approval, rather than a standing capability restrained only by habit. The main alternatives fail because standing dual assignments are permanent elevation in practice, vaulted keys bypass federation and expiry, and hand-editing shared permission sets risks leaving write access behind.

q: A company federates with SAML and finds the IdP sends a department attribute that AWS roles are not using, forcing separate roles per department. How can the attribute drive authorization directly?
options: Pass the department as a session tag from the SAML assertion and write ABAC policies that match the session tag to resource tags
Create an IAM user per department to hold the shared policies
Rename each role to include the department and assign roles manually per user
Strip the department attribute so all roles behave identically
explain: Pass the department as a session tag from the SAML assertion and write ABAC policies that match the session tag to resource tags. SAML attributes can become session tags at federation, and ABAC policies can then authorize by department without multiplying roles. The main alternatives fail because manual role assignment per user does not scale and ignores the attribute already provided, stripping it removes useful signal, and shared department users destroy individual identity.

q: An auditor flags that a VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 allows any principal in the VPC to reach any bucket, including personal buckets outside the company. Which endpoint policy change closes this while keeping approved application access working?
options: Allow only the organization's buckets by adding an aws:ResourceOrgID condition and the specific application actions to the endpoint policy
Allow all buckets but log endpoint usage to CloudWatch for review
Remove the endpoint so all S3 traffic uses the internet gateway instead
Restrict the endpoint by source port range in the subnet route table
explain: Allow only the organization's buckets by adding an aws:ResourceOrgID condition and the specific application actions to the endpoint policy. Endpoint policies can condition on the resource's organization, confining the network path to company-owned buckets while preserving application flows. The main alternatives fail because removing the endpoint pushes traffic to the internet and loses the control point, logging observes rather than restricts, and route tables cannot express organization conditions.

q: A new administrator asks why a role they created cannot be assumed by its intended service even though the role's permission policy is correct. Which overlooked element should they check first?
options: The account's password policy, which governs role assumption
The role's trust policy, which controls which principals may assume the role independently of its permission policy
The role's session duration, which defaults to zero until set
The permission policy's version number, which must be manually incremented
explain: The role's trust policy, which controls which principals may assume the role independently of its permission policy. A role has two sides: the trust policy decides who can assume it, and the permission policy decides what the session can do; a correct second side cannot fix a missing first side. The main alternatives fail because session duration defaults to one hour rather than zero, password policies govern IAM user passwords, and policy versions are managed automatically on update.

q: A bank uses a customer managed KMS key for its loan archive and compliance requires cryptographic material to be renewed on a schedule without re-encrypting the archive by hand. Which KMS feature satisfies the renewal requirement?
options: Export the key material monthly and re-import it under a new alias
Schedule deletion and recreation of the key each year with a new key ID
Rotate the data keys by re-uploading every archived object each quarter
Enable automatic key rotation on the symmetric customer managed key so KMS creates new backing material annually while keeping the same key ID
explain: Enable automatic key rotation on the symmetric customer managed key so KMS creates new backing material annually while keeping the same key ID. Automatic rotation generates fresh backing material for the same key ID and KMS transparently uses it for new encryptions while old material still decrypts existing data. The main alternatives fail because deleting and recreating the key breaks references and risks data loss, key material for AWS-generated keys cannot be exported, and manual re-upload is the hand work the requirement excludes.

q: A developer's IAM policy allows kms:Decrypt on a key, yet calls still fail until an administrator edits a second document attached to the key itself. Which concept explains this two-sided authorization?
options: A KMS key policy must enable IAM policies for the key; without that delegation in the key policy, IAM allows alone have no effect
KMS keys require a bucket policy in addition to the key policy
IAM policies apply to KMS only after the key is used once from the console
The developer must be the key's creator for IAM policies to apply
explain: A KMS key policy must enable IAM policies for the key; without that delegation in the key policy, IAM allows alone have no effect. Every KMS key has a key policy, and IAM policy authorization works only when the key policy delegates to the account's IAM policies. The main alternatives fail because bucket policies belong to S3, key creation ownership does not gate IAM delegation, and no console first-use step exists in KMS authorization.

q: Amazon EBS needs to encrypt volumes with a customer managed key, but the storage team does not want a permanent standing permission granted to the service in the key policy. Which KMS mechanism gives the service time-limited use of the key on behalf of users?
options: A key policy statement granting the whole account unconditional decrypt rights
KMS grants created for the service, which can be listed, constrained, and retired when no longer needed
An IAM user for the EBS service whose key is stored in the volume metadata
Disabling the key between volume creation operations
explain: KMS grants created for the service, which can be listed, constrained, and retired when no longer needed. Grants delegate constrained, revocable permission to use a key, which is how AWS services obtain temporary key access for resources they create for users. The main alternatives fail because services do not hold IAM user keys, unconditional account-wide decrypt rights abandon least privilege, and disabling the key breaks all workloads using it.

q: A messaging platform encrypts millions of messages per day and cannot call KMS for every single message without latency and cost exploding. Which encryption pattern is designed for this?
options: Envelope encryption: KMS generates a data key, messages are encrypted locally under data keys, and only the small encrypted data keys involve KMS
Use one data key forever for all messages to avoid further KMS calls
Encrypt each message directly with the KMS Encrypt API and accept the call volume
Store messages in plaintext and encrypt only the database indexes
explain: Envelope encryption: KMS generates a data key, messages are encrypted locally under data keys, and only the small encrypted data keys involve KMS. Envelope encryption is the standard KMS pattern for scale: a data key encrypts the payload locally and KMS protects the data key itself. The main alternatives fail because direct KMS encryption is subject to per-call quotas and latency, plaintext storage defeats the purpose, and a single eternal data key makes one compromise expose everything.

q: A research firm must be able to prove which key encrypted each dataset and revoke one dataset's key without affecting others, which rules out the default S3-managed encryption for new buckets. Which S3 encryption option should be standardized?
options: A bucket policy requiring TLS so data is encrypted in transit only
Client-side compression before upload so stored objects are unreadable
SSE-S3 with AES-256 keys managed entirely by Amazon S3
SSE-KMS with a separate customer managed key per dataset classification
explain: SSE-KMS with a separate customer managed key per dataset classification. SSE-KMS with customer managed keys gives per-key control, CloudTrail-visible usage, and independent revocation, while S3-managed keys offer none of that control. The main alternatives fail because SSE-S3 keys cannot be revoked or audited per dataset, TLS protects movement rather than storage, and compression is not encryption.

q: An encrypted EBS snapshot must be shared with a partner account so they can create volumes from it, and the copy operation keeps failing on key permissions. What must accompany the snapshot share for it to succeed?
options: Convert the snapshot to an unencrypted one before sharing it
Share the customer managed KMS key with the partner account as well, so they are authorized to decrypt the snapshot's data
Enable the snapshot's public sharing flag so any account can copy it
Give the partner the source account's root credentials for the copy
explain: Share the customer managed KMS key with the partner account as well, so they are authorized to decrypt the snapshot's data. An encrypted snapshot cannot be used without key access, so the key must be shared with the recipient account alongside the snapshot. The main alternatives fail because unencrypting or public sharing destroys the protection the data requires, and root credentials must never be handed to another account.

q: A global SaaS keeps primary data in one Region and a disaster-recovery copy in another, and wants both copies encrypted under keys with the same key material and ID for simpler failover. Which KMS capability provides this?
options: Copying the key by exporting its material and importing it into a new key
Using two unrelated single-Region keys and re-encrypting all data at failover
Multi-Region KMS keys, replicating the same key ID and material into the second Region as a replica key
A single-Region key called over the internet from the recovery Region
explain: Multi-Region KMS keys, replicating the same key ID and material into the second Region as a replica key. Multi-Region keys are interoperable replicas sharing ID and material, so ciphertext from one Region decrypts in the other without re-encryption. The main alternatives fail because AWS-generated key material cannot be exported, unrelated keys force a full re-encryption during a disaster, and KMS keys only operate within their own Region.

q: A key administrator suspects a customer managed key was exposed and wants to stop its use immediately while an investigation decides its fate. Which action is the correct first response?
options: Schedule the key for deletion with the shortest waiting period
Disable the key immediately, which blocks all use while preserving the key and its data for later decisions
Delete every object encrypted under the key before investigating
Rotate the key so future encryptions use new material
explain: Disable the key immediately, which blocks all use while preserving the key and its data for later decisions. Disabling is reversible and immediate, halting encryption and decryption while investigators decide whether deletion or re-enablement is warranted. The main alternatives fail because deletion scheduling starts an irreversible countdown for data encrypted under the key, destroying data pre-empts the investigation, and rotation does not stop use of existing material.

q: A defense contractor's contract mandates a dedicated, single-tenant hardware security module under their exclusive control, certified to FIPS 140-2 Level 3, for key storage. Which AWS offering matches this mandate?
options: Amazon S3 server-side encryption with customer-provided keys
AWS KMS with a customer managed key and automatic rotation enabled
AWS Certificate Manager with a dedicated certificate authority
AWS CloudHSM, providing dedicated HSM clusters in the customer's VPC under their sole control
explain: AWS CloudHSM, providing dedicated HSM clusters in the customer's VPC under their sole control. CloudHSM is the dedicated single-tenant HSM service meeting the exclusive-control and certification requirement; KMS is a shared multi-tenant service by design. The main alternatives fail because KMS cannot offer dedicated hardware or customer-only control, ACM manages certificates rather than general HSM key storage, and SSE-C concerns S3 object keys, not an HSM cluster.

q: A payments company wants its KMS keys' cryptographic operations to occur inside its own CloudHSM cluster rather than KMS's shared infrastructure. Which KMS feature connects the two?
options: An ACM private CA hosted on the CloudHSM cluster
A VPC endpoint from KMS into the CloudHSM cluster's subnets
A KMS grant issued to the CloudHSM cluster's IAM role
A KMS custom key store backed by the CloudHSM cluster, so keys in that store are generated and used inside the HSMs
explain: A KMS custom key store backed by the CloudHSM cluster, so keys in that store are generated and used inside the HSMs. Custom key stores let KMS create and use keys whose material lives in the customer's CloudHSM cluster, combining the KMS API with HSM-resident material. The main alternatives fail because endpoints move network traffic rather than key material, Private CA issues certificates, and grants delegate key use but do not relocate where keys live.

q: A public website terminates TLS at an Application Load Balancer and the team is tired of manual certificate renewals causing expirations. Which setup removes the manual renewal burden?
options: Disable TLS and rely on the VPC's private subnets for confidentiality
Generate a self-signed certificate on the load balancer each month with a cron job
Import a three-year commercial certificate so renewals are rare
Request the public certificate in AWS Certificate Manager, attach it to the load balancer, and let ACM manage renewal and deployment
explain: Request the public certificate in AWS Certificate Manager, attach it to the load balancer, and let ACM manage renewal and deployment. ACM issues and automatically renews public certificates integrated with load balancers, eliminating manual tracking and reinstallation. The main alternatives fail because long-lived imports still expire and are not ACM-renewed, self-signed certificates are untrusted by browsers, and private subnets do not encrypt traffic in transit.

q: Internal microservices must authenticate each other with X.509 certificates that live for days, not years, and must never be exposed to a public CA. Which service issues and manages these certificates?
options: Self-signed certificates generated at container startup
Let's Encrypt certificates installed by an agent on each host
ACM public certificates requested for each internal service name
AWS Certificate Manager Private Certificate Authority issuing short-lived private certificates
explain: AWS Certificate Manager Private Certificate Authority issuing short-lived private certificates. Private CA is the managed private certificate authority for internal PKI, and it supports short-lived certificate modes suited to ephemeral workloads. The main alternatives fail because public ACM certificates cannot be issued for purely internal names and are publicly trusted by design, external public CAs expose internal naming, and self-signed certificates provide no chain of trust between services.

q: A streaming site behind CloudFront must negotiate only modern, strong TLS with viewers, and legacy protocol versions must be refused. Which configuration enforces this?
options: Add a WAF rule blocking HTTP user agents that look outdated
Terminate viewer TLS at an origin EC2 instance with its own OpenSSL defaults
Select a CloudFront security policy requiring TLS 1.3 (with TLS 1.2 as the minimum floor the policy enforces) for viewer connections
Enable HTTP/2 and assume legacy TLS versions are disabled automatically
explain: Select a CloudFront security policy requiring TLS 1.3 (with TLS 1.2 as the minimum floor the policy enforces) for viewer connections. The distribution's security policy sets the minimum TLS version and cipher suites CloudFront will negotiate with viewers. The main alternatives fail because origin TLS settings govern the CloudFront-to-origin leg, not viewers, WAF rules inspect requests after TLS exists, and HTTP/2 enablement does not control TLS versions.

q: An auditor finds S3 requests still succeeding over plaintext HTTP from an old internal tool and requires the bucket to refuse all non-TLS traffic. Which control enforces this at the bucket?
options: Enabling default encryption on the bucket so HTTP requests fail
Moving the bucket into a VPC with a gateway endpoint
A bucket policy statement denying all actions when aws:SecureTransport is false
Requiring SSE-KMS so plaintext requests cannot read the data
explain: A bucket policy statement denying all actions when aws:SecureTransport is false. The aws:SecureTransport condition in a deny statement is the canonical way to require TLS for every request to the bucket. The main alternatives fail because encryption at rest does not block HTTP transport, buckets do not live in VPCs, and SSE-KMS still permits the request to arrive over plaintext even if the data stays encrypted.

q: An unencrypted RDS instance holding customer records must become encrypted, and the team plans to flip a setting on the running instance. Why will that plan fail, and what is the working path?
options: RDS encryption can only be enabled at creation, so the team must copy a snapshot with encryption enabled and restore a new instance from it
Encryption requires the instance to be Multi-AZ before the setting appears
RDS instances inherit encryption from the VPC, so the VPC must be recreated
The setting exists but needs a reboot scheduled through the console
explain: RDS encryption can only be enabled at creation, so the team must copy a snapshot with encryption enabled and restore a new instance from it. Storage encryption is a creation-time property of an RDS instance; the snapshot-copy-and-restore path is the documented way to encrypt an existing instance. The main alternatives fail because Multi-AZ is unrelated to encryption availability, no reboot enables it post-creation, and VPCs have no encryption setting to inherit.

q: A Region's new EBS volumes occasionally launch unencrypted despite a team convention, depending on who built the AMI. Which account-level setting makes encryption unavoidable for new volumes in that Region?
options: Enable EBS encryption by default for the account in that Region, using a specified default key
Encrypt the AMIs so volumes inherit encryption from the image
Ask builders to check the encryption box and audit weekly
Add a tag policy requiring an encrypted tag on every volume
explain: Enable EBS encryption by default for the account in that Region, using a specified default key. Encryption by default is enforced by EC2 itself for every new volume in the Region regardless of caller or image. The main alternatives fail because tag policies govern tag format, not encryption, manual checking is the unreliable status quo, and AMI encryption does not force volumes created from unencrypted snapshots or other paths.

q: A law firm needs clients to verify the authenticity of digitally signed filings for decades, and its cryptographers want a post-quantum signing capability in KMS. Which KMS capability addresses the post-quantum requirement?
options: Use an RSA 4096 key and increase its size again when quantum computers mature
Store the signing key in CloudHSM and rely on its FIPS certification
Create a KMS key with a post-quantum ML-DSA key spec and use it for signing and verification
Enable automatic rotation on an ECC key so signatures stay fresh
explain: Create a KMS key with a post-quantum ML-DSA key spec and use it for signing and verification. KMS supports ML-DSA post-quantum signature schemes for keys used to sign and verify, designed to resist quantum attacks on classical algorithms. The main alternatives fail because larger RSA and ECC remain quantum-vulnerable classical algorithms, rotation does not change the algorithm, and FIPS certification of storage does not make the signature scheme post-quantum.

q: Two agencies must establish shared encryption keys for data that will remain secret for 30 years, and their threat model includes future quantum computers recording today's exchanges. Which KMS post-quantum capability is relevant to protecting key establishment against that threat?
options: CloudHSM clusters upgraded to the newest firmware available
KMS automatic key rotation set to the shortest available interval
KMS support for ML-KEM post-quantum key encapsulation for deriving shared secrets
ACM certificates issued with 4096-bit RSA keys for the agencies
explain: KMS support for ML-KEM post-quantum key encapsulation for deriving shared secrets. ML-KEM is the post-quantum key encapsulation mechanism standardized for establishing shared secrets that remain safe against harvest-now-decrypt-later quantum attacks. The main alternatives fail because rotation and larger RSA address classical key hygiene but not quantum attacks on key establishment, and HSM firmware does not change the cryptographic algorithm in use.

q: A payments service must prove a message authorizing a transfer was not altered in transit between internal systems. Which KMS key type is built for generating and verifying message authentication codes?
options: An HMAC KMS key used with GenerateMac and VerifyMac
A symmetric encryption key used to encrypt the entire message twice
An ML-DSA signing key used to encrypt the message digest
An imported RSA key pair with the private key shared to verifiers
explain: An HMAC KMS key used with GenerateMac and VerifyMac. KMS HMAC keys are dedicated to generating and verifying HMACs, giving integrity and authenticity for messages without encrypting them. The main alternatives fail because double encryption adds confidentiality machinery without an authentication code, signing keys sign rather than encrypt digests in this pattern, and sharing a private key destroys its security value.

q: A partner account must decrypt objects under a key owned by the data provider, and the provider wants to authorize the partner from the provider's side alone. Which statement about cross-account KMS access is correct?
options: Sharing the key's ARN with the partner implicitly authorizes its use
Cross-account KMS use works automatically between accounts in one organization
The partner's IAM policy allowing kms:Decrypt is sufficient by itself
The key policy in the provider's account must allow the partner principal; the partner's IAM policies alone cannot grant use of another account's key
explain: The key policy in the provider's account must allow the partner principal; the partner's IAM policies alone cannot grant use of another account's key. For cross-account use the key policy must grant the external principal, after which the caller's own IAM policies also apply within their account. The main alternatives fail because an IAM policy cannot reach into another account's key without the key policy's grant, ARNs are identifiers not authorizations, and organization membership does not implicitly share keys.

q: A private workload must call KMS without its traffic leaving the VPC, and auditors want the endpoint itself restricted to one key and one role. Which configuration delivers both?
options: A NAT gateway dedicated to KMS traffic from the private subnets
An interface VPC endpoint for KMS with an endpoint policy allowing only the specified key ARN and role
A gateway endpoint for KMS placed on the private route tables
An internet gateway with a security group limited to port 443
explain: An interface VPC endpoint for KMS with an endpoint policy allowing only the specified key ARN and role. KMS is reached through interface endpoints, whose policies can scope principals, actions, and the exact key resource reachable through them. The main alternatives fail because gateway endpoints exist only for S3 and DynamoDB, and NAT or internet gateways send the traffic over public paths the design is trying to avoid.

q: CloudTrail logs delivered to a central bucket must be encrypted with a key the security team controls and validated as untampered. Which trail configuration supports both goals?
options: Store logs in CloudWatch Logs with default encryption and no export
Deliver logs to a bucket with SSE-S3 and enable MFA Delete on the bucket
Configure the trail with SSE-KMS using the security team's customer managed key and enable log file validation
Encrypt logs with a key owned by each member account and rotate them manually
explain: Configure the trail with SSE-KMS using the security team's customer managed key and enable log file validation. Trails support SSE-KMS with a chosen key for delivery encryption, and digest-based log file validation proves delivered files were not altered. The main alternatives fail because S3-managed keys remove the key control required, per-account keys fragment central control, and CloudWatch-only storage omits the validated file delivery the auditors asked for.

q: A DynamoDB table storing regulated identifiers must be encrypted under a key the company can disable to render the data unreadable in an emergency. Which table encryption choice gives that kill-switch property?
options: The default AWS owned key, because its policy is editable by the account
TLS in transit between the application and DynamoDB
A customer managed KMS key for the table's encryption at rest, which the company can disable
Client-side field naming conventions that hide the identifiers
explain: A customer managed KMS key for the table's encryption at rest, which the company can disable. A customer managed key is under the customer's control, so disabling it stops decryption of the table's data; AWS owned keys cannot be viewed, disabled, or audited by the customer. The main alternatives fail because AWS owned key policies are not customer-editable, naming conventions are not encryption, and TLS protects data in motion rather than at rest.

q: A Lambda function reads database credentials passed as environment variables, and a review requires those variables encrypted under the team's own key with decrypt access separated from deployment access. Which approach meets the review?
options: Encrypt the function's environment variables with a customer managed KMS key and scope kms:Decrypt for the function role separately from the deployer role
Put the credentials in an S3 object the whole account can read
Base64-encode the credentials before setting them as variables
Store the credentials in the function description field instead
explain: Encrypt the function's environment variables with a customer managed KMS key and scope kms:Decrypt for the function role separately from the deployer role. Lambda supports CMK encryption of environment variables, and key permissions can separate who deploys configuration from which identity may decrypt it at runtime. The main alternatives fail because encoding is not encryption, description fields are broadly visible metadata, and account-readable storage widens rather than separates access.

q: A Redis cluster in ElastiCache carries session data and compliance now requires that data moving between nodes and clients be encrypted as well as the data at rest. Which setting addresses the in-motion requirement?
options: Enable ElastiCache in-transit encryption (TLS) for the replication group
Place the cluster in private subnets with no internet route
Enable at-rest encryption with a customer managed key only
Require clients to compress payloads before sending them
explain: Enable ElastiCache in-transit encryption (TLS) for the replication group. In-transit encryption is the distinct ElastiCache feature that TLS-encrypts traffic between clients and nodes and between nodes themselves. The main alternatives fail because at-rest encryption protects stored data only, private subnets control reachability rather than confidentiality on the wire, and compression is not encryption.

q: A company is building a two-tier private PKI: an offline root in a vault-like account delegating to issuing subordinates in workload accounts. Which ACM Private CA design matches?
options: A single subordinate CA with no root, self-signed by each workload
A root CA in the security account kept offline in practice, with subordinate CAs for day-to-day issuance in the workload accounts
CloudHSM clusters in each account issuing browser-trusted certificates
One public ACM certificate per account used as a local CA
explain: A root CA in the security account kept offline in practice, with subordinate CAs for day-to-day issuance in the workload accounts. Private CA supports CA hierarchies, letting an organization keep a root as the trust anchor while subordinate CAs handle issuance closer to workloads. The main alternatives fail because public certificates cannot act as CAs for private issuance, a rootless self-signed design gives no chain of trust, and CloudHSM stores keys but is not itself a managed CA service.

q: A team imported its own commercial certificate into ACM for a load balancer and is surprised that, unlike ACM-issued certificates, it approaches expiry with warnings but no renewal. Which fact explains this and what must the team do?
options: ACM does not renew imported certificates; the team must obtain a renewed certificate and reimport it before expiry
Imported certificates renew only when the load balancer is restarted
The certificate is renewed by the issuing CA pushing it to ACM automatically
ACM renews imported certificates if the account enables paid support
explain: ACM does not renew imported certificates; the team must obtain a renewed certificate and reimport it before expiry. Managed renewal applies to certificates ACM issues; imported certificates remain the owner's responsibility to renew and reimport. The main alternatives fail because restarts and support tiers do not change ACM's renewal scope, and external CAs have no channel to push renewals into an ACM import.

q: After enabling automatic rotation on a KMS key, an engineer expects last year's ciphertexts to become undecryptable and is confused that they still decrypt. Which explanation is correct?
options: Old ciphertext decrypts only because of a caching bug in the SDK
Rotation adds new backing material for new encryptions but retains old material for decryption, so existing ciphertext remains readable until it is re-encrypted
Rotation failed silently and must be re-enabled from the CLI
Rotation deletes old material after a 30-day grace period
explain: Rotation adds new backing material for new encryptions but retains old material for decryption, so existing ciphertext remains readable until it is re-encrypted. KMS rotation is designed to be transparent: the key ID and decryptability of existing data are preserved while new data uses fresh material. The main alternatives fail because rotation does not fail silently when enabled, SDK caching does not explain service-side decryption, and old material is retained rather than deleted on a timer.

q: An incident review asks exactly who decrypted a set of regulated objects last month and with which key. Which data source answers this?
options: CloudWatch memory metrics on the decrypting application hosts
S3 access logs showing the object's storage class transitions
The KMS key policy history stored in the key's metadata
CloudTrail records of KMS decrypt operations, which log the key, principal, and time for each use
explain: CloudTrail records of KMS decrypt operations, which log the key, principal, and time for each use. KMS logs cryptographic operations to CloudTrail as management events, providing the auditable record of who used which key and when. The main alternatives fail because key policies show intended permissions rather than actual usage, S3 logs do not record KMS operations, and host metrics contain no key-usage identity detail.

q: A multi-tenant SaaS wants cryptographic isolation per tenant so that offboarding one tenant can make only that tenant's data permanently unreadable. Which key design achieves this?
options: Tag one shared key with tenant names and filter decrypt calls by tag in the application
Issue a separate customer managed KMS key per tenant and schedule that key for deletion at offboarding
Encrypt all tenants under one shared key and delete the tenant's rows at offboarding
Use SSE-S3 for tenant data so S3 handles isolation automatically
explain: Issue a separate customer managed KMS key per tenant and schedule that key for deletion at offboarding. Per-tenant keys make cryptographic erasure possible: destroying one key renders only that tenant's ciphertext unreadable. The main alternatives fail because a shared key cannot be destroyed for one tenant without harming all others, application tag filters are bypassable and not cryptographic isolation, and S3-managed keys give no per-tenant control.

q: Two administrators keep undermining each other's key changes: the same people who use a production key daily can also edit its policy and disable it. Which separation should the key policy enforce?
options: Give every administrator both administration and usage for convenience
Remove the key policy and rely on IAM policies from all accounts
Let the workload roles administer the key so they are never blocked
Grant key administration (policy, rotation, disabling) to a small admin role and key usage (encrypt/decrypt) to workload roles, with neither holding the other's permissions
explain: Grant key administration (policy, rotation, disabling) to a small admin role and key usage (encrypt/decrypt) to workload roles, with neither holding the other's permissions. KMS key policies support separating administrators from users of a key, enforcing separation of duties on the most sensitive control plane. The main alternatives fail because combining both permission sets is the problem being fixed, a key always has a key policy, and letting users administer the key widens the same risk.

q: A storage team faces soaring KMS request charges from an S3 bucket with SSE-KMS and millions of small objects, without any change in security requirements. Which S3 feature reduces those KMS calls?
options: Switch the bucket to SSE-S3 so objects stop being encrypted
Increase the KMS request quota for the account each month
Batch object uploads into larger files before writing them
Enable S3 Bucket Keys so a short-lived bucket-level key encrypts objects and cuts KMS requests
explain: Enable S3 Bucket Keys so a short-lived bucket-level key encrypts objects and cuts KMS requests. S3 Bucket Keys keep the SSE-KMS security model while generating far fewer KMS requests by caching a bucket-level data key. The main alternatives fail because SSE-S3 changes the key management model the requirements fixed, quota increases do not reduce call volume or cost per call, and batching uploads changes the application's data layout for a platform feature's job.

q: A new Amazon EFS file system for regulated documents must be encrypted under the compliance team's key, and a junior engineer plans to attach the key after creation. What should the architect correct in that plan?
options: EFS encryption and its KMS key are chosen at file system creation and cannot be added later; the file system must be created encrypted with the chosen key
EFS inherits its key from the default EBS key of the account
The key can be added later if the file system is empty
EFS keys can be attached later but only during a maintenance window
explain: EFS encryption and its KMS key are chosen at file system creation and cannot be added later; the file system must be created encrypted with the chosen key. Like several AWS storage services, EFS binds encryption to creation, so the correct key must be specified when the file system is built. The main alternatives fail because no maintenance window or emptiness condition changes the creation-time rule, and EFS does not inherit EBS settings.

q: A media company is replacing TLS 1.0 listeners on its Network Load Balancer after a scan flagged weak protocol support. Which NLB capability enforces the modern protocol floor?
options: Assign a TLS security policy to the listener that sets TLS 1.2 or higher (with TLS 1.3 where the policy supports it) and modern cipher suites
Enable termination protection so listeners cannot be deleted
Add a WAF association to the load balancer to filter old clients
Move the listener to port 443 from port 8443
explain: Assign a TLS security policy to the listener that sets TLS 1.2 or higher (with TLS 1.3 where the policy supports it) and modern cipher suites. Listener security policies define the protocol versions and ciphers a load balancer will negotiate, which is where the TLS floor is enforced. The main alternatives fail because termination protection guards deletion, NLBs do not take WAF associations, and the port number has no bearing on negotiated protocol versions.

q: A CloudFront distribution serves a custom domain from an alternate domain name, and its ACM certificate request keeps failing validation for the distribution's use. Which requirement is the team most likely missing?
options: CloudFront certificates must be wildcard certificates for the apex domain
The certificate must be issued by a private CA for distributions
Certificates used with CloudFront must be requested or imported in the US East (N. Virginia) Region
CloudFront requires certificates with 4096-bit RSA keys only
explain: Certificates used with CloudFront must be requested or imported in the US East (N. Virginia) Region. ACM certificates for CloudFront are a global-use case anchored in us-east-1, regardless of where the content or viewers are. The main alternatives fail because apex wildcards, private issuance, and specific key sizes are not CloudFront requirements; private certificates are not publicly trusted for viewer traffic at all.

q: A regional API Gateway endpoint for a payments API needs its own custom domain with a certificate, and the team requested the certificate in us-east-1 out of habit from CloudFront work. What should they do differently?
options: Request it in the Region closest to the majority of callers
Request the ACM certificate in the same Region as the regional API endpoint
Use a Private CA certificate because the API is regional
Import the certificate into every Region to be safe
explain: Request the ACM certificate in the same Region as the regional API endpoint. Regional endpoints use certificates from their own Region, unlike edge-optimized and CloudFront use cases anchored in us-east-1. The main alternatives fail because caller proximity is irrelevant to certificate placement, importing everywhere adds unmanaged copies, and private certificates are not trusted by external API callers.

q: A company stores its most sensitive archives in AWS Backup and wants vault contents encrypted under a key in the security account with tightly controlled access. Which design provides this?
options: Place the vault in a private subnet so its contents are encrypted
Use the default aws/backup key and add a resource tag for sensitivity
Create the backup vault with a customer managed KMS key and a vault access policy restricting which accounts and roles may use it
Encrypt each backup job's data with a client password before it runs
explain: Create the backup vault with a customer managed KMS key and a vault access policy restricting which accounts and roles may use it. Backup vaults accept customer managed keys and vault access policies, combining controlled encryption with explicit cross-account access governance. The main alternatives fail because the default key's policy is AWS-managed rather than security-account controlled, job passwords are unmanageable at scale, and vaults are a managed resource, not something placed in subnets.

q: Ephemeral build workers need certificates to fetch artifacts over mutual TLS, but issuing year-long certificates to machines that live for an hour is flagged as excessive. Which Private CA mode was designed for this cost and lifetime profile?
options: A public ACM certificate renewed hourly by a Lambda function
One shared worker certificate installed on the golden image
General-purpose mode with 825-day certificates for every worker
Short-lived certificate mode in ACM Private CA, priced and designed for brief-lived certificates
explain: Short-lived certificate mode in ACM Private CA, priced and designed for brief-lived certificates. Private CA's short-lived mode exists for ephemeral workloads, aligning certificate lifetime and cost with machines that exist briefly. The main alternatives fail because long-lived general-purpose issuance recreates the flagged excess, public certificates cannot be reissued hourly in this pattern, and a shared golden-image certificate gives every worker one stealable identity.

q: Two internal services must mutually authenticate before exchanging payment instructions, and both already receive certificates from the company Private CA. Which design completes the mutual authentication requirement?
options: Use one shared client certificate for both services to simplify validation
Have each service send its certificate's public key in an HTTP header
Encrypt the payload with SSE-KMS and skip connection authentication
Configure both services to present their Private CA certificates and validate the peer against the Private CA trust chain (mTLS)
explain: Configure both services to present their Private CA certificates and validate the peer against the Private CA trust chain (mTLS). Mutual TLS with certificates from a common private trust anchor authenticates both endpoints of the connection, not just the server. The main alternatives fail because headers can be spoofed by anyone who copies them, payload encryption does not authenticate the connecting peer, and a shared certificate makes the two services indistinguishable.

q: An SQS queue carrying order events must be encrypted with the platform team's key, and producers in another account report access denied on SendMessage. What is the most likely missing permission?
options: The KMS key policy must allow the producer's principal to use the key (GenerateDataKey/Decrypt as applicable) because SSE-KMS queues require key access from producers and consumers
The producers need an SQS endpoint in their own VPC before sending
SQS queues cannot be shared cross-account when encryption is on
The queue's visibility timeout must be extended for cross-account senders
explain: The KMS key policy must allow the producer's principal to use the key (GenerateDataKey/Decrypt as applicable) because SSE-KMS queues require key access from producers and consumers. With SSE-KMS, sending to and reading from the queue involves the key, so cross-account principals need key permissions in addition to queue permissions. The main alternatives fail because visibility timeout affects message availability timing, endpoints are a network choice rather than the key authorization failure, and encrypted queues do support cross-account use once the key allows it.

q: A Redshift cluster for financial reporting must be encrypted, and the auditors additionally want the cluster's backups protected by the same controlled key. Which configuration satisfies both?
options: Enable TLS between the BI tool and the cluster and call the data encrypted
Export reports to S3 with SSE-KMS and leave the cluster unencrypted
Enable cluster encryption with a customer managed KMS key so the cluster and its automated snapshots are encrypted under that key
Encrypt only the cluster's node storage with a node-level password
explain: Enable cluster encryption with a customer managed KMS key so the cluster and its automated snapshots are encrypted under that key. Redshift encryption with a customer managed key covers the cluster's storage and its snapshots under the customer's controlled key.
