The main alternatives fail because runbook steps are manual and forgettable, denying VPC creation blocks legitimate work without creating the required routes, and findings report the problem after the account is already live.

q: Logs from a acquired company's accounts must join the central archive within a day of their organization invitation being accepted. Which organization-trail property makes this automatic?
options: Each acquired account must create its own trail with the same name
The organization trail and organization log destinations apply to member accounts by virtue of membership, so newly joined accounts are covered without per-account trail creation
CloudTrail event history backfills the archive when accounts join
The archive bucket sends invitations to new accounts to start logging
explain: The organization trail and organization log destinations apply to member accounts by virtue of membership, so newly joined accounts are covered without per-account trail creation. Organization trails cover member accounts as members; coverage follows the organization relationship rather than per-account setup. The main alternatives fail because identically named local trails are a fragile manual imitation, buckets do not invite accounts to log, and event history is a short-term per-account view that does not feed the archive.

q: A governance review must show that every account's Security Hub standards scores trend over time, not just today's snapshot. Which practice produces the trend evidence?
options: Rely on the console's memory of past scores when revisited
Periodically export Security Hub findings and control results (for example to the central S3 archive via custom actions/EventBridge or scheduled API collection) and analyze the time series
Ask account owners to record their scores in a shared document
Screenshot the standards page each quarter from one account
explain: Periodically export Security Hub findings and control results (for example to the central S3 archive via custom actions/EventBridge or scheduled API collection) and analyze the time series. Trends require deliberately persisted snapshots in central storage; the console presents current state, so scheduled export is the evidence mechanism. The main alternatives fail because consoles do not retain a queryable history of scores for this purpose, single-account screenshots miss the organization, and self-recorded scores are unverifiable.

q: A member account's administrator tries to leave the organization to escape its guardrails, and leadership wants this to be impossible without organization-level approval. Which fact reassures leadership?
options: Any member admin can leave instantly and take the account's data with them

Accounts in an organization with all features enabled cannot unilaterally escape SCP governance; leaving requires organization processes and the management account controls the organization's policies and structure
SCPs continue to apply forever even after an account leaves
Leaving is blocked only if the account has an active support plan
explain: Accounts in an organization with all features enabled cannot unilaterally escape SCP governance; leaving requires organization processes and the management account controls the organization's policies and structure. With consolidated organization features, member accounts are governed by the organization and cannot simply discard its policy layer at will. The main alternatives fail because unilateral departure would defeat the governance model, support plans are unrelated to organization membership, and SCPs cease to apply once an account is genuinely outside the organization, which is why departure is controlled.

q: A European insurer must keep policyholder data processed and stored only within EU Regions, including backups and replicas. Which combination enforces residency end to end?
options: Trust each team's deployment checklist to choose EU Regions
Encrypt EU data with a US-held key so location does not matter
Deploy region-pinned stacks in EU Regions, deny other Regions with an SCP using aws:RequestedRegion, and restrict replication and backup copy destinations to EU Regions by policy
Store data in the EU but allow global replication for durability by default
explain: Deploy region-pinned stacks in EU Regions, deny other Regions with an SCP using aws:RequestedRegion, and restrict replication and backup copy destinations to EU Regions by policy. Residency is enforced only when creation, replication, and backup paths are all constrained to the approved Regions by preventive policy. The main alternatives fail because global replication copies data out of the EU by design, checklists are advisory, and key location does not change where the data itself resides.

q: A government customer requires evidence that AWS services handling its data meet SOC 2 and ISO 27001, and asks the company to produce the underlying reports. Where do these compliance reports come from?
options: The customer's own Config rules proving AWS's internal controls
Screenshots of the AWS console's compliance dashboard from sales
The AWS Trust Center marketing pages describing the programs
AWS Artifact, which provides on-demand access to AWS's SOC, ISO, and other compliance reports and agreements
explain: AWS Artifact, which provides on-demand access to AWS's SOC, ISO, and other compliance reports and agreements. Artifact is the official channel for AWS compliance documentation, including auditor reports the customer can review under NDA terms. The main alternatives fail because marketing pages are not the controlled reports, screenshots are not evidence artifacts, and customer-side Config cannot attest to AWS's internal control environment.

q: An AI service used for claims triage must have a complete, reviewable record of its decisions for regulators, including prompts, outputs, and the invoking identity. Which audit design provides this?
options: Keep only the final claim decision in the claims database
Log model names in application logs and sample outputs weekly
Enable Bedrock model invocation logging (prompts and responses) to central log storage together with CloudTrail records of the invoking principals, retained under the compliance retention policy
Rely on the AI vendor's internal logs, available on request
explain: Enable Bedrock model invocation logging (prompts and responses) to central log storage together with CloudTrail records of the invoking principals, retained under the compliance retention policy. Regulator-grade AI audit trails combine invocation content logs with identity-bearing API trails under controlled retention, which the Bedrock and CloudTrail combination provides. The main alternatives fail because decisions without inputs cannot be reviewed for correctness or bias, sampled application logs are incomplete by design, and a vendor's internal logs are outside the company's evidentiary control.

q: A bank's cross-border rule forbids EU customer records from being transferred to its US analytics platform, even in derived or aggregated jobs. Which architecture respects the restriction while still allowing EU analytics?
options: Anonymize records by removing names while keeping account numbers
Let analysts download EU extracts to US laptops for modeling

Run analytics inside the EU Region on EU-resident data and share only approved, non-customer aggregates if policy permits; technical controls block EU data stores from replicating or exporting to US Regions
Copy EU records to the US nightly and delete them after each job
explain: Run analytics inside the EU Region on EU-resident data and share only approved, non-customer aggregates if policy permits; technical controls block EU data stores from replicating or exporting to US Regions. The restriction is about the data's location and movement, so processing must move to the data and egress paths must be technically closed, not procedurally discouraged. The main alternatives fail because nightly copies are transfers regardless of later deletion, partial anonymization leaves regulated identifiers in place, and laptop extracts are uncontrolled transfers.

q: Before launching a new payments workload, the architecture board requires a structured review of what could go wrong, who would attack it, and which controls answer each threat. What is this exercise, and what should it produce?
options: A risk acceptance memo: leadership signing off without analysis
Threat modeling: a structured analysis of assets, trust boundaries, and threats that produces prioritized security controls and design changes before build
A penetration test: hiring testers to attack the running workload after launch
A compliance scan: running Config rules against the finished account
explain: Threat modeling: a structured analysis of assets, trust boundaries, and threats that produces prioritized security controls and design changes before build. Threat modeling is the pre-build discipline that maps threats to controls while design changes are still cheap, producing the control set the board asked for. The main alternatives fail because penetration tests validate a built system, acceptance memos record decisions without the analysis, and configuration scans check deployment state rather than design threats.

q: A risk register lists a threat with high impact but low likelihood and another with moderate impact and high likelihood, and budget covers one mitigation this quarter. Which risk assessment principle should guide the choice?
options: Defer both because only one can be funded
Prioritize by overall risk exposure (likelihood combined with impact and business context), documenting the rationale and any residual risk accepted
Mitigate whichever item the loudest stakeholder prefers
Always mitigate the highest-impact item regardless of likelihood
explain: Prioritize by overall risk exposure (likelihood combined with impact and business context), documenting the rationale and any residual risk accepted. Risk assessment ranks by combined exposure and context so limited budget addresses the greatest expected harm first, with the remainder consciously accepted or scheduled. The main alternatives fail because impact alone ignores probability, stakeholder volume is not analysis, and deferring both wastes the available mitigation budget.

q: A data protection architecture for a health platform must address data in use, in transit, and at rest, plus who can reach each state. Which set of controls represents a complete architecture rather than a single feature?
options: Enabling S3 default encryption and considering the architecture complete
Encryption at rest with customer managed keys, TLS in transit, tokenization or masking for data in use in analytics, and identity/data-perimeter controls governing access to all three states
Backups taken daily so data can be restored after any incident
A WAF in front of the application as the data protection layer
explain: Encryption at rest with customer managed keys, TLS in transit, tokenization or masking for data in use in analytics, and identity/data-perimeter controls governing access to all three states. Data protection is layered across states and access paths; the combined controls address storage, movement, processing exposure, and authorization together. The main alternatives fail because one storage feature leaves transit and use exposed, a WAF filters web attacks rather than protecting data states, and backups address availability, not confidentiality or access control.

q: A multinational must accept the AWS Business Associate Addendum for HIPAA workloads and download its PCI attestation for its own assessors. Which console provides both?
options: The service terms page linked from the AWS homepage footer
The AWS Organizations console's agreements tab for member accounts
A support ticket requesting documents from the account team
AWS Artifact, where agreements such as the BAA are accepted and compliance reports such as PCI documentation are downloaded
explain: AWS Artifact, where agreements such as the BAA are accepted and compliance reports such as PCI documentation are downloaded. Artifact centralizes both agreement acceptance (including the BAA) and compliance report downloads for the organization. The main alternatives fail because Organizations manages accounts rather than compliance agreements, marketing/legal pages do not provide the controlled documents, and support tickets are not the system of record for these artifacts.

q: Audit logs themselves contain sensitive prompt data from an AI workload, creating a compliance problem inside the compliance evidence. Which handling resolves this tension?
options: Apply data protection to the log pipeline: redact or mask sensitive fields before central storage, restrict log access to auditors with a need, and encrypt logs with a controlled key, keeping invocation metadata auditable
Stop logging AI invocations so the problem disappears
Give every engineer log access so nothing is hidden
Store logs in a public bucket so auditors can reach them easily
explain: Apply data protection to the log pipeline: redact or mask sensitive fields before central storage, restrict log access to auditors with a need, and encrypt logs with a controlled key, keeping invocation metadata auditable. The evidence must remain useful without becoming a new sensitive data store, so minimization, restricted access, and encryption are applied to the logs themselves. The main alternatives fail because ending logging destroys the audit requirement, public storage is a breach vector, and broad access multiplies exposure of the sensitive content.

q: A company's data residency register claims EU data stays in the EU, but an S3 cross-Region replication rule quietly copies a bucket to a US Region for durability. Which control would have prevented the silent violation?
options: Encrypting replicated objects with an EU key while copying continues
Renaming the US bucket to include a do-not-use prefix
Replication and destination restrictions in bucket and account policies (and SCP conditions) that permit replication only to approved EU destinations
A quarterly manual review of every bucket's replication settings
explain: Replication and destination restrictions in bucket and account policies (and SCP conditions) that permit replication only to approved EU destinations. Preventive destination restrictions stop noncompliant replication at configuration time rather than discovering it in reviews. The main alternatives fail because manual reviews find violations late, names do not constrain replication, and encryption does not change the residency fact that data now sits in the US.

q: Regulators in a new market require that encryption keys for citizen data be controlled within that market's jurisdiction, separate from the company's global key estate. Which key architecture complies?
options: Keys stored in the global security account in the home Region
Region-local customer managed keys (or an in-Region custom key store) whose policies and administration are restricted to that jurisdiction's accounts and roles
One multi-Region key administered from headquarters for all markets
A single key shared by every market with tag-based separation
explain: Region-local customer managed keys (or an in-Region custom key store) whose policies and administration are restricted to that jurisdiction's accounts and roles. Jurisdictional key control requires the keys and their administration to live in that jurisdiction, which Region-local keys with scoped administration provide. The main alternatives fail because multi-Region and home-Region designs place material or control outside the jurisdiction, and tags on a shared key do not create jurisdictional separation.

q: An assessor asks for evidence of encryption, logging, and access controls across all accounts for the last audit period, in a form they can test rather than admire. Which collection approach produces testable evidence?
options: Export Config aggregator compliance history, CloudTrail logs from the archive, and Security Hub control results for the period into the evidence collection, sourced from the central security accounts
Provide architecture diagrams drawn for the assessment
Ask each team to write a summary of their controls for the period
Invite the assessor to browse the live consoles during the audit week
explain: Export Config aggregator compliance history, CloudTrail logs from the archive, and Security Hub control results for the period into the evidence collection, sourced from the central security accounts. Central aggregators and archives hold the period's actual configuration and activity records, which assessors can sample and re-perform against. The main alternatives fail because live consoles show today rather than the audit period, diagrams show intent, and written summaries are claims without underlying records.

q: A SaaS serving German public-sector clients faces data sovereignty expectations covering not just location but also operational control and protection from foreign legal compulsion as far as architecture can provide. Which architectural choices best support the sovereignty posture?
options: US deployment with a contractual promise to resist foreign requests
EU storage but administration from global admin roles in all Regions

EU-Region deployment with EU-resident customer managed keys, strict SCP region restrictions, and data-perimeter policies limiting access to organization principals, with operational access governed through EU-based roles
Global deployment with data anonymized by removing email addresses
explain: EU-Region deployment with EU-resident customer managed keys, strict SCP region restrictions, and data-perimeter policies limiting access to organization principals, with operational access governed through EU-based roles. Sovereignty postures are built from location, key control, and access perimeter combined; architecture can constrain where data lives, who can reach it, and under whose keys. The main alternatives fail because contracts alone do not change technical exposure, weak anonymization leaves regulated data identifiable, and global administration undermines the operational-control element.

q: A new AI feature's threat model identifies prompt injection leading the model to reveal another tenant's data as the top threat. Which controls from the threat model should be implemented before launch?
options: Tenant-scoped data access enforced outside the model (per-tenant authorization on retrieval), Bedrock Guardrails for content and sensitive information, and invocation logging to detect misuse
Logging only successful purchases so injected sessions blend in
Increasing the model's context window so it confuses tenants less
A stronger system prompt telling the model to keep tenants separate
explain: Tenant-scoped data access enforced outside the model (per-tenant authorization on retrieval), Bedrock Guardrails for content and sensitive information, and invocation logging to detect misuse. Tenant isolation must be enforced by the application's authorization layer and retrieval scoping, with guardrails and logging as supporting controls; the model cannot be its own security boundary. The main alternatives fail because instructions to the model are exactly what injection attacks override, context size does not create isolation, and hiding misuse in sparse logs defeats detection.

q: Backups of a regulated database are copied to a second Region for resilience, until counsel rules the second Region's jurisdiction unacceptable for this data. Which change restores compliance while keeping resilience?
options: Pause new backups until counsel changes their position
Keep the copies but rename the vault to indicate restricted use
Restrict backup copies and vault policies to approved Regions (for example within the same jurisdiction) and delete the noncompliant copies, verifying deletion in the backup audit records
Encrypt the cross-border copies with a stronger key and keep them
explain: Restrict backup copies and vault policies to approved Regions (for example within the same jurisdiction) and delete the noncompliant copies, verifying deletion in the backup audit records. Resilience must be rebuilt inside the jurisdictional boundary, with destination restrictions preventing recurrence and audited deletion closing the existing violation. The main alternatives fail because renaming changes nothing material, stronger encryption does not change where data resides, and pausing backups leaves the existing copies in place while creating an availability gap.

q: A privacy regulation grants customers erasure rights, but the platform's S3 Object Lock retention for transaction records is set to compliance mode for seven years. How should the architect reconcile the conflict?
options: Apply legal and regulatory analysis per data class: Object Lock retention governs records under legal retention duties, while erasable data classes are kept out of compliance-mode lock or use governable retention, with the distinction documented for regulators
Turn off Object Lock for every bucket to simplify erasure
Delete the locked objects using the root account's special deletion right
Ignore erasure requests until the seven years expire for all data
explain: Apply legal and regulatory analysis per data class: Object Lock retention governs records under legal retention duties, while erasable data classes are kept out of compliance-mode lock or use governable retention, with the distinction documented for regulators. Different data classes carry different duties; the architecture must separate retention-bound data from erasable data instead of treating one rule as universal. The main alternatives fail because compliance-mode locks cannot be deleted even by root before expiry, blanket refusal misapplies retention to data it does not cover, and removing all locks sacrifices required tamper protection.

q: A fintech operating in three jurisdictions wants one evidence pack per jurisdiction showing which controls operated where, without mixing data across borders. Which evidence design supports per-jurisdiction packs?
options: Let each jurisdiction's team assemble evidence from memory at audit time
Store all evidence in one Region regardless of its origin jurisdiction
Collect compliance evidence per account/Region grouping aligned to jurisdictions (Config aggregators and archives scoped per jurisdiction) so each pack is drawn from its own boundary
Merge all evidence globally and redact jurisdiction labels afterwards
explain: Collect compliance evidence per account/Region grouping aligned to jurisdictions (Config aggregators and archives scoped per jurisdiction) so each pack is drawn from its own boundary. Evidence architecture must mirror the jurisdictional boundaries it attests to, so scoped collection per jurisdiction is the design that produces clean packs. The main alternatives fail because global merging recreates the mixing problem, memory-based assembly is unverifiable, and single-Region evidence storage can itself violate the residency rules being attested.

q: A workload processes card payments and the team must demonstrate the cardholder data environment is segmented from the general corporate estate. Which architecture evidences segmentation for assessors?
options: Shared accounts with a policy asking staff not to mix workloads

A dedicated account (or OU) for the cardholder environment with SCP restrictions, private networking with no routes to corporate VPCs except inspected paths, and its own logging into the central archive
A separate VLAN naming convention inside the shared corporate VPC
A spreadsheet listing which servers touch card data
explain: A dedicated account (or OU) for the cardholder environment with SCP restrictions, private networking with no routes to corporate VPCs except inspected paths, and its own logging into the central archive. Account-level isolation plus controlled network paths and independent logging is demonstrable segmentation; assessors can test boundaries that actually exist. The main alternatives fail because naming conventions and spreadsheets describe intent without enforcing it, and unenforced requests inside shared accounts are not segmentation.

q: A company expanding to a country with data localization law discovers its global DynamoDB table already replicates user profiles into that country's Region from elsewhere and out again. Which remediation aligns the table design with localization?
options: Encrypt profile fields client-side and continue global replication
Add a warning banner in the app for users in that country
Remove the regulated dataset from the global table pattern: use Region-local tables for that jurisdiction's data with replication disabled across its border
Keep the global table but increase its throughput so transfers are faster
explain: Remove the regulated dataset from the global table pattern: use Region-local tables for that jurisdiction's data with replication disabled across its border. Localization governs where data is stored and moved, so the dataset must exit the cross-border replication design entirely. The main alternatives fail because faster transfers worsen nothing but fix nothing, client-side encryption does not change the data's legal location, and banners inform users without changing the architecture's compliance.

q: An annual risk assessment must cover new AI services whose failure modes (hallucination, data leakage, misuse) differ from traditional workloads. Which assessment update is required?
options: Rate all AI risks as maximum severity to be safe
Exclude AI services from assessment until standards mature

Extend the risk register and threat models to AI-specific threats, map them to the AI controls in use (guardrails, identity, human oversight, invocation logging), and score residual risk for leadership acceptance
Reuse last year's register unchanged since the accounts are the same
explain: Extend the risk register and threat models to AI-specific threats, map them to the AI controls in use (guardrails, identity, human oversight, invocation logging), and score residual risk for leadership acceptance. Risk assessment must evolve with the estate: AI threats get their own analysis and control mapping so residual risk decisions are informed. The main alternatives fail because unchanged registers miss the new threat classes, blanket maximum ratings destroy prioritization, and exclusion leaves the fastest-growing risk area ungoverned.

q: Auditors need read-only access to compliance evidence for two weeks without any ability to change resources or see customer data stores. Which access design fits?
options: Copies of all evidence on USB drives mailed to the audit firm
A time-bound, read-only auditor role scoped to the evidence sources (Artifact, Config aggregator, Security Hub, archive logs) in the security accounts, expiring automatically
The security team's own credentials shared for the engagement
Temporary administrator access so auditors are not blocked by missing permissions
explain: A time-bound, read-only auditor role scoped to the evidence sources (Artifact, Config aggregator, Security Hub, archive logs) in the security accounts, expiring automatically. Scoped, expiring, read-only access gives assessors what they need to test while preserving least privilege and attribution. The main alternatives fail because administrator access overshoots the need and endangers the estate, removable media leaves evidentiary control, and shared credentials destroy accountability.

q: A data lake centralizes every Region's raw customer events for analytics, and a new residency ruling makes that centralization unlawful for one Region's data. Which redesign keeps analytics lawful?
options: Compress the restricted data before centralizing it so it counts as different data
Centralize it anyway and note the ruling in the risk register
Federate the analytics: process the restricted Region's data in-Region and centralize only the derived, approved outputs, with the raw store's replication and ingestion paths to other Regions closed
Move the central lake to the restricted Region and pull all other Regions' data there instead
explain: Federate the analytics: process the restricted Region's data in-Region and centralize only the derived, approved outputs, with the raw store's replication and ingestion paths to other Regions closed. When raw data cannot move, computation must move to the data and only lawful derivatives may travel, enforced by closing the raw paths. The main alternatives fail because compression changes size, not legal status, knowingly centralizing violates the ruling regardless of register notes, and reversing the flow exports every other Region's data into the restricted jurisdiction.

q: A threat modeling workshop for a public API lists an unauthenticated endpoint that reveals whether an email is registered, enabling account enumeration. Which outcome should the workshop produce for this finding?
options: Acceptance of the risk because enumeration is not a breach
A plan to hide the endpoint URL from the public documentation
A design change before launch: make responses indistinguishable and rate-limit the endpoint, recorded as a threat with its mitigation in the model
A note to monitor the endpoint after launch and decide then
explain: A design change before launch: make responses indistinguishable and rate-limit the endpoint, recorded as a threat with its mitigation in the model. Threat modeling exists to change design before build; enumeration is mitigated by indistinguishable responses and throttling, and the decision belongs in the model. The main alternatives fail because post-launch monitoring accepts an avoidable design flaw, dismissing enumeration ignores its role in credential attacks, and obscurity does not protect a public endpoint.

q: A regulated workload's evidence includes AI invocation logs that must be retained for five years in the same jurisdiction as the workload. Which storage decision satisfies the retention and residency together?
options: Store logs in the cheapest Region globally with five-year lifecycle
Retain logs for one year centrally and summarize them for the remaining four
Store invocation logs in the workload's Region in the central archive account structure with a five-year retention (lifecycle plus Object Lock as required), under a Region-local key
Keep logs for five years in each developer's local environment
explain: Store invocation logs in the workload's Region in the central archive account structure with a five-year retention (lifecycle plus Object Lock as required), under a Region-local key. Retention period and storage jurisdiction are independent requirements that must both be met by the log destination's Region and lifecycle design. The main alternatives fail because cheapest-Region storage breaks residency, developer-local retention is uncontrolled and loss-prone, and summaries are not the retained logs the rule requires.

q: A company subject to financial reporting rules must show its cloud control changes themselves are governed: who changed an SCP, when, and under what approval. Which records provide this control-over-controls evidence?
options: The current SCP documents, which show the end state only
The AWS console's recent-items list in the management account
CloudTrail organization records of Organizations API calls (policy changes) from the management account, retained in the tamper-resistant archive, correlated with change tickets
Engineers' recollections captured in the annual review meeting
explain: CloudTrail organization records of Organizations API calls (policy changes) from the management account, retained in the tamper-resistant archive, correlated with change tickets. Changes to governance policies are API events; their CloudTrail record in the archive is the auditable history assessors can test against approvals. The main alternatives fail because current-state documents cannot show who changed what or when, recollections are not records, and console convenience lists are not retained evidence.

q: A children's education app faces heightened data protection duties and asks which architecture choices demonstrate data minimization by design. Which set best demonstrates minimization?
options: Collect every attribute available in case features need it later
Retain all data indefinitely in case regulators ask about it
Give all staff access so any question can be answered quickly
Collect only the attributes the features need, set short retention with automatic deletion, restrict access by ABAC to staff roles with a need, and log access to the remaining data
explain: Collect only the attributes the features need, set short retention with automatic deletion, restrict access by ABAC to staff roles with a need, and log access to the remaining data. Minimization means the architecture holds less data, for less time, reachable by fewer people, with accountability for the access that remains. The main alternatives fail because speculative collection, indefinite retention, and broad access are the three patterns minimization exists to prevent.

q: An enterprise must prove to a regulator that customer data cannot be read by AWS operators as a routine matter and that access by any party is governed. Which honest architectural answer should be given?
options: Guarantee that no AWS employee could ever access any data under any circumstance
State that encryption with S3-managed keys removes all operator access concerns
Claim the data is safe because the buckets are not public

Explain the layered controls that constrain access: encryption with customer managed keys and their policies, data-perimeter conditions, and CloudTrail visibility of key usage, noting these govern and evidence access rather than claiming absolute impossibility
explain: Explain the layered controls that constrain access: encryption with customer managed keys and their policies, data-perimeter conditions, and CloudTrail visibility of key usage, noting these govern and evidence access rather than claiming absolute impossibility. Accurate sovereignty answers describe enforceable customer-side controls and auditability without overclaiming; key control and usage logging are the substantive mechanisms. The main alternatives fail because absolute guarantees are not supportable for any cloud service, non-public buckets say nothing about operator access paths, and S3-managed keys place key control with the provider rather than the customer.

q: A migration plan moves a regulated workload to AWS, and compliance requires the risk assessment to be completed and accepted before any production data moves. Which sequencing demonstrates governance in the migration plan?
options: Gate the data migration phase on the completed threat model, risk register, and control implementation evidence, with sign-off recorded before cutover
Run the assessment in parallel and file it whenever it finishes
Skip assessment for migrated workloads since they were compliant on-premises
Migrate data first and assess risk once the workload stabilizes
explain: Gate the data migration phase on the completed threat model, risk register, and control implementation evidence, with sign-off recorded before cutover. Governance gates work only if the risky step cannot proceed before the assessment that authorizes it, which the phase gate enforces. The main alternatives fail because assessing after data moves or in untracked parallel removes the gate's protection, and on-premises compliance does not transfer automatically to a new architecture.

q: A global retailer must restrict transfers of support tickets containing EU customer details to its support platform hosted outside the EU. Which design keeps support working within transfer restrictions?
options: Route EU tickets to the global platform over TLS and rely on encryption in transit
Ask EU customers to consent to transfer in the ticket form and proceed globally
Translate tickets into English before transfer so they are transformed data
Deploy the support workload for EU customers in the EU with EU-resident data storage, and mask or tokenize customer details before any cross-border escalation workflow
explain: Deploy the support workload for EU customers in the EU with EU-resident data storage, and mask or tokenize customer details before any cross-border escalation workflow. Transfer restrictions govern the data's destination, so the processing and storage for EU tickets must stay in-boundary, with minimization applied to anything that must cross. The main alternatives fail because TLS protects the journey, not the destination's legality, blanket consent in a form does not substitute for architecture where restrictions apply, and translation does not change the data's regulated content.

q: An assessor challenges whether the company's audit trail would catch a privileged user exporting a regulated dataset to an external account. Which trail and detection combination answers the challenge?
options: CloudTrail data-event logging for the data stores plus Access Analyzer external access findings and GuardDuty/CloudTrail-based alerting on cross-account sharing and bulk reads, all retained centrally
A policy statement in the employee handbook prohibiting exports
Quarterly reviews of the dataset's bucket policy by its owner
The dataset's access logs retained in the owning account for 30 days
explain: CloudTrail data-event logging for the data stores plus Access Analyzer external access findings and GuardDuty/CloudTrail-based alerting on cross-account sharing and bulk reads, all retained centrally. Answering the challenge requires both the record (data events in central retention) and active detection of the sharing and exfiltration patterns, not policy statements or short local logs. The main alternatives fail because 30-day local logs under the suspect's own account control can be erased or expire, handbook rules do not detect anything, and owner self-review is the conflict of interest the assessor is probing.

q: A company's Artifact downloads and agreements are scattered across individual accounts, and a new group-level audit cannot establish which entity accepted which agreement. Which Artifact organization practice fixes this?
options: Manage Artifact at the organization level so agreements are accepted for the organization and reports are accessed consistently, with records of acceptance retained as evidence
Store agreement PDFs in a shared drive folder named by year
Ask AWS account managers to confirm agreements by email
Let each account admin download whichever reports they prefer
explain: Manage Artifact at the organization level so agreements are accepted for the organization and reports are accessed consistently, with records of acceptance retained as evidence. Artifact supports organization-level management of agreements and reports, giving one authoritative record of what the organization accepted and accessed. The main alternatives fail because per-account scatter is the problem being fixed, shared-drive copies lose provenance and currency, and email confirmations are not the system of record.

q: A threat model for a new file-sharing feature ranks threats, and the board asks which single output most improves the build phase. Which output should the architect highlight?
options: The meeting attendance record showing the workshop happened
The list of every theoretical threat regardless of applicability
The prioritized threat-to-control mapping that turns each significant threat into concrete design requirements and backlog items for the build
The final risk score averaged across all threats
explain: The prioritized threat-to-control mapping that turns each significant threat into concrete design requirements and backlog items for the build. Threat modeling pays off when its prioritized mappings change what gets built; that mapping is the artifact engineering consumes. The main alternatives fail because unprioritized lists and attendance records document activity without directing work, and an average score hides the specific threats that need controls.

q: A workload in scope for a strict regulator must use only services covered by the regulator's recognized compliance program, and a team proposes a newly launched AWS service. Which verification step must come first?
options: Ask the service team informally whether they feel compliant
Check the service's compliance scope (for example via AWS Artifact and the compliance program's in-scope services list) before designing it into the regulated workload
Assume all AWS services share the same compliance status
Deploy the service and add it to the evidence pack afterwards
explain: Check the service's compliance scope (for example via AWS Artifact and the compliance program's in-scope services list) before designing it into the regulated workload. Regulated designs may only include in-scope services, so scope verification precedes adoption; a service outside scope cannot be cured by good configuration. The main alternatives fail because deploying first creates a finding that must be undone, compliance scope varies by service and program, and informal assurances are not evidence.

q: Data protection for a research platform must let analysts work with trends in patient outcomes without exposing individual patient records. Which technique serves this purpose?
options: Giving analysts read access to the clinical database with a warning banner

De-identification of the analytical dataset (removing or tokenizing direct identifiers and generalizing quasi-identifiers) before analysts receive access, with the identified data kept in the restricted clinical zone
Copying records to spreadsheets with patient names hidden in white text
Encrypting the clinical database and giving every analyst the key
explain: De-identification of the analytical dataset (removing or tokenizing direct identifiers and generalizing quasi-identifiers) before analysts receive access, with the identified data kept in the restricted clinical zone. De-identification transforms the data analysts receive so the analysis proceeds without individual exposure, while identified data stays behind its boundary. The main alternatives fail because warned direct access leaves records exposed, hidden spreadsheet text is still present data, and universal key distribution makes encryption meaningless as an access control.

q: A sovereignty review requires proof that backups, logs, and replicas of a citizen database have never left the home Region, not just that the primary is resident. Which evidence set proves the negative as far as architecture allows?
options: Configuration evidence (Config aggregator records showing replication and backup destinations), SCP region restrictions in force for the period, and CloudTrail records of copy operations, all from the central archive
The database console's current Region displayed in a screenshot
A signed statement from the lead engineer that copies were never made
A list of Regions where the company has no accounts
explain: Configuration evidence (Config aggregator records showing replication and backup destinations), SCP region restrictions in force for the period, and CloudTrail records of copy operations, all from the central archive. Proving a negative rests on showing the controls that constrained destinations and the records of the operations that could have moved data, across the whole secondary-data surface. The main alternatives fail because personal statements and screenshots are unverifiable point-in-time claims, and having no accounts elsewhere does not by itself govern service-level replication destinations.

q: A customer-facing Bedrock chatbot must refuse hateful, violent, and sexual content in both user prompts and model replies, with stricter limits than its internal drafting assistant needs. Which Bedrock Guardrails configuration delivers this?
options: Write a longer system prompt asking the chatbot model to behave
Filter the chatbot's output with regular expressions maintained by the web team

Create a guardrail with content filters set to the required strengths for the chatbot's categories and apply it to the chatbot's model invocations, with a separate, looser guardrail for the internal assistant
Use the internal assistant's single guardrail for both applications
explain: Create a guardrail with content filters set to the required strengths for the chatbot's categories and apply it to the chatbot's model invocations, with a separate, looser guardrail for the internal assistant. Guardrails content filters are the managed, per-application control for blocking harmful categories in inputs and outputs at configurable strengths. The main alternatives fail because system prompts are advisory to the model and bypassable, hand-rolled regex misses paraphrased harmful content, and one shared guardrail cannot express two different strictness levels.

q: A financial advice application must never discuss cryptocurrency trading, steering users back to regulated topics the firm is licensed for. Which guardrail feature enforces this topic boundary?
options: A disclaimer appended to every response about licensing
Denied topics in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, defining cryptocurrency trading so prompts and responses on it are blocked
A word filter containing the single word crypto
Content filters raised to maximum on every category
explain: Denied topics in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, defining cryptocurrency trading so prompts and responses on it are blocked. Denied topics let the application define subjects outside its scope semantically, so varied phrasings of the topic are caught. The main alternatives fail because maximum content filters target harm categories, not business topics, a one-word filter is trivially evaded by synonyms, and disclaimers do not prevent the advice from being given.

q: A support chatbot occasionally echoes customers' email addresses and order numbers into other users' sessions through model responses, and policy requires such data never to appear in outputs. Which guardrail capability addresses this?
options: Asking users not to type personal information into the chat
Storing PII in a separate database the model cannot name
Sensitive information filters in Bedrock Guardrails that detect and block or mask PII in inputs and outputs
Shortening the model's responses so PII is less likely to fit
explain: Sensitive information filters in Bedrock Guardrails that detect and block or mask PII in inputs and outputs. Guardrails' sensitive information filters are built to detect PII types and block or anonymize them in the conversation stream. The main alternatives fail because brevity does not remove PII that does appear, storage separation does not stop the model repeating what users provide, and user instructions do not control model outputs to other sessions.

q: A retrieval-augmented assistant answering from company manuals sometimes invents procedures that are not in any manual, creating safety risk. Which guardrail check targets this hallucination pattern?
options: Profanity word filters applied to the responses
Raising the content filter for violence to its maximum
Denied topics covering every procedure not in the manuals
Contextual grounding checks in Bedrock Guardrails, which score responses against the retrieved source and block answers below the grounding threshold
explain: Contextual grounding checks in Bedrock Guardrails, which score responses against the retrieved source and block answers below the grounding threshold. Contextual grounding specifically evaluates whether responses are supported by the provided source material, which is the hallucination failure described. The main alternatives fail because denied topics cannot enumerate every unlisted procedure, and profanity or violence filters judge tone and harm categories, not factual support.

q: A school-facing writing assistant must block profanity and a custom list of slurs that generic filters miss. Which guardrail feature holds the custom list?
options: Denied topics named profanity with a paragraph of examples
The model's safety training, refreshed nightly by the school
Word filters in Bedrock Guardrails, including custom word and phrase lists managed by the application owner
A client-side JavaScript list that hides bad words after display
explain: Word filters in Bedrock Guardrails, including custom word and phrase lists managed by the application owner. Guardrails word filters support custom lists alongside managed profanity filtering, enforced at the model boundary rather than in the browser. The main alternatives fail because denied topics are semantic subject areas rather than exact word lists, model training is not owner-editable nightly, and client-side hiding still transmits the content and can be bypassed.

q: An AI agent books travel and accesses the user's calendar and payment tools; it must act only with the authority the specific user delegated, never with a shared super-identity. Which AgentCore capability provides this delegated identity?
options: Letting the agent present itself as an administrator to tool APIs
A single IAM role for the agent with permissions to every user's resources
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity, managing workload and user-delegated identities and credentials so the agent acts on behalf of each user with their scoped authorization
Storing each user's password in the agent's memory for sign-ins
explain: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity, managing workload and user-delegated identities and credentials so the agent acts on behalf of each user with their scoped authorization. AgentCore Identity exists to give agents governed identities, including on-behalf-of-user delegation with scoped, managed credentials. The main alternatives fail because a shared super-role and stored user passwords both destroy per-user authorization and attribution, and impersonating administrators is the opposite of delegated scoping.

q: An agentic workflow can refund orders automatically up to a small limit, but any refund above that limit must be approved by a human before money moves. Which design implements the approval gate?
options: A Step Functions state machine using a wait-for-callback (task token) approval step: the agent's refund action pauses above the limit until a human approves or rejects in the approval interface
The agent emails a manager and proceeds if no reply arrives in an hour
The model is prompted to ask itself whether the refund seems reasonable
Refunds above the limit are logged more verbosely but still automatic
explain: A Step Functions state machine using a wait-for-callback (task token) approval step: the agent's refund action pauses above the limit until a human approves or rejects in the approval interface. Step Functions' human approval pattern (pause with a task token, resume on external decision) is the governed way to insert a person into an automated flow before an irreversible action. The main alternatives fail because silence-as-consent and self-review provide no human decision, and verbose logging records an unapproved action rather than gating it.

q: A content generation pipeline drafts social posts with a model, but brand policy requires a human editor's approval before anything is published. Which orchestration pattern enforces the policy?
options: The model rates its own drafts and publishes the confident ones
A Lambda publishes immediately and tags posts for later review
Step Functions orchestrating generation, then a human approval step (task token with notification to editors) that must return approval before the publish step runs
Editors review posts weekly and delete any that should not have run
explain: Step Functions orchestrating generation, then a human approval step (task token with notification to editors) that must return approval before the publish step runs. Placing a callback approval state between generation and publication in the state machine makes human sign-off a structural prerequisite, not a cleanup step. The main alternatives fail because self-rating keeps humans out of the gate, and post-publication review accepts that unapproved content already reached the audience.

q: A Bedrock agent for employees must not retrieve documents from the executive knowledge base even when an employee crafts a prompt asking for them. Which layered control actually prevents the retrieval?
options: Hiding the executive knowledge base's name from the agent's description
A guardrail denied topic named executive documents as the only control

Access control enforced at the data and identity layer (the agent's identity and permissions exclude the executive source, with AgentCore Identity governing the agent's credentials), supported by guardrails on outputs
A system prompt instructing the agent to keep executive content secret
explain: Access control enforced at the data and identity layer (the agent's identity and permissions exclude the executive source, with AgentCore Identity governing the agent's credentials), supported by guardrails on outputs. Authorization on what the agent's identity can reach is the enforceable boundary; output filtering and instructions are supporting layers, not substitutes. The main alternatives fail because a denied topic alone can be evaded by paraphrase and does not govern retrieval permissions, instructions yield to injected prompts, and obscurity collapses on first discovery.

q: A healthcare triage assistant must mask patient identifiers in its logs while still blocking outright any response that would expose another patient's record. Which guardrail distinction should the design use?
options: Turn off sensitive information filters to avoid false positives
Configure PII handling per context: anonymize/mask where redacted content may pass (such as logging and benign echoes), and block where exposure must never occur (cross-patient disclosures)
Block every message containing any identifier, including the patient's own
Mask nothing and rely on access controls for the log bucket alone
explain: Configure PII handling per context: anonymize/mask where redacted content may pass (such as logging and benign echoes), and block where exposure must never occur (cross-patient disclosures). Guardrails let PII actions differ by need, masking for legitimate flows and blocking for prohibited disclosures, which matches the two different risks described. The main alternatives fail because blocking a patient's own identifiers breaks legitimate use, bucket controls do not stop the model emitting data to the wrong user, and disabling filters removes both protections.

q: An agent platform team needs agents to call third-party SaaS tools (CRM, ticketing) using each customer's own OAuth grant, stored and refreshed centrally rather than pasted into prompts. Which AgentCore Identity function serves this?
options: AgentCore Identity's credential/token vaulting for outbound authentication, storing and brokering OAuth tokens so agents call third-party APIs on behalf of the delegating user or workload
The agent's IAM role, which the SaaS tools are expected to trust
Users pasting their SaaS passwords into the chat when asked
Long-lived API keys for the SaaS tools shared by all agents
explain: AgentCore Identity's credential/token vaulting for outbound authentication, storing and brokering OAuth tokens so agents call third-party APIs on behalf of the delegating user or workload. Outbound identity brokering is AgentCore Identity's role: it holds delegated OAuth credentials and presents them to tools without exposing them to the model or prompts. The main alternatives fail because shared keys erase per-customer delegation, passwords in chat are a credential-handling failure, and SaaS tools outside AWS do not evaluate IAM roles.

q: A loan-processing agent prepares a recommendation, but regulations require a licensed human to make and record the final decision on every application. Which workflow design satisfies the regulator?
options: The agent decides, and a human samples ten percent of decisions monthly
The agent decides low-value loans and humans decide the rest
A human is notified of each decision by email after funds move
Step Functions routes every application to a human decision step after the agent's recommendation, with the human's decision and identity recorded before any downstream action proceeds
explain: Step Functions routes every application to a human decision step after the agent's recommendation, with the human's decision and identity recorded before any downstream action proceeds. A mandatory human decision state on every application makes the licensed judgment a structural step with an attributable record, which sampling and after-the-fact notice do not. The main alternatives fail because sampling leaves most decisions unmade by a human, value thresholds contradict the every-application requirement, and notification after action is information, not decision-making.

q: Guardrail interventions on a public chatbot spike every evening, and the team cannot tell whether attacks or a misconfigured filter are responsible. Which observability should they add first?
options: Increasing all filter strengths until the spikes stop
A nightly export of all chat transcripts for manual reading
CloudWatch metrics and logs for guardrail activity (invocation and intervention counts by filter type) with alarms and a dashboard distinguishing intervention categories
Disabling the guardrail during evening hours to compare traffic
explain: CloudWatch metrics and logs for guardrail activity (invocation and intervention counts by filter type) with alarms and a dashboard distinguishing intervention categories. Guardrail usage emits metrics that show which filters intervene and how often, letting the team separate attack patterns from over-broad configuration. The main alternatives fail because manual transcript review does not scale to diagnosis, blindly raising strengths worsens false positives, and disabling the control removes protection to gather data the metrics already provide.

q: Different products need different guardrail strictness: a children's storyteller must be far stricter than an adult fiction editor using the same foundation model. Which guardrail practice supports both?
options: Let users select their preferred strictness in settings
Prompt each product's model with its target audience and trust the model
One global guardrail set to the children's strictness for every product
Maintain separate versioned guardrails per application with their own filter strengths and apply each to its application's invocations
explain: Maintain separate versioned guardrails per application with their own filter strengths and apply each to its application's invocations. Guardrails are reusable, versioned resources applied per invocation, so each application can enforce its own policy on a shared model. The main alternatives fail because children's strictness everywhere would cripple the adult product, audience prompts are not enforcement, and user-selected safety settings surrender the policy to the user.

q: An autonomous remediation agent proposes infrastructure changes; low-risk changes may auto-apply, but production network changes require an engineer's explicit approval with a timeout and escalation. Which Step Functions features implement the approval policy?
options: The agent's own risk score stored in DynamoDB as its approval record
An SNS message to the team channel that the agent treats as approval if reacted to
A callback task token step that notifies the on-call engineer, waits for approve/reject, and uses the state's timeout/heartbeat and catch/escalation path when no decision arrives in time
A Lambda that sleeps for thirty minutes and then applies the change
explain: A callback task token step that notifies the on-call engineer, waits for approve/reject, and uses the state's timeout/heartbeat and catch/escalation path when no decision arrives in time. Step Functions approval steps natively support waiting on an external decision with timeouts and alternate paths, which is the timeout-and-escalation behavior required. The main alternatives fail because sleeping then proceeding is timed consent, not approval, chat reactions are not an auditable authorization mechanism, and self-scored risk is the agent approving itself.

q: A prompt injection campaign tries to get a shopping assistant to reveal its system instructions and internal tool parameters. Which combination best defends the assistant?
options: Publishing the system prompt so there is nothing left to steal
Giving the assistant administrator tool access so injections find nothing restricted

Bedrock Guardrails content and sensitive-information filtering on inputs and outputs, least-privilege tool access through the agent's governed identity, and treating model output as untrusted before tool execution
Removing all tools from the assistant permanently
explain: Bedrock Guardrails content and sensitive-information filtering on inputs and outputs, least-privilege tool access through the agent's governed identity, and treating model output as untrusted before tool execution. Defense in depth assumes some injected text reaches the model, so filtering, scoped tool identity, and output validation together limit what an injection can achieve. The main alternatives fail because publishing internals aids attackers crafting bypasses, administrator access makes a successful injection catastrophic, and removing all tools destroys the product rather than securing it.

q: A multi-tenant agent platform must guarantee one tenant's agent sessions can never present another tenant's delegated tokens to tools. Which AgentCore Identity practice provides the isolation?
options: Keep all tenants' tokens in one vault entry the agents share for simplicity
Bind delegated credentials to the authenticated user/tenant context per session through AgentCore Identity, issuing and presenting tokens only for that session's principal
Let agents request any token by naming a tenant in plain language
Embed tenant tokens in the agent's system prompt at deployment
explain: Bind delegated credentials to the authenticated user/tenant context per session through AgentCore Identity, issuing and presenting tokens only for that session's principal. Identity brokering must be principal-bound per session; tokens are vended for the session's authenticated principal, never selected by the model's say-so. The main alternatives fail because shared vault entries and prompt-embedded tokens erase tenant boundaries, and language-selected tokens let prompt injection choose whose authority to wield.

q: Before a stricter guardrail version goes live for a banking assistant, the team must check it does not block legitimate account-service conversations. Which rollout practice should they follow?
options: Test the new guardrail version against representative legitimate and harmful traffic, deploy it as a new version to a limited scope, and monitor intervention metrics before full rollout
Test only with harmful examples since blocking is the goal
Delete the old guardrail so only the strict one exists
Replace the production guardrail in place during peak hours
explain: Test the new guardrail version against representative legitimate and harmful traffic, deploy it as a new version to a limited scope, and monitor intervention metrics before full rollout. Versioned guardrails allow staged, measurable rollout; testing both false positives and true positives protects the legitimate service the bank must keep running. The main alternatives fail because in-place peak changes and deleting the fallback remove recovery options, and harmful-only testing cannot reveal over-blocking of real customers.

q: An agent invokes a Lambda tool that writes to a database; auditors want the record to show both the agent and the human on whose behalf it acted. Which identity design produces that record?
options: Have users type their employee ID into the prompt for the agent to quote
Propagate the delegated user identity through AgentCore Identity to the tool invocation and log both the agent workload identity and the delegated principal in the tool's audit entries
Log only the Lambda function's execution role for all invocations
Disable tool logging because agent actions are covered by model logs
explain: Propagate the delegated user identity through AgentCore Identity to the tool invocation and log both the agent workload identity and the delegated principal in the tool's audit entries. Dual attribution requires the identity layer to carry the on-behalf-of context into tool calls and the tools to record both identities. The main alternatives fail because the execution role alone attributes everything to the tool itself, self-typed IDs are unverified, and model invocation logs do not capture tool-side effects.

q: A children's educational agent must apply guardrails not only to final answers but also to streamed partial responses, so disallowed content never flashes on screen. Which invocation approach is required?
options: Stream freely and rely on the final message being compliant
Invoke the model with guardrails applied in streaming mode (ApplyGuardrail / streaming guardrail configuration) so chunks are evaluated as they stream
Apply guardrails only to the user's input stream
Buffer the full response on the client and filter it after completion
explain: Invoke the model with guardrails applied in streaming mode (ApplyGuardrail / streaming guardrail configuration) so chunks are evaluated as they stream. Streaming guardrail application evaluates output incrementally, which is the only way to prevent partial disallowed content from being displayed. The main alternatives fail because client buffering after receipt still exposes timing and implementation gaps and is not the service's enforcement point, unfiltered streaming is the failure described, and input-only filtering ignores model-generated content.

q: A guardrail must stop a mental-health support bot from providing crisis counseling beyond its scope while still allowing supportive general conversation and crisis-line referrals. Which configuration expresses this nuance?
options: A denied topic defining clinical crisis counseling as out of scope, paired with an approved response pattern that provides supportive redirection and crisis resources, with content filters tuned for self-harm categories
Block every conversation containing emotional language
Let the model decide case by case with no topic configuration
Disable the bot entirely to eliminate the risk
explain: A denied topic defining clinical crisis counseling as out of scope, paired with an approved response pattern that provides supportive redirection and crisis resources, with content filters tuned for self-harm categories. Denied topics with a designed fallback response let the application refuse the regulated activity while still delivering the safe, helpful behavior required. The main alternatives fail because blocking all emotional conversation destroys the service's purpose, unconfigured model judgment is inconsistent for a safety boundary, and shutdown avoids rather than manages the responsibility.

q: An enterprise wants one accountable view of its AI controls: which guardrails are active on which applications, and where human approvals gate agent actions. Which inventory practice creates this view?
options: Wait for an incident to reveal which controls exist

Maintain a central register (built from the guardrail configurations and versions associated with each application, and the Step Functions approval steps in agent workflows) reviewed as part of AI governance
Ask each product team to describe their AI controls in slide decks
Infer controls from model names in billing reports
explain: Maintain a central register (built from the guardrail configurations and versions associated with each application, and the Step Functions approval steps in agent workflows) reviewed as part of AI governance. AI governance needs an explicit inventory tying each application to its guardrail versions and approval gates, assembled from the actual configurations. The main alternatives fail because slide descriptions drift from reality, billing shows usage not controls, and incident-driven discovery learns the inventory at the worst possible time.

q: A retail agent can browse the product catalog freely but must get human approval before issuing any coupon above a threshold, and the approval must survive agent restarts. Why is Step Functions the right home for this approval rather than logic inside the agent?
options: Agents cannot send notifications, so only Step Functions can email approvers
Step Functions makes the model itself more accurate at judging coupons
The state machine persists the waiting state durably (task token held in the execution) independent of the agent process, so approvals survive restarts and are recorded in execution history
The approval is legally valid only if a state machine records it
explain: The state machine persists the waiting state durably (task token held in the execution) independent of the agent process, so approvals survive restarts and are recorded in execution history. Durability and auditability come from the orchestrator holding the pending approval as managed state with an execution record, rather than volatile in-agent memory. The main alternatives fail because orchestration does not change model accuracy, agents can notify through other means, and legal validity comes from the recorded human decision, not the brand of tool holding it.

q: A guardrail blocks a legitimate chemistry lesson for a tutoring product because its filters treat instructional content like instructions for wrongdoing. Which tuning response is appropriate?
options: Adjust the guardrail configuration for this application (filter strengths and topic definitions scoped to illicit synthesis rather than general chemistry) and retest with curriculum samples, keeping stricter guardrails on general-audience products
Raise every filter to maximum so the behavior is at least consistent
Tell students to phrase questions to evade the filters
Remove guardrails from the tutoring product entirely
explain: Adjust the guardrail configuration for this application (filter strengths and topic definitions scoped to illicit synthesis rather than general chemistry) and retest with curriculum samples, keeping stricter guardrails on general-audience products. Guardrails are per-application and tunable; the fix is scoping the policy to the actual harm for this audience and validating against real curriculum content. The main alternatives fail because removing protection overcorrects a tuning issue, teaching evasion undermines the control's purpose, and maximal filters would block even more legitimate instruction.

q: An agent with AgentCore Identity must authenticate users arriving from the company's existing OIDC provider before any delegated actions occur. Which identity flow does this describe, and what must be configured?
options: The agent issuing its own usernames and passwords to employees
Anonymous access with identity asserted in the first chat message
Outbound authentication: the agent presenting its own credentials to the IdP
Inbound authentication: configure AgentCore Identity to trust the company's OIDC IdP so the agent receives verified user identity before acting on their behalf
explain: Inbound authentication: configure AgentCore Identity to trust the company's OIDC IdP so the agent receives verified user identity before acting on their behalf. Inbound identity is about verifying who is calling the agent; trusting the enterprise OIDC provider makes the agent rely on verified assertions rather than self-claims. The main alternatives fail because outbound authentication concerns the agent calling other systems, self-issued employee credentials recreate a directory the IdP already provides, and chat-asserted identity is unverified by definition.

q: A company runs a steady-state fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in one Region and one instance family for the next three years and wants the deepest discount while accepting a family-specific commitment. Which purchase option best meets this requirement?
options: On-Demand Capacity Reservations with no term commitment
Compute Savings Plans with a one-year commitment and no family restriction
EC2 Instance Savings Plans with a three-year commitment to the chosen family and Region
Spot Instances with a maximum price set to the On-Demand price
explain: EC2 Instance Savings Plans give the largest discount in exchange for committing to a specific instance family in a specific Region for one or three years. Compute Savings Plans are more flexible across families and services but discount less for that same commitment, Spot pricing suits interruptible work rather than steady state, and Capacity Reservations alone provide capacity, not a billing discount.

q: A startup uses Amazon EC2, AWS Fargate, and AWS Lambda in varying proportions each quarter and wants one commitment discount that follows the workload as it shifts between those services. Which option should the architect recommend?
options: EC2 Instance Savings Plans locked to a single instance family
Compute Savings Plans, which apply automatically across EC2, Fargate, and Lambda usage
Zonal Reserved Instances purchased in each Availability Zone
Standard Reserved Instances purchased for each EC2 instance size
explain: Compute Savings Plans apply to EC2, Fargate, and Lambda and automatically follow changes in family, size, Region, and compute service, which fits a shifting mix. Reserved Instances and EC2 Instance Savings Plans are narrower, and Zonal Reserved Instances only add a capacity reservation for EC2 in one Availability Zone.

q: A video-transcoding farm can be interrupted and restarted from checkpoints, and its jobs have flexible completion windows of several hours. Which EC2 purchase option will minimize cost for this workload?
options: Three-year All Upfront Standard Reserved Instances
On-Demand Instances with a Dedicated Host tenancy
EC2 Instance Savings Plans with a three-year term
Spot Instances, using diverse instance types across multiple Availability Zones
explain: Spot Instances offer the deepest discounts on spare capacity and are designed for fault-tolerant, checkpointable, flexible workloads, especially when diversified across types and Availability Zones. Reserved capacity and Savings Plans pay for a commitment this sporadic workload does not need, and Dedicated Hosts add cost.

q: A regulated workload must run on specific EC2 instance types in a specific Availability Zone, and the team also needs assurance that capacity will be available during a disaster-recovery drill. Which purchase option provides the capacity assurance the team needs?
options: Zonal Reserved Instances or On-Demand Capacity Reservations scoped to that Availability Zone
Compute Savings Plans, which reserve capacity wherever usage occurs
Savings Plans for Amazon SageMaker AI with a three-year term
Spot Instances requested with a persistent request type
explain: Only Zonal Reserved Instances and On-Demand Capacity Reservations reserve capacity in a named Availability Zone. Savings Plans are billing discounts and never reserve capacity, and Spot capacity is explicitly not assured.

q: An engineering team over-provisioned its Amazon EC2 instances a year ago and now wants data-driven recommendations for smaller instance sizes that still meet performance needs. Which tool should the team use first?
options: Amazon CloudWatch alarms on CPU utilization alone
AWS Cost Explorer, filtered by service and usage type
AWS Trusted Advisor checks for idle load balancers
AWS Compute Optimizer, which analyzes utilization history and recommends rightsized instance types
explain: Compute Optimizer uses historical utilization metrics to recommend optimal EC2, Auto Scaling group, Lambda, and other resource configurations. Cost Explorer shows spend but does not model performance headroom, and a single CPU alarm cannot evaluate memory, network, and other dimensions together.

q: A retail application predictably scales from 10 instances on weekday nights to 80 instances every morning at 8 a.m. and back down at 6 p.m. Which scaling approach most cost-effectively matches this pattern?
options: Keeping 80 On-Demand instances running around the clock for safety
Manual scaling performed by an operator after users report slowness
Scheduled scaling actions on the Auto Scaling group aligned to the known morning and evening times
Spot Fleet requests that wait for the cheapest capacity each morning
explain: Scheduled scaling proactively adds and removes capacity on a known timetable, so the fleet is right-sized before demand arrives and does not stay oversized overnight. Running the peak fleet continuously wastes money, and reactive manual scaling harms both cost and performance.

q: A web tier experiences unpredictable traffic spikes, and the team wants Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to maintain average CPU utilization near 55 percent without manual intervention. Which scaling policy best fits this goal?
options: A target tracking scaling policy on the ASGAverageCPUUtilization metric with a 55 percent target
Simple scaling with a long cooldown and a single fixed adjustment
A step scaling policy that adds a fixed 10 instances on every alarm
Scheduled scaling actions recreated daily from traffic forecasts
explain: Target tracking automatically adjusts capacity to hold a chosen metric at its target value, which suits unpredictable load. Step and simple scaling react to thresholds with fixed adjustments and require more tuning, while scheduled scaling needs a predictable timetable the workload does not have.

q: A company migrates stateless container tasks from Amazon EC2 to AWS Fargate and learns that some batch tasks tolerate interruption. Which additional choice lowers the cost of those interruptible tasks?
options: Place all Fargate tasks on Dedicated Hosts
Run the interruptible tasks on Fargate Spot capacity
Purchase Standard Reserved Instances for the Fargate tasks
Run every task with Fargate provisioned capacity reservations
explain: Fargate Spot runs tasks on spare capacity at a discount in exchange for accepting interruption with a short warning, matching batch work that tolerates restarts. Fargate has no Dedicated Host or Reserved Instance purchase model, and provisioned reservations are not a Fargate discount mechanism.

q: A team runs long-lived, event-driven workflows in AWS Step Functions where each execution lasts several minutes, must keep a full execution history, and runs only a few thousand times per month. Which workflow type is most cost-appropriate?
options: Express Workflows, which require every execution to finish within five minutes
Standard Workflows, which charge per state transition but suit long-running, low-volume, auditable executions
Step Functions distributed map runs billed as Lambda invocations only
Amazon EventBridge Scheduler rules that replace the workflow entirely
explain: Standard Workflows support long durations, exactly-once semantics, and full history, and their per-transition pricing is economical at low volume. Express Workflows cap duration at five minutes and price by duration and requests, which favors very high-volume, short executions instead.
