q: A critical production stack must not be accidentally deleted by an operator with stack permissions. Which CloudFormation control directly prevents deletion?
options: Enable termination protection on the stack
Set the stack policy to deny all resource updates
Add a DeletionPolicy of Snapshot to every resource in the template
Require a change set for every stack operation
explain: Termination protection blocks stack deletion until it is explicitly disabled, which is the direct safeguard against accidental removal. A stack policy controls updates to specific resources, not deletion of the stack itself.

q: An update fails midway and an engineer needs the stack to stay in its failed state so the team can inspect resource events instead of rolling back immediately. Which option supports this troubleshooting need?
options: Enable termination protection so the failed update cannot complete
Disable rollback on failure for the stack operation so failed resources are retained for investigation
Delete the failed resources manually before reviewing stack events
Use a change set to hide the failed resources from the console
explain: CloudFormation's rollback-on-failure behaviour can be disabled for create or update operations, preserving the failed state for diagnosis. The trade-off is that the team must clean up or roll back manually afterward.

q: A new CDK environment cannot deploy because the resources CDK needs for asset storage and deployment roles do not yet exist there. Which step prepares that environment?
options: Synthesize the app and store the template in Parameter Store
Create a CloudFormation Hook for the target account
Bootstrap the environment with the AWS CDK bootstrap stack
Enable StackSets for the CDK application
explain: Bootstrapping provisions the S3 bucket, roles, and other resources the CDK uses to deploy assets in an account-Region pair. Synthesis only produces the template; it does not prepare the target environment.

q: A StackSet uses service-managed permissions and a new Region becomes available where the baseline must also run. What must the administrator do for existing target accounts to receive instances in that Region?
options: Nothing, because StackSets always deploy to every current and future Region automatically
Recreate the StackSet from scratch with a new template
Bootstrap each account again for the new Region
Add the Region to the StackSet deployment targets and create stack instances there
explain: StackSets deploy only to the accounts and Regions specified as deployment targets; adding a Region is an explicit target change. Automatic deployment applies to accounts joining a targeted OU, not to unlisted Regions.

q: A company wants StackSets to run under AWS Organizations so target accounts do not each need a manually maintained execution role. Which permission model provides this?
options: Service-managed permissions, where CloudFormation creates and manages the required roles through Organizations integration
Self-managed permissions, where the team pre-creates administration and execution roles in every account
Cross-account IAM users created in each target account for StackSet access
A single root user credential shared with the administration account
explain: Service-managed StackSets integrate with Organizations and manage the deployment roles automatically. Self-managed permissions shift that role creation and maintenance to the team.

q: A team wants a reusable, machine-readable rules file that checks CloudFormation templates for required encryption and tagging before deployment in a pipeline. Which policy-as-code tool is designed for template evaluation of this kind?
options: AWS CloudTrail, which records template API calls for later review
CloudFormation Guard, which evaluates templates and other structured data against policy rules
Amazon CloudWatch, which alarms on template size
AWS CodeDeploy, which rolls back templates that fail a scan
explain: CloudFormation Guard is a policy-as-code evaluation tool that checks structured data such as templates against rules and can gate a pipeline. CloudTrail records activity but does not evaluate template policy.

q: A proactive Hook is being introduced, but the team first wants violations logged for two weeks without blocking any deployments. Which Hook configuration achieves this?
options: Set the Hook's failure mode to fail and rely on developers to ignore the errors
Configure the Hook as an AWS Config rule with periodic evaluation
Set the Hook's failure mode to warn so non-compliant operations are reported but allowed to proceed
Attach the Hook only to the production stack policy
explain: Hooks support warn and fail modes; warn mode surfaces violations for tuning and adoption without stopping deployments. Fail mode would block the operation the team wants to observe.

q: A secret in Secrets Manager must be usable by an application running in a different AWS account, under strict control over which account can read it. Which feature enables this sharing?
options: A dynamic reference in a template in the owning account, which automatically shares the secret
A Parameter Store advanced parameter shared through the console
An SCP that grants the consuming account access to the secret
A resource-based policy on the secret that grants access to the other account, together with appropriate KMS key permissions
explain: Secrets Manager supports resource-based policies for cross-account access, and the consumer also needs permission to use the KMS key encrypting the secret. SCPs set permission ceilings and never grant access on their own.

q: A team argues that using Parameter Store SecureString and Secrets Manager are interchangeable for database credentials. Which distinction most undermines that claim?
options: Secrets Manager provides built-in managed rotation for credentials, while Parameter Store does not rotate the underlying credential
Parameter Store cannot encrypt values at rest under any configuration
Secrets Manager values cannot be referenced from CloudFormation templates
Parameter Store parameters cannot be versioned
explain: Both can store encrypted values, but only Secrets Manager offers native credential rotation workflows that update the target database. That lifecycle difference is why credentials usually belong in Secrets Manager.

q: A company repeatedly deploys the same stack definition to development, staging, and production and gets identical resources each time, even when a deployment is retried after a network failure. Which IaC property is being demonstrated?
options: Imperative sequencing, where each retry replays every creation step
Idempotency of declarative deployments, where applying the same desired state again produces no further change
Manual runbook execution with operator judgement at each step
Drift detection, which blocks any retried deployment
explain: Declarative, idempotent tooling converges infrastructure to the stated desired state, so a safe retry does not create duplicates. Imperative step replay is exactly what can create duplicates after a partial failure.

q: A developer runs a command to preview the CloudFormation template that a CDK app will deploy, without deploying anything. Which CDK operation does this?
options: Bootstrapping the environment, which outputs the template for review
Executing a change set generated by the CDK CLI
Synthesizing the CDK app, which emits the CloudFormation template and cloud assembly
Running a CDK Aspect that deploys the template for inspection
explain: CDK synthesis translates constructs into a CloudFormation template that can be inspected, diffed, and handed to a pipeline. Bootstrapping prepares an environment; it does not render the app's template.

q: A CloudFormation template must create a resource type that CloudFormation does not support natively, including its create, update, and delete logic. Which extension should the team build?
options: A nested stack containing an empty template that waits for manual creation
A CloudFormation Hook that creates the unsupported resource after validation
A stack policy that allows the unsupported resource type
A custom resource backed by a Lambda function that implements the provisioning logic
explain: Custom resources let a Lambda-backed provider implement lifecycle logic for unsupported resource types within a stack deployment. Hooks validate operations; they are not a substitute provisioning engine.

q: A StackSet rollout for a compliance baseline must skip one regulated account and one Region where a separate baseline applies. Which approach enforces the exclusion while keeping the rest of the rollout automated?
options: Deploy to the target OUs but explicitly exclude the specified account and Region from the stack instances
Deploy everywhere and delete the stack instances from the excluded account afterward
Use a separate template with the compliance resources removed for all accounts
Disable automatic deployment for the entire organization
explain: StackSets allow specific accounts and Regions to be excluded from deployment targets, preserving automation elsewhere. Deploy-then-delete creates a window where the wrong baseline is live in a regulated account.

q: An auditor asks whether a control is preventive, detective, or proactive. An SCP that denies creating an unencrypted volume is best classified as which type?
options: Detective, because it evaluates volumes after they are created
Preventive, because it stops the non-compliant action from succeeding at request time
Proactive, because it inspects a template before provisioning begins
Corrective, because it encrypts existing volumes automatically
explain: Preventive controls block a disallowed action when it is attempted, as an SCP deny does. Proactive controls evaluate intent before provisioning, such as Hooks, while detective controls find violations after the fact.

q: A team wants to stop a deployment if a proposed resource violates policy, before any resource exists, rather than cleaning it up afterward. Which pairing correctly matches that goal?
options: AWS Config rules alone, because they evaluate resources before creation
CloudWatch alarms alone, because they block deployments when they fire
CloudFormation Hooks or CDK Aspects for pre-provisioning checks, instead of relying only on AWS Config rules for after-the-fact detection
Amazon S3 lifecycle rules, because they expire non-compliant templates
explain: Hooks run before provisioning and Aspects run at synthesis, so both can stop a bad deployment early. Config rules are valuable but detective, so relying on them alone means the resource is created first.

q: An administrator must ensure that when a stack is deleted, its RDS database is preserved as a final snapshot rather than destroyed with no copy. Which template attribute should be set on the database resource?
options: UpdateReplacePolicy set to Delete for the database resource
Termination protection enabled on the database resource itself
A stack policy statement protecting the database from updates
DeletionPolicy set to Snapshot for the RDS resource
explain: DeletionPolicy controls what happens to a resource when its stack is deleted, and Snapshot creates a snapshot for supported resources such as RDS and EBS. Termination protection guards the stack, not the per-resource deletion outcome.

q: A stack update must replace a resource, but the team wants the old resource retained rather than deleted when replacement completes. Which attribute governs that behaviour?
options: UpdateReplacePolicy set to Retain for the resource
DeletionPolicy set to Snapshot for the resource
Fn::ImportValue pointing at the replacement resource
A change set execution mode of Retain
explain: UpdateReplacePolicy applies specifically when an update requires replacement, and Retain keeps the old resource in the account. DeletionPolicy applies to stack deletion, which is a different lifecycle event.

q: A company plans to bring several manually created S3 buckets and DynamoDB tables under CloudFormation management without recreating them. Which capability supports adopting existing resources into a stack?
options: Drift detection, which automatically adopts any resource it finds
Resource import, where existing resources are mapped to logical IDs in a template and imported into the stack
StackSets, which import resources from all accounts at once
Change sets, which convert manual resources into stack resources on execution
explain: CloudFormation resource import associates existing resources with a template so they become stack-managed without recreation, after which drift detection can verify they match. Drift detection alone only reports differences.

q: A platform team wants the StackSets service, not the team, to keep deployment roles current as the organization grows. Which additional benefit does the service-managed model provide for new accounts?
options: New accounts receive root access to the administration account for deployments
Templates are automatically rewritten for each new account's naming standards
Stack instances can be deployed automatically to new accounts in targeted OUs without manually creating execution roles in each account
Stack policies in new accounts are disabled until the team reviews them
explain: Service-managed permissions let CloudFormation create and manage the execution role in target accounts, which is what makes automatic deployment to new OU members practical. Self-managed permissions require the team to provision those roles first.

q: A deployment pipeline must reject any template that declares a plaintext secret value in a parameter default before the template reaches CloudFormation. Which combination best implements this policy-as-code gate?
options: Rely on Secrets Manager rotation to clean up the plaintext value after deployment
Use a CloudWatch alarm on the stack to notify the team after creation
Add an SCP that grants read access to the template bucket
Run CloudFormation Guard or an equivalent template check in the pipeline and fail the stage when a rule matches a plaintext secret pattern
explain: A pipeline policy check can inspect the template artifact and stop promotion before deployment, which is policy as code applied at the gate. Post-deployment notification or rotation does not prevent the secret from being committed and deployed.

q: A SecureString parameter holds a shared API key, and leadership asks why rotation will be harder than expected. Which accurate explanation should the architect give?
options: Parameter Store stores and versions the value but has no built-in workflow to change the credential at the external service, so rotation must be built separately
SecureString parameters cannot be encrypted, so the key is exposed during rotation
Parameter Store automatically deletes old versions, making rollback impossible
Secrets Manager is required before any parameter can be read by Lambda
explain: Parameter Store provides storage, encryption via KMS, and versioning, but it does not coordinate changing the credential on the target system. Secrets Manager rotation exists precisely to coordinate both sides of a credential change.

q: During a StackSet update, the administrator wants deployments in different Regions to proceed in parallel, but operations within each Region to remain sequential. Which setting expresses this?
options: Failure tolerance set to zero for every Region in the operation
Region concurrency type set to parallel, with sequential behaviour being the alternative for one-Region-at-a-time rollouts
Stack instance concurrency set to sequential across all accounts
Automatic deployment enabled for all organizational units
explain: StackSet operation preferences include Region concurrency, which can be sequential or parallel across Regions. Failure tolerance controls how many failures are allowed, not the ordering model.

q: A CDK Aspect adds a required cost-allocation tag to most resources, but a handful of legacy resources must be exempted without removing the Aspect. What is the cleanest way to handle the exemptions?
options: Delete the Aspect and add tags manually to every other resource
Move the legacy resources into a separate AWS account permanently
Have the Aspect check a property or tag on each construct and skip the exempted constructs explicitly
Disable synthesis checks for the entire CDK application
explain: Aspects visit constructs programmatically, so the Aspect itself can contain a deliberate, auditable exemption check. Removing the Aspect sacrifices organization-wide enforcement to solve a narrow exception.

q: A template parameter for a production password is marked NoEcho, yet a reviewer still flags the design as unsafe. Which reason best justifies the reviewer's concern?
options: NoEcho prevents CloudFormation from using the value during deployment
NoEcho parameters are stored in plaintext in the template by design
NoEcho automatically shares the value with every account in the organization
NoEcho only masks display in console and API output; the value still has to be supplied and managed outside a dedicated secrets store with rotation and auditing
explain: NoEcho is a display safeguard, not a secrets-management solution: it provides no rotation, fine-grained access control, or secret lifecycle auditing. Referencing Secrets Manager addresses those gaps instead of passing raw secret values around.

q: An operations team wants one place to prove that every account's logging bucket matches the approved configuration today and historically. Which service provides the configuration history to support that proof?
options: AWS Config, which records configuration items and their changes over time for resources in each account
CloudFormation stack events, which retain the full history of every resource
AWS CloudTrail Lake alone, which stores resource configuration snapshots
Amazon Inspector, which inventories bucket configuration history
explain: AWS Config records a configuration item whenever a supported resource changes, building the historical record auditors need. Stack events describe deployments, not the ongoing configuration history of every resource.

q: A multi-Region StackSet deployment must start in the primary Region and only continue if that Region succeeds, to limit blast radius during a risky change. Which rollout choice fits?
options: Use parallel Region concurrency with a high failure tolerance for maximum speed
Use sequential Region concurrency and a low failure tolerance so the operation stops early on failure
Enable automatic deployment so all Regions update as soon as accounts join
Set maximum concurrent accounts to the total number of target accounts
explain: Sequential Region deployment with tight failure tolerance deliberately trades speed for a smaller blast radius, which suits a risky change. Parallel deployment with high tolerance does the opposite.

q: A developer defines a reusable construct that bundles an encrypted bucket, its policy, and logging, and publishes it for other teams to instantiate with two lines of code. Which CDK concept is being used?
options: A CDK Aspect, which publishes resource bundles to a registry
A CloudFormation Hook, which other stacks invoke as a resource
A construct, specifically a higher-level construct that composes multiple resources into a reusable pattern
A StackSet, which distributes the construct to other accounts
explain: Constructs are the building blocks of CDK apps, and higher-level constructs encapsulate opinionated patterns for reuse. Aspects modify or validate constructs; they are not the reusable resource bundle itself.

q: After a Hook moves from warn to fail mode, deployments that create open security groups begin failing in the pipeline's account, exactly as intended. Which statement best describes what has been achieved?
options: A detective control is now cleaning up open security groups after creation
A corrective control is now remediating existing security groups in all accounts
A compensating control has replaced the need for security groups entirely
A proactive control is now preventing non-compliant infrastructure from being provisioned
explain: Because the Hook evaluates the intended resource before provisioning and blocks it in fail mode, the control is proactive. Existing open groups elsewhere still need detective and corrective controls to find and fix them.

q: A finance team needs per-stack cost visibility, so every resource created by CloudFormation must carry the stack's name and ID tags automatically. Which behaviour already provides this without extra template code?
options: CloudFormation automatically applies stack-level tags such as the stack name and stack ID to resources that support tagging
AWS Config adds cost tags to resources after it evaluates them
CDK Aspects are required for any tag to appear on a CloudFormation resource
StackSets add finance tags only when service-managed permissions are used
explain: CloudFormation propagates stack tags and adds its own identifying tags to taggable resources, giving basic per-stack attribution for free. Teams often add richer business tags on top of that baseline.

q: A template uses a Secrets Manager dynamic reference for a database password. The password is later rotated in Secrets Manager, but the running database resource is not updated by CloudFormation. Why is this expected behaviour?
options: Dynamic references permanently copy the secret into the template file
Dynamic references resolve the secret value at stack operation time, so a later rotation does not by itself trigger a stack update to apply the new value
Rotated secrets cannot be used by CloudFormation after their first version
CloudFormation deletes the secret version used by the stack during rotation
explain: CloudFormation resolves a dynamic reference when the stack is created or updated; rotation alone does not redeploy the stack or necessarily require it, because applications reading the secret directly get the new value while stack-managed properties change only on a stack operation.

q: An organization wants both a hard ceiling on what accounts may do and a check on what templates intend to do. Which layered design is correct?
options: Use SCPs to evaluate templates and Hooks to set account permission ceilings
Use only AWS Config rules, which provide both prevention and template inspection
Use SCPs as the preventive ceiling for accounts and CloudFormation Hooks as the proactive check on templates before provisioning
Use Parameter Store to store both the SCP and the Hook definitions
explain: SCPs and Hooks operate at different layers: SCPs bound what principals in an account can do, while Hooks inspect the resources a deployment intends to create. Layering them covers both the actor and the artifact.

q: A StackSet deployment is failing in one account with an error that the execution role cannot be assumed. The StackSet uses self-managed permissions. What is the most likely fix?
options: Switch the template to use dynamic references for the role credentials
Enable termination protection on the target stack instance
Increase the StackSet failure tolerance so the error is ignored
Create or repair the CloudFormation execution role in the target account and ensure the administration role is trusted to assume it
explain: Self-managed StackSets depend on an administration role and a pre-created execution role in each target account with the correct trust relationship. Raising failure tolerance would hide, not fix, an account that never deploys.

q: A team stores application settings as plaintext String parameters and an audit now requires encryption, auditing of reads, and hierarchical organization by application and environment. Which Parameter Store design meets this?
options: Use SecureString parameters organized in a path hierarchy, with KMS encryption and CloudTrail logging of API access
Convert the settings to Secrets Manager secrets with automatic rotation enabled
Store the settings as stack outputs so they inherit stack encryption
Embed the settings in a CloudFormation Guard rules file
explain: Parameter Store supports hierarchical paths, SecureString encryption with KMS, and API-level auditing, matching a configuration-data requirement. Rotation is not needed for ordinary settings, which is why Secrets Manager would be heavier than necessary here.

q: A regulated workload requires that no human ever sees the database credentials used by a CloudFormation-deployed application, including during deployment. Which design best satisfies this?
options: Pass credentials as NoEcho parameters typed by an operator at deploy time
Keep credentials only in Secrets Manager, reference them by dynamic reference or grant the application runtime access, and audit access through CloudTrail
Email credentials to the deployment pipeline and delete the message afterward
Store credentials in a private S3 object that the pipeline downloads
explain: Secrets Manager keeps the credential out of templates, consoles, and human hands while providing controlled access and an audit trail. Any design where an operator types or transfers the password exposes it to a human by construction.

q: A team wants a pipeline where a commit triggers a build, tests, a security gate, and then a staged deployment, all as one orchestrated workflow. Which service should orchestrate those stages?
options: AWS CodeBuild alone, which manages multi-stage approvals across accounts
Amazon EventBridge, which replaces pipeline stages with cron rules
AWS CodePipeline, which sequences source, build, test, approval, and deploy actions
AWS CodeDeploy alone, which fetches source code and runs unit tests
explain: CodePipeline is the orchestration service that connects source, build, test, approval, and deployment actions into stages. CodeBuild and CodeDeploy each perform one part of that workflow rather than coordinating all of it.

q: A CodeBuild project fails because the commands to install dependencies and run tests were never defined for the build. Which file or setting supplies those build commands and phases?
options: The AppSpec file, which defines deployment hooks for CodeBuild
The CloudFormation template used to create the build VPC
The CodePipeline artifact stored in Amazon S3
The buildspec file, which defines build phases and commands for CodeBuild
explain: The buildspec is CodeBuild's build specification, organized into phases such as install, pre_build, build, and post_build. AppSpec belongs to CodeDeploy deployments, not to how a build runs.

q: An EC2 application must be replaced with a new version while the old version keeps serving traffic until the new fleet is healthy behind the load balancer. Which CodeDeploy deployment style provides this?
options: Blue/green deployment, where a new fleet is provisioned and traffic shifts only after the replacement is ready
In-place deployment, where the agent updates instances while they remain in service
Rolling deployment inside a single instance using the CodeDeploy agent
Canary deployment performed by restarting half of each instance
explain: Blue/green keeps the original environment serving while a parallel environment is prepared, then shifts traffic and can keep the old fleet for rapid rollback. In-place updates modify the live instances themselves.

q: A Lambda function deployment must run a validation test before any production traffic moves and a cleanup function afterward. Which file defines those lifecycle hooks for CodeDeploy?
options: The buildspec file, which contains the Lambda alias configuration
The AppSpec file, which names the Lambda hooks that run at deployment lifecycle points
The pipeline definition, which embeds hook code directly
The SAM template's globals section, which replaces AppSpec hooks
explain: For Lambda and ECS deployments orchestrated by CodeDeploy, the AppSpec file specifies lifecycle hook functions such as BeforeAllowTraffic and AfterAllowTraffic. The buildspec governs builds, not deployment traffic shifting.

q: A regulated service requires that only 10 percent of traffic reach a new Lambda version for five minutes, with automatic halt on errors, before the rest shifts. Which deployment configuration should be selected?
options: An all-at-once configuration so errors are detected across all traffic immediately
A rolling configuration that restarts one instance at a time
A canary configuration such as CodeDeployDefault.LambdaCanary10Percent5Minutes
A linear configuration that shifts 50 percent every minute
explain: Canary deployments expose a small percentage of traffic for a defined interval, limiting blast radius while validation runs. All-at-once maximizes exposure, which is the opposite of the stated risk control.

q: A team wants traffic to a new version to increase in equal increments, for example 10 percent every ten minutes, until it reaches 100 percent. Which deployment pattern is this?
options: A blue/green deployment with a single traffic shift
A canary deployment that stops after the first increment
An in-place deployment with a fixed batch size
A linear deployment strategy
explain: Linear shifting moves traffic in equal percentage increments at regular intervals. A canary makes one small initial shift followed by the remainder, while blue/green shifts essentially all at once after preparation.

q: A startup deploys with an all-at-once CodeDeploy configuration and a defect reaches every user within seconds. Which lesson should drive the next deployment design?
options: Adopt a gradual strategy such as canary or linear so a defect affects only a small share of traffic before rollback
Keep all-at-once but remove alarms so the deployment finishes faster
Replace CodeDeploy with manual deployments to slow the release
Disable rollback so the defective version stabilizes in production
explain: Gradual traffic shifting exists precisely to bound the impact of an undetected defect and to give alarms time to fire. Removing alarms or rollback removes the safety signals the strategy depends on.

q: Production deployments must automatically return to the previous version when a CloudWatch alarm enters ALARM state during traffic shifting. Which capability should be configured on the deployment?
options: A manual approval action that pages an engineer to decide on rollback
Automatic rollback triggered by deployment alarms in CodeDeploy or the deployment platform
A CodeBuild post-build script that rebuilds the previous artifact nightly
Termination protection on the deployment group
explain: CodeDeploy and related deployment configurations can monitor CloudWatch alarms during a deployment and automatically roll back when an alarm fires. Manual approval is too slow to satisfy an automatic-rollback requirement.

q: A central pipeline in a tooling account must deploy into separate staging and production accounts that do not trust each other by default. Which set of resources makes cross-account deployment work?
options: AWS credentials for the target accounts stored as plaintext environment variables in CodeBuild
A single IAM user in the tooling account with administrator access to its own account only
A cross-account IAM role in each target account that the pipeline can assume, plus an artifact bucket and KMS key whose policies allow that access
A public S3 artifact bucket so target accounts can read artifacts without policies
explain: Cross-account pipelines work through assumed roles in the target accounts and artifact encryption and storage policies that explicitly allow the pipeline and those roles. Storing other accounts' credentials in a build job violates least privilege and the cross-account model.

q: A pipeline fails at the deploy stage in another account with a KMS access error even though the artifact bucket policy is correct. What is the most likely missing permission?
options: The CodeCommit repository policy must allow the target account to push code
The CloudWatch Logs policy must allow the target account to read build logs
The artifact bucket must be made publicly readable for decryption to succeed
The customer managed KMS key policy must allow the target account or its deployment role to decrypt the pipeline artifacts
explain: Pipeline artifacts are encrypted with a KMS key, so cross-account consumers need both S3 access and KMS permissions on that key. Bucket access alone cannot decrypt the objects.

q: A container team needs deeper vulnerability findings for images in Amazon ECR, including continuous rescanning as new vulnerabilities are published. Which service provides that enhanced scanning?
options: Amazon Inspector, with enhanced scanning enabled for Amazon ECR
Amazon ECR basic scan-on-push only, which rescans images daily
AWS CodeBuild, which scans images during every build by default
Amazon GuardDuty, which scans container images before they are pushed
explain: Inspector provides enhanced ECR scanning with continuous evaluation against newly disclosed vulnerabilities and richer findings. Basic ECR scanning is a point-in-time scan with a more limited finding set.

q: A team compares ECR basic image scanning with Inspector enhanced scanning for a compliance requirement that findings be updated when a new CVE affects an already-pushed image. Which statement is correct?
options: Basic scanning continuously rescans, and Inspector scans only once at push time
Inspector enhanced scanning continuously rescans images, while basic scanning evaluates an image at scan time and does not provide the same continuous coverage
Both services block deployment automatically whenever any CVE is present
Neither service can report operating-system package vulnerabilities
explain: The key distinction is continuous versus point-in-time evaluation: Inspector keeps findings current as the vulnerability landscape changes. Neither scanner blocks deployment by itself; a pipeline gate must act on the findings.

q: A team still hosts its source in AWS CodeCommit and wants each push to the main branch to start the delivery workflow automatically. Which integration should be configured?
options: Schedule AWS CodeDeploy to poll the repository every hour
Store the repository URL in a CodeBuild environment variable
Trigger AWS CodePipeline from the CodeCommit repository event for the main branch
Use Amazon Inspector to watch the repository for commits
explain: CodePipeline can use CodeCommit as a source action so repository changes start a pipeline execution. Polling or manual starts would not meet the automatic-trigger requirement.

q: An image that passes staging must be the exact same image promoted to production, with no rebuild between environments. Which practice guarantees this?
options: Rebuild the image in production from the same Dockerfile and commit
Copy the image using its latest tag so production always gets the newest build
Run CodeBuild again in production with the staging build identifier
Promote the immutable image digest from the staging registry to production instead of rebuilding or retagging a mutable tag
explain: Promotion by digest ensures the binary that was tested is the binary that ships. Rebuilding can produce different bits, and a mutable tag such as latest can point at a different image by the time production pulls it.

q: A data science team must compare two foundation models on the same question-answering dataset using consistent quality metrics before choosing one for production. Which Amazon Bedrock capability supports this?
options: Amazon Bedrock model evaluation jobs, which score model outputs against a dataset using automatic or human evaluation
Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, which compare model prices at runtime
AWS CodePipeline model actions, which rank models by latency alone
Amazon Inspector model scanning, which grades answer quality
explain: Bedrock Evaluations runs models over a task dataset and reports metrics such as accuracy or robustness, with automatic metrics or human reviewers. Guardrails filter content at runtime; they do not run comparative evaluation jobs.

q: For a generative AI feature, subjective qualities such as helpfulness and tone cannot be judged reliably by automatic metrics alone. Which evaluation approach should the team add?
options: Increase the model's temperature until outputs appear more varied
Human evaluation within an Amazon Bedrock evaluation job, using reviewers to score model outputs
Use ECR image scanning to rate the quality of generated answers
Rely only on inference latency as a proxy for answer quality
explain: Bedrock evaluation jobs support human workforces for subjective dimensions that automated metrics cannot capture well. Latency and image scanning say nothing about whether an answer is helpful or appropriate in tone.

q: An ECS service must expose a new task revision to a test listener first, validate it, and only then shift production listener traffic gradually. Which deployment controller enables this flow?
options: Amazon ECS rolling updates using the default scheduler with two target groups
AWS CodeBuild with a second build stage for the test listener
Blue/green deployments for Amazon ECS controlled by AWS CodeDeploy using production and test listener rules
Amazon ECR replication between the test and production clusters
explain: CodeDeploy's ECS blue/green model manages alternate target groups and listener rules so traffic can be validated on a test listener before production shifting. The native rolling scheduler updates tasks in place without that listener-based promotion flow.

q: An ECS service uses rolling updates and must always keep at least 75 percent of its desired tasks healthy during a deployment. Which service settings control this?
options: The CodeDeploy canary interval and bake time on the service
The task definition's network mode and launch type
The ALB health check interval and deregistration delay alone
minimumHealthyPercent and maximumPercent on the ECS service deployment configuration
explain: ECS rolling deployments are governed by minimumHealthyPercent and maximumPercent, which bound how many tasks may be added or removed during replacement. Those percentages are what keep the stated healthy floor during an update.

q: A serverless team wants CodeDeploy to shift traffic between two Lambda function versions using an alias. Which prerequisite makes traffic shifting possible?
options: Publish immutable function versions and point an alias at them so CodeDeploy can weight traffic between versions
Keep editing the $LATEST version so CodeDeploy can shift traffic to it
Store both versions as Lambda layers in the same function
Use a function URL with basic authentication enabled
explain: Aliases can route weighted traffic only between published versions, not to the unpublished $LATEST version. Publishing versions is therefore the prerequisite for CodeDeploy-managed Lambda traffic shifting.

q: A Lambda deployment must fail if the function's signed code package has been altered after the approved build. Which control enforces code signing for Lambda?
options: Enable ECR image scanning on the function's deployment bucket
Configure a code signing configuration with AWS Signer and enforce signature validation on deployment
Require MFA on the IAM role that updates the function
Attach a Lambda layer containing the expected checksum
explain: Lambda code signing uses Signer profiles and a code signing configuration whose enforcement mode can block unsigned or tampered packages. A layer or MFA does not validate the package signature at deployment.

q: A pipeline stage must block promotion when Inspector reports a critical vulnerability in the candidate image, but allow promotion when only low findings exist. Which design implements this gate?
options: Enable scan-on-push and assume any pushed image is safe to promote
Store the scan report in S3 and review it during a monthly audit
Query Inspector findings for the image in a pipeline step and fail the stage when a critical finding threshold is met
Add a manual approval that asks reviewers whether scanning was enabled
explain: An effective gate actively evaluates findings against a threshold and fails the pipeline before promotion. Merely enabling scanning or reviewing reports later does not stop a vulnerable image from shipping.

q: A CodeBuild project needs a database password for integration tests, and the value must not appear in the buildspec or in plaintext project settings. Which configuration is correct?
options: Write the password into the buildspec as a plaintext variable for simplicity
Export the password from a CloudFormation stack output in plaintext
Place the password in an S3 file downloaded at the start of the build
Store the password in Secrets Manager and reference the secret as a Secrets Manager environment variable in CodeBuild
explain: CodeBuild can inject Secrets Manager and Parameter Store values as environment variables without storing plaintext in project configuration. The buildspec should contain only the reference, never the secret itself.

q: A monorepo pipeline must not allow a staging deployment and a production deployment action for the same execution to overlap in a way that corrupts shared state. Which pipeline concept helps order work safely?
options: Stage structure and action execution ordering in CodePipeline, with approvals and locks provided by sequential stages
Parallel CodeBuild projects that ignore pipeline stage order
A larger CodeBuild instance type so actions finish before conflicts occur
ECR immutable tags applied to source artifacts
explain: CodePipeline stages run in order and gate progression, so placing promotion steps in separate sequential stages with approvals prevents uncontrolled overlap. Compute size does not create ordering guarantees.

q: A team using AWS CDK Pipelines wants the pipeline itself to update automatically whenever developers change the pipeline definition in code. Which property of CDK Pipelines provides this?
options: The pipeline deploys application stages before checking its own definition
The pipeline is self-mutating: it first updates its own definition from source, then deploys the application stages
CodeBuild rebuilds the pipeline definition from the deployed template nightly
StackSets push pipeline changes to every account each hour
explain: Self-mutation is the defining CDK Pipelines behaviour: a synthesis change to the pipeline triggers a pipeline self-update stage before application deployment. That keeps pipeline-as-code under the same version control as the app.

q: A pipeline deploys the same application to two Regions, and the build artifact must be available in each deployment Region. Which design is required?
options: Store the artifact only in the pipeline's home Region and let deploy actions download it globally without configuration
Use a single S3 bucket with public access enabled for all Regions
Configure cross-Region actions with artifact stores in each Region so CodePipeline can deliver the artifact where the deploy action runs
Rebuild the application separately in each Region from a copied repository
explain: CodePipeline cross-Region actions rely on per-Region artifact buckets (with replication of the artifact as needed) so deploy actions can access inputs locally. A single home-Region bucket alone does not satisfy a cross-Region action's artifact store requirement.

q: Before production deployment, a release manager must review test results and explicitly approve the release during business hours. Which pipeline element implements this human gate?
options: A CodeBuild test action configured with a long timeout
A CodeDeploy alarm that waits for an acknowledgement click
An EventBridge schedule that pauses the pipeline until morning
A manual approval action in CodePipeline, optionally notifying approvers through Amazon SNS
explain: A manual approval action pauses the pipeline until an authorized reviewer approves or rejects, and SNS can deliver the notification. Timeouts and schedules delay work but do not record a human decision.

q: A CodeBuild project must build a Docker image, which requires access to the Docker daemon in privileged mode, but security asks that this be limited to only that project. Which approach is correct?
options: Enable privileged mode only on the specific CodeBuild project that builds Docker images and restrict who can modify that project
Enable privileged mode on every CodeBuild project in the account for consistency
Run the Docker build on a developer workstation and upload the image manually
Disable image scanning so the privileged build is not flagged
explain: Building Docker images in CodeBuild requires privileged mode, and scoping it to the single project that needs it follows least privilege. Applying it everywhere widens the security surface without benefit.

q: Build agents in private subnets have no internet route, yet CodeBuild must reach AWS service APIs to report results and fetch artifacts. Which network design supports this?
options: Move the build project to a public subnet with an open security group
Run CodeBuild in the VPC with appropriate routes and VPC endpoints or NAT for the AWS services it must reach
Store artifacts on the build host so no AWS calls are needed
Disable VPC configuration and rely on the default build network
explain: VPC-attached CodeBuild projects can only reach services their subnet routing allows, so private deployments need interface or gateway endpoints (or NAT) for services such as S3, Logs, and Secrets Manager. Removing the VPC would break access to private test resources.

q: A CodeDeploy in-place deployment repeatedly fails on a subset of EC2 instances while others succeed, and the agent logs show the agent is not running there. What is the most likely cause and fix?
options: The deployment group needs a larger canary percentage to reach those instances
The instances need to be moved into a different deployment configuration
The CodeDeploy agent is missing or unhealthy on those instances, so install or restart the agent and verify its IAM and connectivity requirements
The AppSpec file must be stored in the pipeline artifact bucket
explain: In-place deployments depend on the CodeDeploy agent polling and executing on each instance, so a stopped agent explains a consistent per-instance failure pattern. Deployment percentages do not repair a missing agent.

q: An API Gateway stage must receive a small share of canary traffic so a new API deployment can be validated with real requests before full release. Which API Gateway feature provides this?
options: A second account that mirrors production traffic at random
Lambda alias weighting attached to the integration function only
CodeDeploy in-place deployment applied to the API stage
Canary release settings on the stage, which route a configured percentage of traffic to the canary deployment
explain: API Gateway supports stage-level canary releases that split traffic between the production and canary deployments and record separate metrics and logs. That stage-level split is independent of how the backend function itself is deployed.

q: After a failed Lambda deployment, traffic must return instantly to the version that was serving before the release began. Which mechanism makes that instant return possible?
options: The alias still references the previous published version, so shifting the alias weight back restores it immediately without redeploying code
Rebuilding the previous version from source and publishing it again
Restoring the function configuration from a CloudFormation change set
Re-running the pipeline from the source stage
explain: Because both versions remain published and the alias controls routing, rollback is a routing change rather than a new deployment. That is the core speed advantage of alias-based traffic shifting.

q: A team replaces its self-hosted Git server with a managed connection so CodePipeline can start on pushes to an external Git provider without storing personal access tokens. Which integration should be used?
options: A plaintext personal access token stored in a CodeBuild environment variable
A CodeConnections connection (formerly CodeStar Connections) to the external Git provider as the pipeline source
An S3 bucket that developers manually upload archives to after each push
A CodeCommit mirror that an engineer refreshes weekly
explain: CodeConnections provides a managed, OAuth-based connection to supported third-party Git providers for pipeline sources without embedding personal tokens. Manual uploads and mirrors break the automatic trigger requirement.

q: Build times have grown because every CodeBuild run downloads the same dependencies from scratch. Which CodeBuild feature most directly reduces this repeated work?
options: Increasing the build timeout so downloads have more time to finish
Running builds in parallel across ten projects with no shared state
Build caching, using an S3 cache or local cache modes such as Docker layer caching, restored at the start of each build
Disabling dependency version pinning so fewer files are downloaded
explain: CodeBuild caching persists dependency or layer artifacts between builds so unchanged work is reused. A longer timeout tolerates the slowness rather than removing it.

q: A security scan of an EC2 fleet and its workloads must run continuously and report software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure. Which service should be enabled on those instances?
options: Amazon ECR, which scans EC2 instances that host registries
AWS CodeDeploy, which reports vulnerabilities in deployment groups
Amazon CloudWatch, which converts instance logs into CVE findings
Amazon Inspector, which scans EC2 instances for vulnerabilities and network reachability findings
explain: Inspector's EC2 scanning evaluates installed software against vulnerability data and can assess network exposure. ECR scanning is limited to container images and registries.

q: A team wants images scanned automatically every time one is pushed to its private registry, with results available before deployment decisions are made. Which configuration delivers this?
options: Enable scan on push for the Amazon ECR repository, using basic or Inspector enhanced scanning
Schedule a CodeBuild project to list images once a week
Require developers to run a local scanner and attach a note to the image tag
Enable CloudWatch Container Insights on the registry
explain: ECR scan-on-push triggers a scan when an image is pushed so findings exist at promotion time. A weekly or manual process leaves a window where unscanned images can deploy.

q: A production registry must prevent a promoted image tag from later pointing at a different, untested image. Which ECR setting enforces this?
options: Enable scan on push so tags are checked before they change
Enable tag immutability on the repository so existing tags cannot be overwritten
Set a lifecycle policy that expires untagged images after one day
Replicate the repository to a second Region for tag protection
explain: Tag immutability makes a pushed tag permanently reference the same image digest, protecting promotion integrity. Lifecycle policies clean up images but do not stop a tag from being reused.

q: A pipeline deploys infrastructure into a production account, but the pipeline's own service role belongs to the tooling account. Which trust arrangement is required for the deployment action?
options: The production account root user shares credentials with the pipeline through Secrets Manager
The pipeline role is granted administrator access in the tooling account only
The deployment provider assumes a role in the production account whose trust policy allows the pipeline or its designated role, scoped to the deployment permissions needed
The production account disables IAM role assumption for deployment safety
explain: Cross-account actions work by role assumption into the target account with a scoped permissions policy and an explicit trust relationship. Tooling-account permissions alone have no effect inside the production account.

q: A CloudFormation deploy stage in a pipeline must stop automatically if the newly deployed application breaches its error alarm in the first minutes after release. Which combination best provides this safety net?
options: Add a second source stage that re-runs the previous commit after a delay
Increase the CodePipeline stage timeout so the alarm has time to clear itself
Require the release manager to watch a dashboard for the first hour
Monitor the stack deployment with CloudWatch alarms and enable automatic rollback so a breaching alarm returns the stack to its prior state
explain: CloudFormation deployments can be configured with alarm monitoring and automatic rollback, turning an early production signal into an automatic recovery. Human dashboard watching does not meet an automatic requirement.

q: A Bedrock evaluation job must judge a summarization model, but the team has no labeled ground-truth summaries. Which evaluation design is still valid?
options: Use model-as-judge or human evaluation with a defined rubric, providing input prompts and scoring criteria instead of ground-truth labels
Cancel evaluation because automatic accuracy metrics are the only possible method
Measure only tokens per second and treat it as summary quality
Scan the model endpoint with Inspector to grade summary quality
explain: Not all evaluation needs reference answers: Bedrock evaluations support human and model-based judging against a rubric for qualities such as completeness and faithfulness. Throughput alone cannot stand in for quality.

q: Before a generative support assistant goes live, the team must verify that its answers stay grounded in retrieved company documents and flag invented facts. Which activity belongs in the validation plan?
options: Check only that the assistant responds within two seconds on average
Evaluate outputs against the source documents for faithfulness or groundedness using Bedrock Evaluations or structured human review
Confirm the assistant's container image has no critical vulnerabilities
Review the assistant's IAM policy for wildcard actions
explain: Output validation for a retrieval-based assistant must score whether answers are supported by the retrieved sources, which is a quality evaluation concern. Latency, image scans, and IAM reviews are necessary checks but do not detect invented facts.

q: A change freeze is in effect, yet an urgent security patch must be deployed through the normal pipeline. Which governance approach preserves both the freeze and the emergency path?
options: Deploy directly from a workstation so no pipeline record is created
Disable the pipeline's approval actions for the rest of the freeze
Keep the pipeline's approval gate and require explicit, audited approval from authorized approvers for the emergency change, rather than bypassing the pipeline
Grant all developers production deployment rights until the freeze ends
explain: An audited exception through the existing approval gate keeps traceability while allowing the urgent fix. Bypassing the pipeline destroys the deployment record exactly when scrutiny is highest.

q: Test results from CodeBuild need to appear as a structured report in the pipeline so reviewers can see failing tests without opening raw logs. Which CodeBuild feature provides this?
options: CodeDeploy deployment history filtered by test name
CloudWatch dashboards pinned to the pipeline page
S3 versioning on the artifact bucket
CodeBuild test reports, created by specifying report groups for formats such as JUnit in the buildspec
explain: CodeBuild can publish test and coverage results to report groups from common formats, making failures visible and trendable. Artifact storage preserves files but does not render structured test results.

q: A CodeDeploy deployment group should ignore a noisy alarm that is unrelated to the release, while still rolling back on the application's own error alarm. Which configuration expresses this?
options: Configure the deployment group's alarm list with only the relevant alarms, and use the option to ignore alarm polling state appropriately for alarms not under evaluation
Delete the noisy alarm from CloudWatch so it cannot affect any deployment
Set the deployment configuration to all-at-once so alarms have no time to fire
Attach every alarm in the account to the deployment group for maximum coverage
explain: Deployment groups monitor a defined set of CloudWatch alarms; scoping that list to release-relevant alarms prevents unrelated signals from triggering rollbacks. Deleting a shared alarm harms other operational uses of it.

q: A team assumes blue/green deployment automatically protects its database, but a new version writes data in a format the old version cannot read. What risk remains despite the deployment strategy?
options: Blue/green doubles database storage permanently, making rollback impossible
Rollback may be unsafe because data written by the new version can be incompatible with the previous version, so schema and data changes need backward-compatible design
The load balancer cannot shift traffic back to the blue environment
CodeDeploy deletes the old database when traffic shifts to green
explain: Traffic-level rollback does not undo data changes, so expand-and-contract, backward-compatible migrations are still required. Deployment strategy and data compatibility are separate concerns that must both be designed.

q: A SaaS team wants a failed in-progress pipeline execution to be superseded cleanly when a newer commit arrives, instead of deploying stale code after the newer release. Which CodePipeline execution mode addresses this?
options: Queued mode, which always runs every execution to completion in order
Parallel mode, which deploys every commit simultaneously
Superseded execution mode, where a newer execution can replace an older in-progress execution at a stage
Manual mode, which requires an engineer to cancel each stale execution
explain: Superseded mode prevents an older, slower execution from deploying after a newer commit has already moved ahead. Queued mode intentionally preserves order and would still deploy the stale change.

q: An organization wants scanning, signing, and approval evidence retained for every promoted artifact so an auditor can reconstruct who approved what shipped. Which pipeline design best supports this?
options: Keep evidence in the build agent's local disk until the monthly audit
Delete pipeline artifacts after each successful deployment to save cost
Allow developers to note approvals in the commit message only
Record scan results and signature verification as stage outputs, require a manual approval action, and retain pipeline execution history and artifacts under versioning
explain: Auditable promotion requires durable, structured evidence: scan and signing results, a recorded approval decision, and retained versioned artifacts. Ephemeral agent storage and commit messages are not reliable evidence stores.

q: A Lambda function that processes payments must never run unsigned or externally built packages in production. Which control should be enforced at deployment time?
options: Enforce a Lambda code signing configuration backed by an AWS Signer profile so only packages signed by the trusted profile can be deployed
Rely on ECR scan-on-push to validate the Lambda zip package signature
Require the pipeline's CodeBuild project to run in privileged mode
Trust the S3 bucket policy on the deployment bucket as signature validation
explain: Lambda code signing with enforcement rejects packages that are unsigned or signed by an untrusted profile, providing provenance control at deploy time. Registry scanning evaluates vulnerabilities, not package signatures for Lambda zip deployments.

q: In a blue/green ECS deployment, production traffic must not shift until an operator or automated check confirms the green environment passed its validation tests. Which CodeDeploy mechanism holds traffic at that point?
options: The CodeBuild test stage, which automatically blocks the load balancer listener
The deployment's traffic rerouting readiness check, which waits for approval or a lifecycle hook result before shifting production traffic to the replacement task set
An ECR lifecycle policy that prevents the green image from being pulled early
A CloudWatch alarm in OK state, which CodeDeploy treats as deployment approval
explain: Blue/green deployments can pause before traffic shifting until the replacement environment is declared ready, separating validation success from promotion. Build tests alone do not control the listener shift at deployment time.

q: A platform team must verify that a container image deployed to production was signed by its own CI process and not substituted afterward. Which signing and verification design supports this?
options: Record the image tag in the pipeline execution history and compare tags before deployment
Enable ECR scan-on-push and treat a completed scan as proof of signing
Sign the image with AWS Signer for OCI artifacts during the pipeline and verify the signature against the trusted Signer profile before deployment
Store the image digest in Parameter Store and require operators to compare it manually
explain: Signer can create and manage signatures for container images, and verification against the trusted profile proves provenance. A tag or an unaided manual digest comparison does not provide cryptographic signing evidence.

q: The same pipeline definition is reused for many releases, but each execution must record which Git tag triggered it and pass that value to its build and deploy actions. Which CodePipeline feature supports this?
options: A separate pipeline cloned for every Git tag that might be released
Hard-coded environment variables edited by an operator before each run
CodeDeploy deployment groups named after each release tag
Pipeline-level variables in a CodePipeline V2 pipeline, set at execution start (for example from a Git tag trigger) and referenced by actions
explain: V2 pipelines support pipeline-level variables that can be populated by triggers such as Git tags and passed through an execution, avoiding cloned pipelines per release. Manual edits break auditability and repeatability.

q: An operations team needs to know CPU utilization trends, application log lines, and the path of individual requests through microservices. Which mapping of telemetry to services is correct?
options: CloudWatch for metrics and logs, and AWS X-Ray for distributed request traces
CloudWatch for traces, X-Ray for log retention, and S3 for metrics
Amazon SNS for metrics, CloudWatch for traces, and X-Ray for dashboards
Systems Manager for all telemetry, with CloudWatch used only for billing
explain: CloudWatch collects metrics and logs, while X-Ray records traces made of segments and subsegments that show a request's path and timing across services. Each telemetry type has a distinct collection and analysis path.

q: A request slows down only when it reaches one downstream service, and the team needs per-service timing inside a single request trace. Which X-Ray data provides this?
options: CloudWatch log groups sorted by timestamp for the request hour
Segments and subsegments in the trace, which record timing for each service and downstream call
X-Ray sampling rules, which store the duration of every call
SNS notifications generated when a trace completes
explain: X-Ray breaks a trace into segments per service and subsegments for downstream calls such as databases and HTTP APIs, exposing where time is spent. Sampling rules decide which traces are recorded, not what the timing breakdown shows.

q: A team running containers on multiple platforms wants vendor-neutral collection of traces and metrics without rewriting instrumentation for AWS-specific APIs. Which solution should it adopt?
options: AWS X-Ray SDK alone, because it is the vendor-neutral OpenTelemetry distribution
CloudWatch Logs agents installed on every developer workstation
AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry, using OpenTelemetry instrumentation and collectors to send telemetry to AWS and other backends
Amazon SNS topics formatted as OpenTelemetry spans
explain: ADOT is AWS's supported OpenTelemetry distribution, so teams instrument once with open standards and can export to X-Ray, CloudWatch, or other destinations. The X-Ray SDK uses AWS-specific APIs rather than the open standard.

q: An EKS platform team cannot see per-pod CPU, memory, and network performance in one place and is missing container-level failures. Which CloudWatch feature should be enabled?
options: CloudWatch Synthetics canaries for each pod
Amazon X-Ray sampling for pod network traffic
CloudWatch RUM for node-level resource metrics
CloudWatch Container Insights for the cluster
explain: Container Insights collects cluster, node, pod, task, and service-level metrics and logs for ECS, EKS, and Kubernetes environments. Synthetics and RUM measure user experience, not container resource performance.

q: Logs from dozens of application accounts must stream in near real time into one central logging account for security analysis. Which CloudWatch Logs mechanism supports this cross-account streaming?
options: CloudWatch Logs subscription filters sending log events to a destination such as Kinesis Data Firehose or a Lambda function in the central account
Daily manual exports from each account's log groups to a shared workstation
CloudWatch dashboards shared from each application account
X-Ray traces copied into the central account each hour
explain: Subscription filters stream log events as they arrive to a supported destination, including cross-account destinations with the required destination policy. Export tasks are batch-oriented and too slow for near-real-time security analysis.

q: A cross-account log destination rejects events from a new application account even though the subscription filter is configured. Which missing element most likely explains this?
options: The log group in the source account has a retention period that is too short
The destination policy in the logging account does not yet grant that source account permission to put log events
The destination account has not enabled CloudWatch dashboards
The source account's logs are encrypted with the default CloudWatch key
explain: Cross-account subscriptions require a destination policy that explicitly allows each source account (or its organization) to deliver events. A correctly built filter cannot override a destination policy that does not trust the sender.

q: Compliance requires application logs to be retained for seven years, but they are queried only during rare investigations after the first 90 days. Which storage design balances retention and cost?
options: Keep all seven years in CloudWatch Logs at the standard retention setting
Store the logs on EBS volumes attached to logging instances
Export or deliver logs to Amazon S3 and transition older objects to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval or Deep Archive with a lifecycle policy
Delete logs after 90 days and recreate them if an investigation occurs
explain: S3 lifecycle tiers are designed for long, cheap archival retention with retrieval delays that suit rare investigations. Keeping rarely queried data in hot log storage for seven years is unnecessarily expensive.

q: An alarm must fire when application error log lines exceed a threshold, even though the application emits no explicit error metric. Which CloudWatch feature creates the needed metric?
options: A Synthetics canary that counts errors in the application UI
An X-Ray annotation that increments a billing metric
A log export task that tallies errors each night
A metric filter on the log group that counts log events matching the error pattern
explain: Metric filters turn matching log events into CloudWatch metric data points, which can then drive alarms and dashboards. Without the filter, free-text log lines are not alarmable metrics.

q: Pager alerts fire whenever either CPU is briefly high or a single health check fails, creating alert fatigue even though the service stays healthy. Which alarm design reduces this noise while still catching real outages?
options: A composite alarm that requires multiple underlying alarms to be in ALARM state before notifying
A single metric alarm with the evaluation period reduced to one data point
An SNS topic that delivers alerts only during business hours
Disabling actions on all alarms and reviewing them weekly
explain: Composite alarms combine child alarms with AND/OR logic, so notification can require corroborating signals of a genuine problem. Shortening evaluation makes a single alarm more trigger-happy, not less.

q: When a critical CloudWatch alarm fires, an incident should be opened automatically with responders engaged, not just an email sent. Which integration best provides this?
options: Send the alarm to an S3 bucket for responders to check each morning
Configure the alarm action to create an OpsItem or engage an incident through AWS Systems Manager (OpsCenter / Incident Manager) in addition to SNS notification
Attach the alarm to a Synthetics canary that restarts the application
Convert the alarm into a CloudWatch dashboard annotation
explain: Systems Manager OpsCenter and Incident Manager turn alarm signals into tracked operational work with ownership and response workflows. An SNS email alone notifies but does not create a managed incident record.

q: A public API must be probed every five minutes from multiple locations to verify a full create-read-delete transaction, with screenshots and logs on failure. Which service should be used?
options: CloudWatch RUM, which waits for real users to attempt the transaction
Amazon X-Ray, which samples only transactions users actually make
CloudWatch Synthetics canaries that run scripted checks on a schedule
CloudWatch Container Insights, which probes external APIs by default
explain: Synthetics canaries are scheduled, scripted probes that exercise APIs or pages and report success, latency, and failure artifacts. RUM depends on real user traffic and cannot guarantee a probe when traffic is absent.

q: A product team needs to understand real browsers, devices, and geographies affecting page load times for actual visitors to its web app. Which monitoring service provides this?
options: CloudWatch Synthetics, which generates simulated visits from AWS locations
Amazon X-Ray, which records browser rendering time for every visitor
CloudWatch Logs, which infers browser type from server logs
CloudWatch RUM, which collects client-side performance and error data from real user sessions
explain: RUM embeds a web client in the application to capture real user performance, errors, and session data segmented by browser, device, and geography. Synthetics data is simulated, so it complements rather than replaces real-user data.

q: A service owner defines a 99.9 percent availability objective over 30 days and wants burn-rate alerting when the objective is being consumed too fast. Which CloudWatch capability is built for this?
options: CloudWatch Application Signals, which supports service-level objectives (SLOs) and burn-rate alarms based on service signals
CloudWatch Logs Insights, which calculates SLO compliance from free-text queries
Amazon SNS, which tracks error budgets for each service
AWS X-Ray, which sets availability targets for traced services
explain: Application Signals discovers services, collects golden signals, and lets teams create SLOs with burn-rate alarms. Logs queries can support analysis but are not the managed SLO construct.

q: A manager confuses an internal engineering target with a contractual commitment to customers. Which statement correctly distinguishes an SLO from an SLA?
options: An SLO is legally binding, while an SLA is an informal team aspiration
An SLO is an internal target for a service indicator, while an SLA is a formal agreement with consequences if the commitment is not met
An SLO measures log volume, while an SLA measures trace volume
An SLO and an SLA are identical terms used by different cloud providers
explain: SLOs are the measurable targets a team sets for itself, typically set tighter than any external SLA so the team reacts before contractual commitments are breached. Treating an internal target as a contract misstates the obligation.

q: A Bedrock-based assistant's answer quality and correctness decline over several weeks although latency and error rates stay normal. Which monitoring approach is most likely to detect this model drift?
options: Watch only the 5xx error metric, because quality problems always cause errors
Increase X-Ray sampling so more traces are stored for the model
Periodically evaluate live or sampled outputs against a baseline with Amazon Bedrock Evaluations and track quality metrics over time in CloudWatch
Review the container CPU metrics for the inference endpoint daily
explain: Model drift is a quality phenomenon, not an infrastructure one, so it requires scheduled evaluation of outputs against a baseline and trending of those scores. Healthy latency and error metrics can coexist with steadily worsening answers.

q: Leaders need a single view of an AI agent's task success rate, average steps taken, and tool-call failures, not just API latency. Which observability focus addresses this?
options: Monitor only the foundation model's token count per request
Restart the agent whenever its latency rises above average
Store agent prompts in S3 and count them weekly
Monitor agent-level performance signals such as task completion, trace steps, and tool success alongside inference latency in CloudWatch and agent traces
explain: Agent performance is measured by outcomes: whether tasks complete, how efficiently, and where tool calls fail. Token counts and latency alone cannot show an agent that is fast but failing its tasks.

q: Users report a generative application feels slow, and the team must decide whether the model or a downstream retrieval call is responsible. Which data best separates the two?
options: Distributed traces (X-Ray or ADOT) that time the model invocation segment separately from retrieval and tool subsegments, together with inference latency metrics
A single end-to-end average latency metric for the whole application
The total monthly inference bill for the model
A Synthetics canary that loads the marketing homepage
explain: Segment-level tracing attributes time to each step of a request, so a slow model call can be distinguished from a slow retrieval call. A single aggregate metric hides exactly the distinction the team needs.

q: A serverless team wants custom application metrics published without running a metric agent or making separate PutMetricData calls for every event. Which CloudWatch feature embeds metrics in log output?
options: CloudWatch Logs subscription filters that convert logs into SNS messages
CloudWatch Embedded Metric Format, where structured log events are automatically extracted as metrics
Amazon S3 event notifications that publish metrics on object creation
X-Ray annotations that double as high-resolution metrics
explain: Embedded Metric Format lets applications emit metrics in a defined JSON log format that CloudWatch automatically turns into metrics, which suits Lambda and container workloads. It avoids custom metric API plumbing per event.

q: During an incident, an engineer must search error patterns across twenty log groups for the last three hours in one query. Which tool is designed for interactive cross-log-group analysis?
options: CloudWatch metric filters, which run ad hoc text searches on demand
S3 Select on exported log archives in Glacier
CloudWatch Logs Insights, which queries multiple log groups with a dedicated query language
Systems Manager Session Manager, which greps instances interactively
explain: Logs Insights provides interactive, structured querying across selected log groups and time ranges, returning fields, statistics, and visualizations. Metric filters create metrics prospectively; they are not an ad hoc investigation tool.

q: A Lambda function's traces are missing the downstream DynamoDB and HTTP calls that appear for other services in the same application. Which change completes the trace?
options: Increase the function's memory so traces have room to include subsegments
Enable CloudWatch Logs for the function and rely on log correlation alone
Raise the X-Ray sampling rate to 100 percent for all services
Instrument the function code with X-Ray or ADOT so downstream calls are captured as subsegments and trace context is propagated
explain: Sampling cannot create subsegments that were never recorded; the code must be instrumented to capture downstream calls and propagate trace headers. Log enablement alone does not build the trace structure.

q: An engineer opens the service map and sees one service with a high fault rate whose downstream dependency shows elevated latency. Which tool is the engineer using?
options: The AWS X-Ray service map (also surfaced through CloudWatch ServiceLens views), which visualizes services, dependencies, latency, and faults
CloudWatch RUM session replay for backend services
Amazon Inspector findings sorted by service name
Systems Manager inventory grouped by managed node
explain: The service map renders traced services and their connections with latency and error indicators, making it the fastest way to localize a fault in a distributed request path. The other tools serve device, security, and inventory use cases.

q: A central observability account must view metrics and traces from fifty application accounts without logging into each one. Which CloudWatch capability links those accounts for cross-account observability?
options: Sharing a single IAM user credential among all account administrators
CloudWatch cross-account observability using Observability Access Manager (OAM) links from source accounts to a central monitoring account
Exporting each account's dashboards to S3 and importing them centrally
Enabling CloudWatch Synthetics in the central account for every service
explain: OAM links let a monitoring account view and search metrics, logs, traces, and related telemetry shared by linked source accounts. Credential sharing violates account isolation and is not a monitoring feature.

q: A team wants the same operational dashboard visible from several accounts that own different parts of a service. Which CloudWatch sharing model supports this?
options: Copy the dashboard JSON manually whenever a widget changes
Publish the dashboard as a public web page without authentication
Share the CloudWatch dashboard with the other accounts (view-only or edit permissions) for cross-account viewing
Attach the dashboard to an SNS topic for distribution
explain: CloudWatch supports cross-account dashboard sharing with controlled permissions, so all teams see the same live widgets. Manual JSON copies drift immediately after the first edit.

q: A trading application needs metric data at one-second granularity for a custom latency metric during short scaling events. Which CloudWatch configuration provides this?
options: Set the standard metric period to one second in the alarm only
Export the metric to S3 every second using a subscription filter
Enable detailed monitoring on the load balancer and reuse its period
Publish the metric as a high-resolution custom metric with a one-second storage resolution
explain: High-resolution metrics must be published with StorageResolution of 1 second; alarms can then evaluate them at short periods. Standard metrics are stored at coarser resolution regardless of alarm settings.
