q: Traffic to a retail service is highly seasonal, so a fixed CPU threshold alarms every sale event even though behaviour is normal for that season. Which alarm type adapts to the expected pattern?
options: A CloudWatch anomaly detection alarm, which alarms when the metric moves outside a modelled expected band
A static threshold alarm with the threshold raised permanently
A composite alarm that includes the marketing calendar as a child alarm
An alarm based on a single data point with no evaluation period
explain: Anomaly detection models the metric's normal seasonal behaviour and detects genuine deviations from it. Raising a static threshold would also hide real incidents outside sale periods.

q: Kubernetes nodes show healthy averages, but individual pods are being CPU-throttled and restarting, which cluster averages conceal. Which data source exposes the pod-level problem?
options: CloudWatch billing metrics broken down by linked account
CloudWatch Container Insights performance logs and metrics at pod and container level for the EKS cluster
X-Ray traces sampled from the cluster's ingress controller only
Amazon S3 storage metrics for the cluster's log bucket
explain: Container Insights publishes granular metrics down to the pod and container, revealing throttling and restarts that node averages mask. Billing and storage metrics contain no workload performance detail.

q: A log group created two years ago still retains every log forever, and storage cost grows each month although investigations never look back more than 90 days. Which fix controls this cost?
options: Disable log delivery to the group so no new charges accrue
Move the log group to a different Region with cheaper storage
Set a 90-day retention policy on the log group so CloudWatch automatically expires older events, archiving anything needed longer to S3
Convert the log group to a metric filter with no retention
explain: Retention policies bound how long CloudWatch keeps log events, and pairing a short hot retention with S3 archival covers both cost and compliance. Stopping delivery would destroy the observability the team still needs.

q: A streaming pipeline processing log events must not expose customer email addresses that appear in application logs to downstream analytics. Which CloudWatch Logs feature can mask this data?
options: Log group encryption with a customer managed KMS key
Metric filters that count email-shaped strings
Subscription filters that drop entire log groups containing emails
CloudWatch Logs data protection policies, which identify and can mask sensitive data patterns in log events
explain: Data protection policies use managed and custom data identifiers to detect and mask sensitive data in logs, including in subscription deliveries. Encryption protects data at rest but does not hide values from authorized log consumers.

q: Finance asks for a one-off analysis of last year's logs that are no longer in CloudWatch, to answer a billing dispute. Which method retrieves that historical data if it was archived correctly?
options: Query the archived logs in Amazon S3 (for example with Athena) from the export or Firehose archive, rather than expecting them in CloudWatch
Run Logs Insights against the deleted retention period in CloudWatch
Restore the log group from a CloudWatch snapshot
Open an X-Ray trace for each request from last year
explain: Once logs age out of CloudWatch retention, the S3 archive created by export tasks or subscription delivery to Firehose is the system of record, and Athena can query it in place. CloudWatch cannot query data it has expired.

q: A watchdog check must alarm precisely when a service stops sending its heartbeat metric, rather than when the value is merely low. Which alarm setting handles absent data correctly?
options: Set the alarm threshold to zero and treat missing data as not breaching
Configure the alarm to treat missing data as breaching so a gap in data points triggers the alarm
Use anomaly detection with missing data ignored by default
Create an SNS subscription that fires when no messages arrive
explain: Alarms decide how to treat missing data points; choosing breaching makes silence itself an alarm condition, which is the correct semantic for a dead-man's-switch heartbeat. Treating missing data as healthy would hide a total outage.

q: An alarm should page the on-call team and simultaneously open a tracked operational item so the issue is not lost if the page is missed. Which alarm actions should be combined?
options: Publish the alarm to a CloudWatch dashboard and a log group
Trigger a Synthetics canary and an S3 export from the alarm
Send an SNS notification for paging and create an OpsItem in Systems Manager OpsCenter from the same alarm state change
Attach the alarm to a second alarm with no actions
explain: CloudWatch alarms can perform multiple actions on a state change, so SNS paging plus automatic OpsItem creation gives both immediate attention and durable tracking. A dashboard annotation alone creates neither.

q: A canary that tests a checkout flow in a private VPC fails to reach the application's internal endpoint. Which canary configuration detail is most likely wrong?
options: The canary's runtime version is newer than the application's framework
The canary is configured to take screenshots on failure
The canary schedule is set to every five minutes instead of every minute
The canary's VPC configuration, subnets, or security group do not allow network access to the private endpoint
explain: Synthetics canaries can run inside a VPC, but they need the correct subnets and a security group that can reach the target endpoint. Schedule and screenshot settings affect cadence and evidence, not basic connectivity.

q: A team already has Synthetics canaries and asks why real-user data is still needed before a frontend release decision. Which limitation of canaries justifies adding RUM?
options: Canaries test scripted paths from AWS locations and cannot represent the diversity of real users' browsers, devices, networks, and behaviours that RUM captures
Canaries cannot run more than once per day, so their data is too sparse
Canaries do not produce any metrics that can be alarmed on
RUM is required for canaries to execute their scripts
explain: Synthetic coverage is controlled and repeatable but narrow; RUM reveals how the release actually performs for the real population. The two are complementary, which is why mature teams run both.

q: A platform team wants service discovery, health, and latency signals for services on EKS, ECS, and Lambda with minimal custom instrumentation work. Which enablement path fits?
options: Manually build a separate dashboard for every service from raw log queries
Enable CloudWatch Application Signals, which auto-instruments supported environments and discovers application services and their dependencies
Install the CloudWatch agent on every Lambda function
Create an X-Ray group for each service and maintain it by hand
explain: Application Signals is designed to reduce instrumentation effort by collecting and correlating signals automatically in supported environments and presenting a service-level view. Manual dashboards do not scale with service count.

q: An SRE review focuses on latency, traffic, errors, and saturation for a checkout service. Which observability concept are these four measures an example of?
options: The four pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework
The four stages of a CodePipeline delivery workflow
The four golden signals used to judge service health from the user's perspective
The four types of CloudWatch alarm states
explain: Latency, traffic, errors, and saturation are the classic golden signals for monitoring a service, and Application Signals organizes service health around them. They are operational measures, not framework pillars or pipeline stages.

q: Tracing every request is too costly, but the team must guarantee that a baseline number of traces per second is always captured plus a percentage of additional traffic. Which X-Ray sampling configuration provides this?
options: A CloudWatch alarm that samples requests when latency is high
A Lambda memory setting that reserves space for trace storage
An S3 lifecycle rule that samples stored traces after upload
An X-Ray sampling rule with a fixed reservoir for the baseline rate and a percentage applied to additional requests
explain: X-Ray sampling rules combine a reservoir (a fixed number of requests per second) with a sampling percentage for the remainder, exactly matching a guaranteed baseline plus proportional coverage. Storage and alarm settings do not control trace capture.

q: A polyglot organization wants one instrumentation standard so Java, Go, and Python services can all send traces to multiple analysis tools. Which choice best supports that goal?
options: Instrument with OpenTelemetry APIs and use AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry collectors and exporters
Require every team to use the X-Ray SDK's proprietary segment format
Convert all services to a single programming language before tracing
Store traces as free-text logs and parse them per language
explain: OpenTelemetry provides language SDKs under one standard, and ADOT packages AWS-supported distributions and collectors for it. A proprietary single-vendor format undermines the multi-tool portability the organization wants.

q: Log subscriptions are set up in every account, but events from the eu-west-1 source accounts never arrive at the central destination in the same Region's logging pipeline, while us-east-1 works. Which architectural fact most likely explains this?
options: CloudWatch Logs subscriptions silently drop any Region outside the United States
CloudWatch Logs subscription destinations operate per Region, so each source Region needs its own destination and subscription arrangement feeding the central pipeline
The eu-west-1 log groups must be renamed to match the us-east-1 naming pattern
SNS topics in the logging account block European log events by default
explain: Log subscription delivery is regional: a destination in one Region cannot receive subscription streams from log groups in another. Multi-Region aggregation therefore deploys a destination or forwarder per Region into the central store.

q: Raw log volume is too large to ship directly to long-term storage, so the central pipeline must buffer, compress, and optionally transform events before writing them to S3. Which delivery service fits this role?
options: Amazon SNS, which compresses large batches into S3 objects
AWS X-Ray, which archives log batches after tracing them
Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose, which buffers and can transform records before delivering them to S3
CloudWatch Alarms, which write compressed log files on state changes
explain: Firehose is the managed delivery stream for this pattern: it receives subscription events, buffers them by size or time, can invoke a transform, and writes compressed objects to S3. SNS is a notification fan-out service, not a buffered archive writer.

q: A flaky external dependency causes brief single-point breaches several times a day, and the team wants an alarm only when at least three of the last five evaluation points breach. Which alarm configuration expresses this?
options: Set the alarm period to five seconds and the threshold to three
Create five separate alarms and subscribe them all to SNS
Treat missing data as breaching for the dependency alarm
Set datapoints to alarm to 3 out of 5 evaluation periods for the alarm
explain: The M-out-of-N datapoints-to-alarm setting tolerates isolated spikes while still alarming on sustained problems. It is the standard way to express that exact tolerance in a metric alarm.

q: After a host is terminated, its old alarm sits in a state that confuses new operators reviewing the alarm list. Which state is the alarm most likely in, and why?
options: INSUFFICIENT_DATA, because the metric has stopped reporting data points for the alarm to evaluate
ALARM, because a terminated host is always treated as breaching
OK, because missing metrics are converted to zero values
DISABLED, because CloudWatch automatically disables alarms for terminated resources
explain: When a metric stops publishing, its alarm transitions to INSUFFICIENT_DATA rather than OK or ALARM, signalling that the monitoring itself has a gap. Cleanup or missing-data treatment decisions should be based on that meaning.

q: A regulated log group must be encrypted with a key whose access the security team controls and can audit separately. Which configuration is required?
options: Enable default CloudWatch encryption and export the AWS managed key policy
Associate a customer managed KMS key with the log group and grant the CloudWatch Logs service permission to use it
Store an encryption password as a log group tag
Encrypt each log line in application code and disable CloudWatch encryption
explain: Log groups support association with a customer managed KMS key, and the key policy must allow the Logs service to use it. AWS managed keys do not give the security team the separate control and audit they require.

q: An alarm must trigger per payment method, extracted from log lines, rather than as one aggregate error count. Which metric filter capability creates those separate series?
options: Create one log group per payment method and filter each separately
Use a composite alarm with one child alarm per log line
Assign a dimension value extracted from the log event, such as the payment method field, in the metric filter
Publish the metric through Embedded Metric Format without dimensions
explain: Metric filters can extract dimension values from log fields, producing a distinct metric time series per payment method that can be alarmed independently. Without the dimension, all methods collapse into one aggregate.

q: EC2 instances in a private fleet must report memory and disk utilization, which the standard CloudWatch metrics do not include, along with their system logs. Which agent should be deployed?
options: The X-Ray daemon, which also collects host memory metrics
The CodeDeploy agent, which publishes host utilization after deployments
The Systems Manager agent alone, which includes memory metrics by default
The unified CloudWatch agent, configured to collect memory and disk metrics and to push log files to CloudWatch Logs
explain: Memory and disk usage are not among the hypervisor-level default EC2 metrics, so the CloudWatch agent is required to collect them from inside the instance, alongside log shipping. Other agents serve tracing, deployment, or management roles.

q: A Synthetics canary for a private internal tool must authenticate and reach an endpoint that resolves only inside the company's VPC. Which canary design is appropriate?
options: Run the canary in the VPC with subnets and security groups that can reach the internal endpoint, storing any credentials in Secrets Manager
Run the canary outside a VPC and add the internal hostname to a public DNS zone
Embed the service account password in the canary script stored in S3
Use RUM instead, because browser users are already inside the network
explain: VPC-attached canaries can probe private endpoints when their networking permits it, and Secrets Manager keeps credentials out of the script artifact. Publicly exposing an internal tool just to test it would create the risk monitoring is meant to reduce.

q: A RUM application monitors only a fraction of sessions to control cost, yet the team still needs representative performance data across user segments. Which RUM setting controls this trade-off?
options: The canary frequency configured for Synthetics
The session sampling rate configured for the RUM app monitor
The X-Ray reservoir size for traced requests
The log group retention period for the web tier
explain: RUM app monitors can sample a percentage of user sessions, balancing data volume and cost while keeping a representative sample. The other sampling controls belong to synthetic, tracing, and log subsystems.

q: A team creates an SLO that 99.9 percent of requests complete within 300 milliseconds over a rolling 30-day window, measured from Application Signals latency data. Which element of the SLO is the 300-millisecond value?
options: The error budget, which is the 0.1 percent complement of the target
The burn rate, which is calculated from the threshold and window
The threshold on the service level indicator (SLI) that defines a good event for the latency objective
The SLA penalty that applies when the threshold is missed
explain: In an SLO, the SLI is the measured quantity, the goal is the target percentage, and the threshold defines which events count as good. The error budget is derived from the goal, not from the latency threshold itself.

q: A planned database migration will cause a short, approved period of elevated errors that should not consume the service's error budget reporting for the month. Which SLO practice handles this?
options: Delete the SLO and recreate it after the migration so history resets
Lower the SLO target permanently to absorb the migration errors
Stop all monitoring during the migration so no bad events are recorded
Use an exclusion window (or equivalent planned-downtime handling) for the approved maintenance period in the SLO configuration where supported, documented in advance
explain: Planned maintenance is handled transparently by excluding the agreed window from SLO accounting, preserving the integrity of the rest of the period. Deleting history or blinding monitoring destroys the trust SLOs are meant to create.

q: Input data to a recommendation model gradually shifts as customer behaviour changes, and offline accuracy on last year's test set no longer predicts live performance. Which monitoring signal detects this in production?
options: Compare the statistical distribution of live inputs and outputs with the training baseline on a schedule and alert on significant drift, triggering re-evaluation or retraining
Compare this month's inference bill with last month's and alert on a 10 percent change
Watch the endpoint's CPU utilization for a sustained increase
Count the number of distinct users per day as a drift proxy
explain: Drift detection is fundamentally a distribution comparison between live data and the baseline the model was validated on. Cost, CPU, and user counts can move for many unrelated reasons and do not measure input shift.

q: An AI agent's overall latency doubles, but model inference time is unchanged. Which tracing insight most likely explains the increase?
options: The foundation model has silently become slower for all customers
The agent is taking more steps or retrying tool calls, visible as additional spans and repeated tool invocations in its traces
CloudWatch has begun charging more for the same trace volume
The agent's log group retention was extended, slowing its execution
explain: Agent latency includes reasoning steps and tool calls, so trace analysis showing extra steps or retries explains growth that model metrics cannot. This is why agent observability must cover the whole execution trace, not just the model call.

q: A support agent built on Bedrock succeeds on most tasks but fails disproportionately on refund cases that require two specific tool calls in sequence. Which monitoring approach surfaces this pattern?
options: Review the monthly Bedrock invoice grouped by model
Run a Synthetics canary that opens the agent's admin console
Analyse agent traces segmented by task type, tracking step-level and tool-level success rates in CloudWatch so the failing sequence can be isolated
Enable Container Insights on the agent's account
explain: Segmenting agent traces by task and tool exposes where in a multi-step workflow failures concentrate, which aggregate success rates hide. Billing and infrastructure views contain no step-level execution detail.

q: Metrics from many accounts must stream continuously to a central analytics platform with only a few minutes of delay, rather than being pulled account by account. Which CloudWatch feature provides this export?
options: CloudWatch dashboard sharing, which exports metric values on a schedule
Logs Insights scheduled queries that convert metrics into log records
X-Ray trace indexing, which includes metric summaries per trace
CloudWatch Metric Streams, which deliver metric data continuously to a destination such as Kinesis Data Firehose for delivery to S3 or a partner platform
explain: Metric Streams are the managed near-real-time export path for CloudWatch metrics, including cross-account metrics visible to a monitoring account. Dashboards display data; they do not stream it to an analytics store.

q: One tenant's API keys account for most of a service's throttling errors, but aggregate metrics hide which key is responsible. Which CloudWatch feature identifies the top contributors to a metric pattern?
options: CloudWatch Contributor Insights, which ranks top contributors such as API keys or user agents from log data
CloudWatch anomaly detection, which lists the users causing each anomaly
Synthetics canaries grouped by tenant name
Metric filters that publish one metric for the whole service
explain: Contributor Insights builds ranked contributor time series from structured logs, exposing the heaviest keys or clients behind an aggregate problem. A single aggregate metric filter cannot break the problem down by contributor.

q: After a failed Synthetics check, responders need the screenshots, HAR data, and logs the canary produced to diagnose what the user would have seen. Where are these canary artifacts stored?
options: In the canary's Lambda function code storage, retained for 30 days
In the Amazon S3 bucket configured for the canary's artifacts, with failure details also reported in CloudWatch
Attached to the CloudWatch alarm as downloadable files
In CloudWatch RUM sessions recorded for the canary user
explain: Synthetics writes run artifacts such as screenshots, logs, and HAR files to its configured S3 artifacts bucket, while metrics and status appear in CloudWatch. Alarm records reference the failure but do not hold the artifacts themselves.

q: An SLO shows 40 percent of its error budget consumed in the first three days of a 30-day window while traffic is normal. What should the team conclude and do?
options: The SLO is healthy because 60 percent of the budget still remains
The window should be shortened to one day so the consumption percentage resets
The service is burning its error budget far faster than the sustainable rate, so releases should be slowed or halted and reliability work prioritized until the burn rate falls
More traffic should be driven to the service to dilute the error ratio
explain: Error budgets are a rate problem, not just a remaining-balance problem: consuming 40 percent in a tenth of the window implies exhaustion long before it ends. Resetting the accounting window hides the risk instead of reducing it.

q: An EC2 instance enters a stopped state unexpectedly, and an approved diagnostic script must run automatically while the event is recorded for the operations team. Which automation chain fits?
options: A CloudWatch alarm that directly edits the instance's state
A CodePipeline stage that redeploys the instance from source
A Synthetics canary that restarts the instance on failure
An EventBridge rule matching the EC2 state-change event that invokes a Systems Manager Automation runbook and publishes a notification
explain: EventBridge routes service events to targets, and Systems Manager Automation executes defined runbook steps, giving an auditable event-driven response. Alarms evaluate metrics; they are not the general event router for state changes.

q: Servers must receive operating-system patches on a defined schedule, only during approved windows, with compliance reporting afterward. Which Systems Manager capabilities should be combined?
options: Patch Manager with a patch baseline, targeted through a maintenance window, with patch compliance reported in Systems Manager
Run Command used manually by each server administrator after patch release
CloudFormation stack updates that replace instances whenever a patch appears
CodeDeploy deployments that apply operating-system patches as app revisions
explain: Patch Manager defines baselines and scans or installs, maintenance windows control when operations run, and compliance data shows which instances conform. Ad hoc manual patching cannot provide the schedule or the reporting.

q: A patch baseline for a regulated fleet must auto-approve critical security patches seven days after release, but never approve a specific faulty patch version. Which baseline configuration expresses this?
options: A maintenance window that runs seven days after every Microsoft release
Approval rules that auto-approve by severity and release age, with an explicit reject list containing the faulty patch
A tag on each instance naming the patches it refuses
A CloudWatch alarm that blocks the faulty patch at install time
explain: Patch baselines support auto-approval rules based on severity, classification, and days since release, plus explicit approved and rejected patch lists. The window controls timing of operations, not which patches qualify.

q: An engineer needs to distinguish a patch operation that only reports missing patches from one that actually installs them during the window. Which Patch Manager operations correspond to these?
options: Scan installs patches in test mode, while Install only writes a report
Both operations install patches, differing only in reporting format
Scan reports compliance without installing, while ScanAndInstall (install operation) applies missing patches that the baseline approves
ScanAndInstall is used for Linux only, and Scan is used for Windows only
explain: Patch Manager separates assessment from remediation: a scan evaluates and reports, and an install operation applies approved patches. Confusing the two can either leave a fleet unpatched or patch it unexpectedly.

q: A service's quota for a regional resource is at 92 percent of its limit and growth will exhaust it within days, risking failed launches. Which proactive approach should the team implement?
options: Wait for launch failures, then raise a support case for each failed instance
Reduce the quota request to match current usage to avoid scrutiny
Spread launches across accounts without requesting any increase
Monitor quota utilization with CloudWatch (via Service Quotas integration or Trusted Advisor checks where available) and submit a Service Quotas increase request before the limit is reached
explain: Service Quotas provides visibility into limits and a request workflow, and utilization alarming gives lead time to act before exhaustion. Waiting for failures turns a predictable capacity issue into an outage.

q: New accounts provisioned for project teams repeatedly hit default quotas that the organization has already had raised elsewhere. Which Service Quotas feature standardizes higher quotas for new accounts?
options: Quota request templates (organization-level templates) that automatically request the approved quota values for accounts in the organization
A CloudFormation Hook that edits quota values during stack creation
An SCP that sets quota values for member accounts
A Parameter Store parameter that stores the desired quota numbers
explain: Service Quotas templates let an organization apply a standard set of quota increase requests automatically to new or specified accounts. Storing a number in a parameter does not change any actual service limit.

q: ECS deployments repeatedly leave a service in a failed state after a bad task definition revision, requiring manual intervention to restore the prior revision. Which ECS feature automates this recovery?
options: ECS capacity providers, which replace the task definition on failure
The ECS deployment circuit breaker, which detects failed deployments and automatically rolls back to the last completed deployment
CloudWatch Container Insights, which redeploys the previous task set
Service quotas, which limit how many failed tasks can start
explain: The deployment circuit breaker monitors deployment success based on task health and rolls the service back automatically when a failure threshold is met. It is purpose-built for the repeated failed-deployment pattern described.

q: A Lambda function invoked asynchronously keeps retrying a poison event and amplifies load on a struggling downstream database. Which configuration changes reduce this retry amplification?
options: Increase the retry attempts to the maximum so the event eventually succeeds
Remove the dead-letter queue so failed events return to the source faster
Lower the asynchronous invocation retry attempts for the function and configure an on-failure destination or dead-letter queue so failed events are captured instead of endlessly retried
Raise the function's memory so each retry runs more quickly
explain: Asynchronous Lambda invocations retry by default, and reducing attempts plus routing failures to a DLQ or destination bounds the amplification while preserving the event for analysis. More retries against a struggling dependency worsen its condition.

q: Client code calling a throttled API retries immediately in a tight loop from thousands of instances, making the throttling worse. Which retry design should replace this?
options: Retry instantly with no delay so requests complete before throttling resets
Retry from a second thread in parallel to double the attempt rate
Disable error handling so throttled calls fail silently
Retry with exponential backoff and jitter, honouring retry-after guidance and capping total attempts
explain: Exponential backoff spaces attempts out as failures persist, and jitter prevents synchronized retry storms across many clients. Immediate or parallel retries concentrate load exactly when the service is signalling overload.

q: One high-volume tenant of a shared platform periodically exhausts shared worker capacity, causing failures for all other tenants. Which resilience pattern isolates this failure domain?
options: Bulkhead isolation, partitioning capacity (for example separate queues, concurrency pools, or accounts) per tenant or tenant tier so one tenant cannot consume the whole pool
A circuit breaker that stops all tenants when any one tenant overloads the system
A single larger shared pool so the noisy tenant has more room
Retries with longer timeouts for the tenants being starved
explain: Bulkheads limit how much of a shared resource one partition can consume, mirroring ship compartments that contain flooding to one section. A global circuit breaker punishes every tenant for one tenant's behaviour.

q: An Auto Scaling group must maintain average CPU near 50 percent without engineers hand-tuning thresholds as load patterns evolve. Which scaling policy should be used?
options: A simple scaling policy with a fixed cooldown and one adjustment
A target tracking scaling policy with the CPU target set to 50 percent
A scheduled scaling action that sets capacity every hour
A manual scaling policy driven by a weekly capacity review
explain: Target tracking automatically creates and tunes the underlying alarms to keep the selected metric near the target value. Simple and scheduled policies require the operator to specify adjustments and timing explicitly.

q: A retail workload shows a strong, repeating daily and weekly load pattern, and capacity must be ready before the morning ramp rather than reacting after it starts. Which scaling feature addresses this?
options: Step scaling, which reacts faster than target tracking to a breach
Instance health checks, which add capacity when instances fail
Predictive scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling, which forecasts load from historical patterns and provisions capacity ahead of demand
Warm pools, which forecast demand using machine learning
explain: Predictive scaling analyses historical load and forecasts future demand so instances launch before the predicted need. Reactive policies, however fast, still wait for a signal that load has already arrived.

q: Before trusting predictive scaling with production capacity, a team wants to see what it would have provisioned over the past weeks without letting it change the group. Which mode provides this evaluation?
options: Enable predictive scaling with a low maximum capacity in production
Disable all other scaling policies and observe for one day
Use target tracking with the forecast metric as a custom target
Run predictive scaling in forecast-only mode to compare its forecasts and recommended capacity against actual behaviour
explain: Forecast-only mode generates forecasts and capacity recommendations without scaling the group, allowing a safe back-test against history. Any mode that changes capacity is no longer a no-risk evaluation.

q: An alarm-based policy must add a large amount of capacity for a big CPU breach but only a little for a small breach. Which policy type maps breach size to adjustment size?
options: Step scaling, which defines different scaling adjustments for different alarm breach magnitudes
Target tracking, which always adds exactly one instance per breach
Simple scaling, which applies multiple adjustments without a cooldown
Scheduled scaling, which varies capacity by time of day only
explain: Step scaling evaluates how far the metric exceeds the threshold and applies the corresponding step adjustment, so bigger breaches get bigger responses. Simple scaling applies a single adjustment and then waits through its cooldown.

q: A legacy group uses simple scaling and oscillates, adding and removing instances every few minutes during borderline load. Which built-in behaviour is meant to damp this, and what is its limitation?
options: Health check grace periods stop all scaling while any instance is unhealthy
The cooldown period prevents further simple-scaling adjustments until it expires, but a single fixed adjustment and cooldown can still respond poorly compared with target tracking
Predictive scaling overrides simple scaling whenever oscillation is detected
Termination protection locks the group size during borderline load
explain: Simple scaling relies on a cooldown to avoid acting on stale metrics, yet its one-size adjustment is crude for varying load. Target tracking generally handles sustained borderline load more smoothly by continuously aiming at a metric target.

q: A conference registration site scales out every weekday at 8 a.m. for a predictable two-hour surge and back in afterward. Which scaling mechanism is the simplest fit for this known schedule?
options: Predictive scaling trained on a single day of data
Step scaling triggered by a clock-based CloudWatch alarm
Scheduled scaling actions that set desired or minimum capacity at the defined times
Manual scaling performed by the on-call engineer each morning
explain: Scheduled actions directly express a known timetable for capacity, which is the simplest and most predictable fit. Predictive scaling earns its complexity when patterns must be learned rather than stated.

q: Instances behind a load balancer return application errors and fail target health checks, yet the Auto Scaling group keeps them in service because they pass EC2 status checks. Which configuration change makes the group replace them?
options: Increase the health check grace period to give the application more time
Enable detailed CloudWatch monitoring on the instances
Set the group's maximum size equal to its desired capacity
Set the Auto Scaling group's health check type to ELB so instances failing load balancer health checks are marked unhealthy and replaced
explain: ASG health check type determines the source of truth for replacement: ELB health reflects application-level failure, while the default EC2 checks can pass for a broken application. A longer grace period would delay replacement further.

q: An ECS service's new tasks fail their load balancer health checks and are continually replaced, flooding logs and masking the underlying bad configuration. Which service setting gives tasks time to start while still detecting genuine failures?
options: Configure an appropriate health check grace period for the ECS service so initial startup is not counted as failure, then investigate the failing health check configuration
Disable the load balancer health checks for the service permanently
Set the desired task count to zero until the next release
Remove the deployment circuit breaker so failed tasks accumulate
explain: The grace period prevents premature replacement during legitimate startup, but repeated post-grace failures still indicate a real problem to fix in the task or health check. Disabling health checks would hide failures rather than manage them.

q: A Lambda function processing an SQS batch of ten messages should retry only the two that failed, not the entire batch. Which event source feature enables this?
options: Configure a dead-letter queue that receives the whole batch on any failure
Report batch item failures so the Lambda event source mapping retries only the failed message IDs (partial batch responses)
Set the function concurrency to one so batches are processed serially
Use an on-failure destination that replays the batch from the start
explain: Partial batch failure reporting lets the function return the specific failed message IDs, so successful messages are deleted and only failures are retried. Whole-batch retry duplicates work and can repeatedly reprocess good messages.

q: Events that a Lambda function cannot process after all retries must be preserved for later investigation and replay, not discarded. Which configuration ensures this?
options: Increase the SQS visibility timeout until processing eventually succeeds
Set the Lambda function timeout to its maximum value
Configure an SQS dead-letter queue (or Lambda on-failure destination) for the event source so exhausted events are captured
Enable Lambda provisioned concurrency for the function
explain: A DLQ or destination is the capture mechanism for poison events after retries are exhausted, preserving payload and context for analysis and redrive. Longer timeouts do not guarantee a permanently failing event will ever succeed.

q: A launch template change requires every instance in a group to be replaced gradually while at least 90 percent of capacity stays healthy. Which ASG feature performs this rolling replacement?
options: A manual termination of the oldest instance repeated until all are replaced
A predictive scaling policy set to refresh mode
A lifecycle hook that blocks new instances from joining
An instance refresh with a minimum healthy percentage, which replaces instances in waves and monitors health as it proceeds
explain: Instance refresh automates progressive replacement after a launch template change, honouring health and percentage controls and supporting rollback signals. Manual termination provides none of those guardrails.

q: Before an instance finishes initializing its application, the Auto Scaling group must not consider it for health replacement, and a custom script must signal when setup is complete. Which ASG feature supports this?
options: Lifecycle hooks that put the instance in a wait state until the setup signals completion or the heartbeat timeout expires
Warm pools that hold the instance outside the group indefinitely
Step scaling adjustments that delay health checks by one interval
Termination protection on the instance until setup completes
explain: Lifecycle hooks pause instances at launch or termination transitions, allowing external setup or draining logic to run and report back before the lifecycle continues. That pause-and-signal model is exactly what staged initialization needs.

q: Configuration drift on managed instances must be corrected continuously, not just at deployment time, so a required agent and file setting are always present. Which Systems Manager capability enforces this desired state?
options: Run Command executions launched manually whenever drift is suspected
Systems Manager State Manager associations that apply and reapply a document on a schedule to target instances
CloudWatch alarms that describe the desired configuration
Patch baselines that include the agent as an approved patch
explain: State Manager associations maintain a defined configuration state on a recurring schedule, remediating drift automatically when the association reapplies. One-off commands cannot provide continuous enforcement.

q: A Run Command operation across 5,000 instances must stop automatically if failures exceed 5 percent, to avoid pushing a bad script to the whole fleet. Which safety controls should be set?
options: A larger command timeout so failing instances have longer to succeed
An EventBridge rule that emails the operator after the operation ends
Rate controls on the Run Command execution: concurrency limits and an error threshold that halts the operation when exceeded
A second Run Command that reverses the first across all instances
explain: Systems Manager rate controls let an operation proceed in waves and stop when the error percentage crosses a threshold, containing a bad change. Notification after completion is too late to limit the blast radius.

q: An automation that calls downstream APIs during an incident must fail fast when the dependency is clearly down, rather than piling up timed-out requests. Which pattern, combined with backoff, provides this?
options: Unlimited retries with a fixed one-second interval until the dependency recovers
A bulkhead that gives the failing dependency its own unlimited pool
Increasing every request timeout to fifteen minutes during incidents
A circuit breaker that opens after a failure threshold, rejecting calls immediately for a cooldown before allowing trial requests
explain: A circuit breaker stops calls to a failing dependency for a period, protecting both caller and dependency, then probes recovery with limited trial traffic. Endless retries amplify the outage they are trying to survive.

q: A disk-full alarm on a log server should trigger an approved cleanup document, but only for that server type and never during the nightly backup window. Which design is correct?
options: Connect the alarm (via EventBridge or alarm action) to a Systems Manager Automation document targeted by the server's tags, with the execution window constrained by schedule or maintenance-window controls
Grant the alarm permission to delete files directly on any instance
Run the cleanup document manually whenever an operator notices the alarm
Create a new Auto Scaling group that replaces the server when its disk fills
explain: Automated remediation should invoke a reviewed document with tight targeting and timing guardrails, preserving control over what runs and when. Replacing the server or granting broad delete powers is disproportionate to a known cleanup task.

q: An S3 bucket found non-compliant by an AWS Config rule for missing default encryption must be fixed automatically using a standard remediation. Which Config capability performs this?
options: A compliance notification sent to the bucket owner's email
Automatic remediation on the Config rule using a Systems Manager Automation document (such as the AWS managed encryption remediation document) with configured retry attempts
A CloudFormation change set generated by the Config rule
An SCP that retroactively encrypts existing buckets
explain: AWS Config supports attaching remediation actions, including automatic execution of SSM documents, with retry settings when a resource is non-compliant. SCPs prevent future actions but cannot fix an existing resource's configuration.

q: Spot capacity for a batch fleet is about to be reclaimed in one Availability Zone, and the group should proactively launch replacements elsewhere before termination. Which ASG feature supports this proactive replacement?
options: Predictive scaling, which moves instances between Availability Zones nightly
Instance refresh, which reacts after Spot instances are terminated
Capacity rebalancing, which launches a replacement when a rebalance recommendation signals elevated interruption risk
Target tracking, which maintains Spot capacity in a single zone
explain: Capacity rebalancing acts on rebalance recommendation signals to launch replacements before Spot instances are interrupted, reducing disruption. Waiting until termination forces a reactive scramble for capacity.

q: A web tier's scale-out is too slow because new instances spend eight minutes installing software before they can serve traffic. Which ASG feature removes most of that delay?
options: A longer health check grace period so slow instances are tolerated
Predictive scaling with the forecast horizon extended to one week
A larger maximum instance size for the group
A warm pool of pre-initialized, stopped or running instances that join the group quickly on scale-out
explain: Warm pools keep instances initialized ahead of need so scale-out skips the lengthy setup when demand arrives. Grace periods tolerate slowness but do not shorten time to useful capacity.

q: A database-backed API must not be overwhelmed when its Lambda front end scales, even if request volume spikes tenfold. Which Lambda setting caps the function's concurrency as a protective rate limit?
options: Reserved concurrency for the function, set to the maximum the database can safely sustain
Provisioned concurrency set to the tenfold spike estimate
Function memory increased so each execution uses the database faster
The event source batch size raised to its maximum
explain: Reserved concurrency both guarantees and caps a function's concurrency, acting as a throttle that protects downstream resources. Provisioned concurrency pre-warms execution environments but does not cap total concurrency.

q: A team's automation Lambda intermittently fails with API throttling when it tags hundreds of resources in a loop. Which code-level change is the correct first fix?
options: Run multiple copies of the Lambda in parallel to finish sooner
Add exponential backoff with jitter to the API calls and reduce call rate, for example by batching or pacing requests
Remove error handling so throttling exceptions are ignored
Increase the Lambda timeout so the loop can retry indefinitely
explain: Throttling is the service asking the caller to slow down, so backing off with jitter and lowering request rate addresses the cause. Parallel copies or indefinite retries increase pressure on the already throttled API.

q: Instances in a group must be recycled at least every 30 days to satisfy a compliance rule, even when no other change requires replacement. Which ASG setting enforces this lifetime limit?
options: A lifecycle hook that terminates instances on their monthly anniversary
A scheduled scaling action that sets desired capacity to zero monthly
Maximum instance lifetime set to 30 days, causing the group to gradually replace older instances
Termination protection that expires after 30 days
explain: Maximum instance lifetime tells the ASG to replace instances that exceed the specified age, performing gradual, health-aware recycling. It achieves compliance rotation without a disruptive full-group restart.

q: An ECS service on Fargate must scale its task count automatically in response to a target utilization maintained by a capacity provider. Which configuration provides managed scaling for the provider?
options: Set the service's desired count manually each week based on forecasts
Use a CloudWatch alarm that starts a CodeBuild project to add tasks
Attach a Lambda function that polls ECS metrics every minute
Enable managed scaling on the ECS capacity provider with a target capacity percentage, used with an Auto Scaling group capacity provider for the underlying capacity
explain: Capacity provider managed scaling adjusts the underlying Auto Scaling group to maintain the target capacity buffer for ECS tasks automatically. Polling Lambdas recreate a managed feature with more operational risk.

q: A latency-sensitive Lambda function needs its provisioned concurrency adjusted automatically to keep utilization near 70 percent rather than fixed by guesswork. Which mechanism does this?
options: An Application Auto Scaling policy for Lambda provisioned concurrency using target tracking on ProvisionedConcurrencyUtilization
Reserved concurrency that grows automatically with request volume
A CloudWatch alarm that edits the function configuration directly
EventBridge Scheduler invoking a configuration script every hour
explain: Lambda provisioned concurrency is scalable through Application Auto Scaling, and target tracking on its utilization keeps a buffer of warm environments without manual resizing. Reserved concurrency is a static cap, not an autoscaling policy.

q: A CloudWatch alarm on queue depth must start a multi-step incident workflow that assigns responders, posts status, and tracks resolution, rather than a one-off script. Which Systems Manager capability is designed for this?
options: Systems Manager Parameter Store, with the incident steps stored as parameters
Systems Manager Incident Manager, with a response plan that defines engagements, runbooks, and escalation for the incident
Patch Manager, with the incident treated as a missing patch
Session Manager, with responders connecting to instances manually
explain: Incident Manager provides structured response plans, responder engagement, runbook execution, and incident timelines integrated with alarm and EventBridge triggers. A single script cannot supply the coordination and record an incident requires.

q: After an automatic remediation runs, auditors require proof of what document version ran, on which resources, and with what result. Which source provides this execution record?
options: The CloudWatch alarm history, which stores full runbook step output
The target instance's local shell history file
Systems Manager Automation execution history, which records the document, targets, steps, and status of each execution
An email sent by the automation to the team distribution list
explain: Automation executions are recorded centrally with inputs, step results, and outcomes, forming the audit trail for automated changes. Local or email records are incomplete and easily lost.

q: A remediation runbook that reboots instances must never reboot more than a small percentage of the fleet at once, even if an operator starts it broadly. Which runbook execution controls enforce this safety constraint?
options: Add a warning sentence at the top of the runbook asking operators to be careful
Increase the runbook timeout so reboots complete slowly
Tag the runbook as production-critical in Systems Manager

Set concurrency and error-threshold rate controls for the Automation execution (or run it through a target-limited, rate-controlled operation) so only a bounded share runs at a time and failures halt it
explain: Rate controls are the enforceable mechanism: they bound parallelism and stop the operation when errors accumulate. Documentation warnings rely on human compliance and do not constrain a broad execution.

q: A destructive remediation for production requires a senior operator's explicit approval inside the runbook before the irreversible step executes. Which Automation feature provides this pause?
options: An approval step (aws:approve) in the Automation runbook that waits for designated approvers before continuing
A CloudWatch alarm action that asks for approval by email
A manual approval action inserted into the patch baseline
A lifecycle hook with its timeout set to 24 hours
explain: Automation runbooks support an approval action that pauses execution until named approvers accept or reject, embedding human control inside the automated workflow. That is the native way to gate a destructive step.

q: An ASG health check replaces an instance that was intentionally made to fail checks during a controlled chaos experiment, ending the experiment early. Which design lesson follows for automated recovery?
options: Health checks should be disabled permanently so experiments are never interrupted
Automated recovery should respect maintenance or experiment signals, for example by suspending health-check replacement processes or tagging instances to exclude them, during planned disruption
Chaos experiments should only run in production without notice to automation
The ASG should be deleted and recreated after every experiment
explain: Self-healing automation cannot distinguish an experiment from an incident unless it is told, so planned disruptions need explicit coordination such as suspending ASG processes. Permanently disabling health checks removes production protection to serve an occasional test.

q: A queue-processing service must scale on backlog per instance rather than CPU, targeting roughly 1,000 messages in queue per running task. Which scaling approach fits this custom signal?
options: Simple scaling on CPU utilization with a five-minute cooldown
Predictive scaling based on last year's queue history alone
Target tracking on a custom CloudWatch metric (or scheduled Lambda-published metric) representing backlog per instance, using the queue depth divided by running capacity
Manual scaling reviewed at the weekly operations meeting
explain: Target tracking can follow a custom metric, and backlog-per-instance is the meaningful ratio for queue workers because it ties capacity directly to work waiting. CPU can stay low while a backlog grows if workers are I/O-bound.

q: A Lambda function fails downstream calls, and its built-in service retries plus application retries plus client retries combine into far more attempts than intended. Which principle should guide the redesign?
options: Add retries at every layer so at least one layer eventually succeeds
Disable idempotency so duplicate attempts are easier to detect
Retry synchronously at the client until the request succeeds, without a cap
Set an overall retry budget: allow retries at only one or two layers, use backoff with jitter, and make operations idempotent so necessary retries are safe
explain: Stacked, unbounded retries multiply load multiplicatively, a classic retry-storm cause. Coordinating retries under a budget with idempotent operations preserves resilience without self-inflicted overload.

q: Operational runbooks for common incidents exist only as wiki pages, and response quality varies by who is on call. Which improvement most directly standardizes execution?
options: Convert the wiki procedures into Systems Manager Automation runbooks with defined steps, inputs, and guardrails, and link them to the incident response plans that invoke them
Require responders to read the wiki aloud on the incident call
Move the wiki pages into a shared S3 bucket for faster access
Print the runbooks and store them at the operations desk
explain: Automation runbooks turn tribal knowledge into consistent, executable, auditable steps with built-in controls, reducing variance between responders. Changing where the prose lives does not change how reliably it is executed.

q: A fleet-wide remediation must run first on a small canary group of instances, and only proceed to the full fleet if the canary group reports no errors. Which execution strategy implements this?
options: Start the operation on all instances and pause it manually if errors appear
Run the Systems Manager operation against the canary target group with rate controls, verify success, then start a second execution for the remaining targets
Tag canary instances and rely on the document to skip the rest of the fleet
Use maximum concurrency so the canary instances happen to run first
explain: Staged rollout requires separate, observable executions per wave; concurrency settings alone do not guarantee canary instances run first or gate the rest. Verifying the canary wave before expanding is the control that limits risk.

q: An instance in an Auto Scaling group needs hands-on troubleshooting and patching, but the group must not terminate it for failing health checks while work is in progress, and overall desired capacity accounting must remain clear. Which ASG state should the operator use?
options: Detach the instance permanently and create a replacement group for it
Suspend the entire Auto Scaling group for the duration of the work
Move the instance into Standby state, work on it outside normal health-based replacement, then return it to service when finished
Set the instance's termination protection and leave it in service
explain: Standby removes an instance from active rotation and health-based replacement while keeping it tracked by the group, which suits deliberate maintenance. Detaching is a permanent separation, and suspending the group affects every instance.

q: A scheduled quota review shows a regional vCPU limit will block a planned migration next month, although current utilization is low. Which action should be taken now?
options: Launch test instances now to raise utilization so the quota rises automatically
Assume quotas increase automatically when an AWS Organization account is created
Wait until migration launches begin failing, then request an emergency increase
Submit a Service Quotas increase request for the target Region with the migration justification, well before the capacity is needed
explain: Quota increases are requests evaluated in advance; submitting early with a clear justification gives time for approval before the migration depends on it. Utilization alone does not raise a limit, and waiting converts a known constraint into a migration failure.
